fit: isolated piperine in a swallowing stimulus
assessment: The physiology comparison used isolated piperine and did not test cracked culinary black pepper in a Parkinson treatment contrast.

fit: topical piperine and reported dysphagia presence in burning-mouth syndrome
assessment: Dysphagia was present in 4/17 at baseline and 3/14 at follow-up. The uncontrolled series supplies no paired dysphagia transition table or severity rating. The rinse used isolated piperine and excluded swallowing the intervention.

fit: mixed swallowing scores with black pepper aroma in six patients
assessment: The four complete swallowing scores include one improvement, two declines and one unchanged. The patient with multiple system atrophy was in the separate rotigotine comparison.

fit: healthy-adult aroma exposure with repeated saliva swallowing
assessment: Registry reports results publication but gives no citation or effect estimate. The university verifies ethics approval 23015. The health ministry gives 50 planned and UMIN gives 30 enrolled. Dysphagia was excluded.

assessment: Immediate swallowing electromyography did not show a pepper aroma effect. No Parkinson group or culinary exposure.

fit: black pepper exposure and antibiotic-treated pneumonia in long-term care
assessment: The crossover abstract reports fewer antibiotic cases during pepper use. Preparation, route, paired counts, swallowing severity, and Parkinson subgroup are unavailable.

fit: sage extract and mouse recognition or acute behavior
assessment: Vocalization and irritability at high extract doses do not measure reduced facial expressiveness.

fit: brewed green tea in Parkinson disease with aggregate daily-living scores
assessment: The pilot reports UPDRS daily-living means of 9.2 and 9.9. It did not give separately measured handwriting size. The 2013 dissertation and 2015 paper represent the same cohort.

fit: isolated caffeine and digitized handwriting kinematics
assessment: The 20-person crossover reports better fluency and higher peak velocity or acceleration after the highest caffeine dose. It supplies no verified letter-size contrast or Parkinson data.

fit: isolated caffeine in Parkinson disease and a handwriting readability item
assessment: The six-month Results state that none of the individual MDS-UPDRS-II components differed between groups. A numerical handwriting estimate and measured size were not reported. This used caffeine capsules.

fit: lifetime recalled green tea and total motor daily-living scores
assessment: The exploratory longitudinal analyses report no clear association of recalled green tea with total motor daily-living severity in idiopathic or LRRK2 Parkinson disease. Handwriting size and the individual item were not estimated, and preparation was unspecified.

fit: green tea powder and older-adult physical function including registered grip strength
assessment: The 78-person trial reported no clear overall physical-performance differences in mixed models and a knee-extension change comparison p=.016. It did not test handwriting and used exercise and a powdered product.

fit: low-fat mixed diet includes nutmeg in a baked recipe; aggregate motor exam
assessment: The apple crisp contains nutmeg of unspecified texture; intake is not individually verified. Composite speech and total motor scores do not establish listener-rated intelligibility or an isolated spice effect.

fit: secondary pooled review of oral and inhaled rosemary and depressive symptoms
assessment: The same-team earlier poster pools five depression comparisons at SMD −0.29 (95% CI −1.01 to 0.42, I²=85%). It uses end scores for trials with different baseline depression. The journal abstract and poster share a review family. Final journal plot and study table remain open.

fit: fresh-derived rosemary extract-hydrolat and acute Bond–Lader mood
assessment: In healthy adults without a depression diagnosis, descriptive contentedness change was 4.30 versus 4.12 on plain water. Separate within-arm tests do not establish a difference. It has no depression scale and belongs to the 2023 ERP and 2025–2026 reporting family.

fit: carbonated rosemary extract and hydrolat beverage with affect outcomes
assessment: A 20-person healthy pilot gives exploratory positive and negative affect scores without significance tests or a depression scale. Equal calmness changes in the table contradict the narrative. Freshness of the leaves in this drink was unverified.

fit: inhaled distilled rosemary oil and Zung depression scores
assessment: Posttest group comparison favored oil over waiting list. Pre-existing class allocation, route and absence of Parkinson disease rule out an isolated fresh-leaf ingestion interpretation.

fit: dried rosemary powder and HADS depression during methadone maintenance
assessment: The original reports no significant HADS depression difference and gives no exact arm means or intervals. The Methods and abstract conflict on dose and duration. A separately significant anxiety outcome cannot settle Parkinson depression.

fit: rosemary extract shared by two fish oil and comparator capsule arms
assessment: PHQ-8 change was inconclusive between arms. Both groups took rosemary extract, leaving its contribution unidentified.

fit: rosemary essential oil among 15 odors in a dementia pilot
assessment: All three groups had a median GDS of zero after treatment. Posttest group comparison was inconclusive. No assigned rosemary-only or culinary exposure.

fit: aqueous and hydroalcoholic rosemary leaf extract in antioxidant assays
assessment: Rosemary extract IC50 values differed by assay and extraction conditions. These are chemical endpoints without culinary oral administration, depression or gait observations.

fit: original aroma abstract with incomplete rosemary mood outcome
assessment: The author abstract attributes reported lower POMS depressed mood to lavender. Rosemary findings concern anxiety and alertness. Exact rosemary depressed-mood values in the full original are unverified. The route is inhaled aroma.

fit: rosemary scent experiment and inaccessible depression subscale original
assessment: The original abstract reports POMS tension, confusion, vigor and fatigue but no depression result. Full article is restricted; the claimed secondary depression values and adjusted result remain unverified. Acute scent differs from fresh leaf ingestion.

fit: Brazilian dried rosemary stem-and-leaf extract and mouse immobility
assessment: Acute and repeated extract exposure reduced immobility in swimming or suspension tests. Open-field locomotion showed no clear difference. A different laboratory and preparation from the Tsukuba studies; no fresh culinary or clinical depression comparison.

fit: dried rosemary extract and grooming behavior after olfactory bulbectomy in mice
assessment: Oral extract after olfactory bulbectomy shortened grooming latency and increased grooming time. The original distinguishes treatment-by-surgery effects from the inconclusive latency treatment main effect. The experiment assesses an indirect animal phenotype and does not establish a clinical depression result.

fit: rosemary polyphenols in the ICR mouse tail-suspension test
assessment: The primary abstract reports reduced immobility and neurotransmitter changes. The journal body remains gated, so preparation and experimental overlap with the Tsukuba dissertation are unverified.

fit: two rosemary species in oral capsules and acute energy or fatigue
assessment: The original reports an exploratory fatigue contrast with inconclusive treatment-by-time mood tests. The capsules combined two species and freshness or processing was unspecified. It gives no depression score.

fit: injected beta-caryophyllene and acute mouse behavior
assessment: More open-arm time and less immobility in behavioral tests followed injection of isolated beta-caryophyllene. This does not establish a clinical outcome from the food preparation.

fit: oral rosemary and depression outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The primary abstract describes favorable outcomes with dried rosemary capsules. The Aucoin poster's endpoint depression estimate is −0.30 (95% CI −0.78 to 0.18; 34 per arm). The original full depression analysis remains open. This student cohort did not have Parkinson disease.

fit: fresh-derived rosemary beverage and fatigue or alertness in healthy adults
assessment: The randomized 80-person experiment measured post-task alertness and fatigue and describes very small unfavorable mood estimates. No nominal individual comparison survived correction. The full numeric mood table remains unverified, and depression was not measured.

fit: dried-leaf tea and human peripheral biomarkers
assessment: In 22 healthy participants the author abstract reports higher BDNF and TNF-alpha after intake. It supplies no controlled clinical depression comparison or fresh leaf exposure.

fit: mixed essential-oil massage containing rosemary and HADS depression
assessment: Results report a favorable blend-plus-massage depression contrast. Baseline group imbalance and inconsistent baseline statistics limit interpretation. Neither rosemary nor ingestion was isolated.

fit: dried rosemary and major depressive disorder outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The dried ground-leaf capsules were an SSRI add-on. Group-by-time p=.005 on BDI-II among 51 completers, with baseline imbalance p=.003 and no documented baseline-covariate adjustment. The strong end-score contrast in the 2026 poster includes the baseline difference.

fit: registered three-extract pain trial with secondary depression measures
assessment: Overall between-group BDI-II p=.149 and baseline BDI-II ≥4 subgroup p=.016. PROMIS depression p=.798 and scoring interpretation remains inconsistent. Authenticated supplements provide a separate psychological quality-of-life result and biomarkers. They do not establish the subgroup timing or isolate fresh rosemary.

fit: oral rosemary extract and composite mental disorder symptoms outside Parkinson disease
assessment: Two extract levels improved over time on the mental disorder screen. The reported results lack a separate comparative depression estimate.

fit: dried rosemary extract and murine immobility from a lab study described in a thesis
assessment: Figure 1-14 has lower tail-suspension immobility than water for both oral dried-leaf extract doses. The animal-level relationship to the same-laboratory Sasaki paper is unresolved. No clinical mood outcome was measured.

fit: rosemary extract and post hoc depression subscale outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The post hoc depression comparison in healthy working men was inconclusive (p = .058).

fit: isolated piperine plus levodopa and rat pharmacokinetics
assessment: Adding piperine increased levodopa exposure in lesioned rats. The experiment did not measure daily off time or cracked black pepper.

fit: optionally cranberry-flavored prebiotic bar in a Parkinson protocol
assessment: The cranberry flavor is an option and individual exposure and cooking are unspecified. No facial-expression motor item is identified in the posted outcomes or results.

fit: cranberry concentrate and animal motor and tissue outcomes
assessment: The four-arm experiment used concentrated juice and measured postural stepping and midbrain histology. The study did not measure facial expressiveness.

fit: soybean oil vehicle and essential tremor
assessment: Spirography improved after 1-octanol in both formulations. Pooled worsened-tremor events and the conflicting six-hour estimates do not isolate soybean oil or a Parkinson rest tremor effect.

fit: oral octanoic acid carried in soybean oil and essential postural tremor
assessment: The prespecified 80-minute comparison was inconclusive; some later outcomes favored the active octanoic acid. The formulation, postural tremor, and trial design supply no isolated refined soybean oil effect on Parkinson rest tremor.

fit: oral soybean oil placebo and essential voice tremor

fit: ground soybeans combined with levodopa and carbidopa
assessment: The original abstract reports longer ON time (p=.028) and less dyskinesia (p<.001) with ground soybeans alongside medication in seven people with Parkinson disease. It provides no refined soybean oil or separate resting-tremor comparison. Body and item results remain open.

fit: dried basil tea and uncontrolled nocturia reports

fit: purple leaf extract and bladder contraction
assessment: Extract made from dried purple basil leaves reduced electrically stimulated isolated mouse bladder contractions in Figure 2. No participant consumed basil and urinary urgency was unmeasured.

fit: oral sweet basil extract and urogenital symptom composite
assessment: The menopausal trial's urogenital composite, which includes urinary symptoms, showed no clear between-group difference at one month (p=.114). It gave no urgency-specific result or evidence in Parkinson’s.

fit: leaf extract capsule and preoperative state anxiety
assessment: Eighty orthopedic surgery candidates were compared using leaf extract capsules or starch. The author abstract reports a lower preoperative state-anxiety score with extract. Neither the preparation nor endpoint matches the frozen claim.

fit: repeated oral alcoholic extract with conflicting immobility by dose in male mice

fit: lemon balm use and perceived improvement in a Parkinson survey

fit: intended Melissa capsule and reported depression questionnaire in older women

assessment: Five-arm study includes a mixed Melissa formulation and a secondary depression endpoint at 12 weeks. Registry status unknown and no results posted. Ingredient attribution would remain limited.

fit: alcoholic leaf extract and cognition or recorded agitation

fit: published scoring comments on the 2002 topical cohort

assessment: The 18-person blinded crossover's author abstract reports greater calmness and reduced alertness at 600 mg one hour after a dose. fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: PDF page 23 identifies Melissa as a source of phenolic acids. The experiment tests isolated acids in perfused rat liver rather than brewed leaf tea.

fit: dementia review and topical or inhaled Melissa essential oil
assessment: The original review describes oil in dementia behavior care. The adjacent depression subsection supplies no treated Melissa depression arm or independent primary cohort.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: The treatment section mentions the genuine species as a dementia cognition or behavior lead, with no brewed Parkinson depression comparison.

fit: lemon balm in two oral botanical mixtures and Beck depression
assessment: Table 3 per-protocol means after 14 days are 5.6 four-extract, 10.5 three-extract and 11.3 placebo. Both active arms have lemon balm, valerian and passionflower. The active contrast changes butterbur. No single-ingredient or Parkinson comparison.

fit: topical oil and Alzheimer agitation, blinded comparison
assessment: Of 114 randomized, 94 were assessed at week 4 and 81 at week 12. No group advantage was detected on the reported comparisons. The study tested agitation rather than depressive symptom severity.

fit: same egg isolate with or without dried-leaf-derived lemon balm
assessment: Adding dried-leaf-derived lemon balm yields HAM-D improvement of 8.4 versus 10.1 points with egg alone, and BDI-II improvement of 11.0 versus 10.5. The active arms do not differ significantly. Neither numerical contrast supplies a reliable brewed-tea effect.

fit: hot-water steep of dried aerial parts in mice exposed to manganese
assessment: After three months of exposure, randomized groups of four received manganese, the hot-water steep, both, or water. Combined exposure attenuated selected tissue oxidation markers. fit: single versus 10-day oral ethanol extract and forced-swim duration in rats
assessment: The single-dose groups showed no clear immobility effect. The ten-day extract comparisons favored shorter immobility at higher doses in males and at all assessed doses in females, and fluoxetine showed a larger effect. The forced-swim sex-by-treatment test was not significant. No clinical Parkinson or brewed-tea condition.

fit: concentrated aqueous extract beverage and acute anxiety in healthy adults
assessment: The fruit-sweetened lower-dose drink favored state anxiety against an artificially sweetened placebo, and the high-dose drink with the same artificial sweeteners as placebo favored worse anxiety at a disputed timepoint. The retrospective registry differs in doses and includes an unreported bar arm.

fit: concentrated water extract and separate rosmarinic acid control in rats
assessment: The short experiment found shorter swim immobility with extract and isolated rosmarinic acid, while swimming and struggling did not clearly change. Ten-day extract groups had less immobility and more swimming. The freeze-dried 12% rosmarinic acid extract, animal assay and absence of clinical outcomes limit transfer.

fit: fixed combinations and isolated extract in colon cells
assessment: The tested extracts had limited individual marker effects. Combinations showed altered inflammatory readouts, with no clinical depression or brewed preparation comparison.

fit: lemon-balm infusion and pooled self-reported symptom changes in psychiatric patients
assessment: Of 26 lemon-balm users, 11 used it with prescribed treatment. Seven reported no change and three decreased intensity. The remaining co-user has no reported direction. The herb row lists dizziness and nausea. Changes are pooled across symptoms and cannot be attributed to the herb or to depression separately.

fit: lemon-balm infusion in a separate psychotic outpatient survey
assessment: Fifteen used lemon balm, two naming depression as the indication. Among eight co-users with medication, five reported no change and three reduced symptoms. One nausea report is listed. The outcomes are pooled across symptoms and are separate from the non-psychotic cohort.

fit: single dry extract and two defined mixtures in a chronic-stress rat model
assessment: Forced-swim immobility with Melissa alone was 199.0 versus 225.5 seconds in stressed controls, p=.348. The Melissa-containing blend was also inconclusive. The other blend showed a favorable comparison and contained no Melissa. The study uses small animal groups and no brewed or Parkinson exposure.

fit: oral hydroalcoholic concentrate in restraint-stressed mice
assessment: Middle and highest groups showed lower swim and suspension immobility than restraint controls. Open-field locomotion was not clearly changed. Methods and Results label the middle arm 75 mg/kg while an accepted figure caption prints 100 mg/kg. Neither a brewed infusion nor a human depression outcome was tested.

fit: brewed dried-leaf exposure, ventricular ectopy endpoint
assessment: The open-label randomized comparison used genuine leaf tea plus lifestyle advice. The adjusted Holter ectopy comparison was favorable. Depression and a Parkinson population are absent from the reported comparison. The body and analytic denominator remain open.

fit: aqueous extract combination and reserpine mouse behavior
assessment: The abstract reports favorable behavior and catalase results for the two-herb combination. It gives no separate numerical lemon-balm outcome or interaction estimate. The experiment uses reserpine and concentrated preparations rather than clinical depression after brewed tea.

fit: individual dry extract and mixture effects on rat serum cytokines
assessment: Both blends reduced chronic TNF-α and IL-6 in the stress model, while single Melissa showed no clear chronic cytokine change. The 2017 behavioral report shares project and formulation details. Cohort overlap is unresolved and this assay does not show a depression effect.

fit: six-extract STW 5-II and functional dyspepsia outcome
assessment: Predefined GI responder rates favored the combination, 61.2% versus 45.1%. Secondary mean score was inconclusive. No isolated herb or depression outcome.

fit: ethanolic leaf extract and inflammatory markers in BV2 cells
assessment: The original experiment reports lower nitric oxide and changes in Nrf2 and HO-1 for a characterized ethanolic mixture in LPS-stimulated cells. The lowest concentration did not show several pathway changes. The experiment has no brewed infusion, Parkinson participants, or depression outcome.

fit: inhaled essential oil and dialysis sadness item
assessment: Original Tables 3 and 4 give 22/34 versus 21/34 for feeling sad (p=.80) and post-treatment severity 2.02 versus 2.14 (p=.84). The post-only item comparisons are inconclusive and concern dialysis and inhaled oil.

fit: injected hydroalcoholic extract and opposing sucrose preference outcomes by diet
assessment: Sucrose intake increased relative to high-fat diet vehicle controls. The lowest extract dose decreased sucrose preference under normal diet versus its own vehicle. Both directions are tied to diet-specific controls and an injection route in rats, with no oral tea or clinical depressive symptoms.

fit: self-reported use among surveyed students for mental-health context
assessment: In the herb-use question 260 of 491 respondents reported lemon balm. Overall CAM satisfaction uses a separate denominator and gives no ingredient-specific change in depression. Preparation and clinical symptom change were not established. This observational record is indirect evidence of use.

fit: acute standardized lemon balm extract and distinct mood and cognitive tasks
assessment: The primary overall calmness effect was null. All four supplements and protocol were checked. Fatigue rose in both groups with an inconclusive interaction, while some task-specific comparisons favored extract. No depression score, brewed preparation or Parkinson population was tested.

fit: plant-associated compounds and predicted depression targets
assessment: This computational screen selects saffron and lemon balm among medicinal plants and predicts compound targets. It supplies no administered food preparation, human depressive symptom result or direction for the frozen hypothesis.

fit: acute lemon balm extract capsules and subjective mood factors in healthy adults
assessment: In 20 healthy volunteers, Figure 3 shows a smaller calmness decline with 300 mg than placebo at 1 and 2.5 hours and with 900 mg at 1 hour. Alertness was lower after 900 mg at all measured times; contentedness was unchanged on the reported comparison. The acute mood scales did not measure clinical depression, and neither Parkinson disease nor brewed lemon balm was tested.

fit: Carmint mixed lemon balm spearmint and coriander for IBS
assessment: Reused primary trial already assessed for0728. Product identity resolves the P95 three-species clue. Abdominal pain comparisons favor the mixture, with attrition and endpoint denominators unresolved; no separate depression or ingredient-specific effect.

fit: mixed STW5 tincture and functional dyspepsia
assessment: The original human trial reports a small investigator-rated GI composite benefit, an inconclusive diary comparison and patient tolerability favoring placebo. No separate depression or lemon balm component result was found in the inspected original.

fit: aqueous leaf extract and categorical depression screening
assessment: Severe depression category counts changed 3/28 to 3/28 versus 10/27 to 6/27. Baseline imbalance and absent verified comparative change prevent directional weight.

fit: mixed STW5 rat gastric stress model
assessment: Indexed original Methods and Results report gastric muscle and hormone endpoints, including inconclusive KCl and adult-stress adrenaline comparisons. No behavioral depression measurement. Original binary unavailable and poster animal overlap unresolved.

fit: capsules and composite premenstrual symptoms in adolescents

fit: cod processing-derived protein and metabolic effects

fit: brewed spearmint crossover and subjective sleep in nasal polyposis

fit: dried aqueous spearmint extract and subjective sleep initiation

fit: concentrated aqueous spearmint extract and sleep measures

fit: flaxseed oil in a mouse anxiety-like behavior test

assessment: Main report gives inconsistent p values and durations. No clear cinnamon effect or Parkinson pain data.

fit: cinnamon powder and clinically measured rheumatoid arthritis pain
assessment: Original abstract favors cinnamon (p<.001) on pain VAS. Table unavailable. Inflammatory arthritis cohort.

fit: cinnamon capsules and primary dysmenorrhea over two cycles

fit: cinnamon bark oil macerate and dyspepsia upper abdominal pain

assessment: The gel lowered late-phase formalin pain scores. Early-phase composite and thermal latency comparisons were inconclusive. Ground cinnamon and Parkinson pain were untested.

fit: cassia within routine medication and multimodal pain care

fit: Parkinson survey recording cumin use with aggregate nonmotor measures

study: BNA2019 injected oil or preference member
fit: animal vehicle or flavored-milk preference outside the frozen preparation
assessment: PT080 and another member report injected corn oil as vehicle or control in a perimenopause model. The oil route, associated interventions and measures differ from oral corn oil.

assessment: Corn oil is used in rat lipid comparisons, feeding paradigms and a toxicant vehicle. No Parkinson clinical endpoint was measured.

fit: corn oil as high-fat diet control and partial marine-lipid substitution

fit: shared collection original source context

assessment: A tumor experiment incorporates corn oil in control or combined diets involving EPA and aspirin. The study does not assign the frozen preparation and clinical endpoint.

assessment: Celery historically relates to the compound. Trial formulation and cognitive scale do not isolate the frozen preparation and outcome.

fit: pharmaceutical compound and composite cognition
assessment: The placebo-controlled comparison favored butylphthalide on global cognition. Full report and executive function estimate remain unavailable.

fit: oral celery extract and spatial and non-spatial memory in healthy mice
assessment: The study reports improved memory tasks. It did not measure executive function in Parkinson’s or administer dried celery leaves as food.

fit: pharmaceutical combination and a mixed cognitive subscore
assessment: A four-drug regimen reported a visuospatial and executive MoCA subscore. The comparison did not isolate dried celery leaf or the compound.

fit: pharmaceutical compound and composite cognition

fit: pharmaceutical compound and composite cognition

fit: pharmaceutical comparison and overall cognition

fit: pharmaceutical adjunct and visuospatial executive domain

fit: fermented red cabbage with beetroot and caraway in healthy adults

fit: mixed vegetable diets with assigned red-cabbage amounts

fit: mixed red-cabbage and root vegetable diets in type 2 diabetes
assessment: The bitter/strong arm had lower 24-hour diastolic change than control, while the systolic comparison was inconclusive. Eating preparation and amount of red cabbage were unspecified, and no standing symptom was measured.

fit: fermented or pickled cabbage and cucumber with six-week clinic pressure
assessment: The between-arm week-six systolic comparison was inconclusive and registry versus paper food-arm denominators differ. Cabbage cultivar and standing symptoms remain unreported.

fit: cooked mixed cruciferous soup and 24-hour pressure
assessment: Systolic pressure was lower than after the control soup. Cabbage type was unspecified and no standing lightheadedness measure was included.

fit: red cabbage microgreens and resting pressure in adults
assessment: Brachial and central pressures were unchanged. The study did not assess standing symptoms, mature red cabbage or Parkinson.

fit: registered fermented versus unfermented red cabbage in allergic rhinitis
assessment: The planned safety assessments may provide a general adverse-event follow-up. No prespecified standing procedure, symptom comparison or observed results are available.

fit: filtered marjoram tea and motor examination in Parkinson
assessment: Only an aggregate motor estimate is accessible. No isolated speech item, acoustic loudness or fresh leaf exposure.

fit: Rubus ulmifolius extract confection and self-reported menstrual-cramp severity
assessment: 20 volunteers, no concurrent control or blinding. The authors report 75% perceived benefit. The exact extract content is unspecified and the formulation descriptions and figure denominators are inconsistent. No PD or frozen fruit.

fit: frozen blackberry drink and exercise recovery biomarkers
assessment: 14 athletes received 200 g frozen fruit in water or red-colored water. No significant between-arm CK differences. The paper did not measure reported pain and identifies only the Rubus genus.

fit: freeze-dried blackberry purée milk and quantified post-exercise muscle soreness
assessment: The exercise challenge trial favored freeze-dried blackberry in milk on immediate perceived soreness. There was no pre-exercise soreness baseline, calories and carbohydrate differed, treatment-by-time p=.914 and separate 24–72h comparisons were inconclusive. Registry and thesis are one non-Parkinson study.

fit: Parkinson pain odds and overall Mediterranean diet adherence
assessment: OR 0.86 (95% CI 0.75–0.98) for higher pattern adherence and pain presence. No separate blackberry intake or preparation contrast and no estimate on severity after frozen berries.

fit: oral nutmeg and secretory diarrhea in one human case

fit: oral nutmeg solvent extracts and unchallenged rat stool mass
assessment: Dry stool mass was 0.976 versus 0.207 g per 100 g at vehicle and the highest ethanol-extract dose. The comparison uses a concentrated preparation and a proxy outcome.

fit: crude suspension and fractions in animal diarrhea challenge
assessment: Crude and petroleum-ether preparations reduced loose stools in an animal challenge. An aqueous preparation did not. Constipation was unmeasured.

fit: high-intake ground-nutmeg self-experiment in a letter
assessment: The indexed letter lacks accessible full text. The constipation observation is reported secondhand and does not establish a culinary dose or Parkinson comparison.

fit: aqueous nutmeg seed extract and rodent small-intestinal transit marker
assessment: Table 3 shows shorter charcoal travel across three extract doses. The Methods and abstract disagree on challenge context and the study does not test clinical constipation.

fit: grapeseed as a shared massage carrier and psychiatric symptom scores
assessment: Both groups received grapeseed massage. Difference concerns added scents. Original body and refining grade unverified.

fit: topical grapeseed oil mixture in Gua Sha and depression scores
assessment: Lower depression scores accompanied the bundled procedure. The trial did not test ingestion or determine the contribution or processing grade of the oil.

fit: grape seed extract and clinical depression scores in migraine
assessment: Adjusted DASS depression p=.95. The extract is not the fixed oil and no participants were studied for Parkinson depression.

fit: mixed Parkinson diet and composite motor score
assessment: Appendix A lists both herbs in a multicomponent diet. Composite UPDRS III scores improved. The examination includes speech, but no item-level result, individual herb amount or preparation, or herb-specific contrast was reported.

fit: crushed fennel seed infusion and unsolicited fatigue mention
assessment: Among ten women reporting on a seed infusion, the other-effects item rose from 0 to 8 points. The narrative mentions fatigue without reporting its direction or count. Controls did not complete the questionnaire. The seeds were crushed and steeped, and the population had menopausal symptoms.

fit: oral fennel oil and categorical fatigue severity in primary dysmenorrhea
assessment: The fatigue distribution favored oil at both strengths. Overall p=.08, with rescue medication and differential discontinuation. Oral oil, cyclic menstrual fatigue and toasted seed in Parkinson differ.

fit: fennel extract and fatigue-specific comparison in primary dysmenorrhea
assessment: The primary abstract gives p=.058 with no fatigue arm means or relative direction. The full Persian results table remains open.

fit: fennel soft capsules and menstrual weakness versus no medication
assessment: The table reports weakness falling 6.65 to 2.88 for fennel and staying at 6.39 for control. It disagrees with the abstract control value. Menstrual weakness, a capsule and an unblinded comparator limit transfer.

fit: fennel seed in a honey mixture evaluated in people with Parkinson disease
assessment: The preparation was unspecified. Survey fatigue counts are pooled across 150 people and cannot be linked to the mixture recipients.

fit: oral Parkinson trial corn vehicle and seated cardiovascular monitoring
assessment: The trial measured seated wrist blood pressure and found no significant contrast. Standing changes and symptoms were not measured as an endpoint.

fit: self-reported cooking corn oil and seated blood pressure
assessment: Predominant corn-oil users had lower seated pressure than people mainly using animal fats. Self-reported exposure, seated monitoring and absence of a symptom endpoint limit the finding.

fit: Parkinson CBD trial dizziness reporting with oral corn vehicle
assessment: The associated thesis reports dizziness in the active arm. Posture and an oil-specific comparison are unavailable.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and blood pressure in seated treated hypertensive adults
assessment: Seated pressure is a distinct outcome from standing lightheadedness. The study neither specifies refining nor compares corn oil against randomized no-oil use.

fit: Scrambled egg offered within both Parkinson diet plans; one visual hallucination event occurred in the ketogenic arm
assessment: Individual intake and event timing are unknown. Hallucinations resolved after pramipexole reduction. The trial did not compare egg-specific visual hallucination frequency.

fit: Mixed diluted Avena formulation with measured sleep efficiency planned
assessment: Completed 81-person short-term insomnia trial with no posted results. It tests a combination tablet and does not isolate oat grain.

fit: Mixed oat-based beverage protocol with sleep quality secondary
assessment: The planned trial in older adults has no posted results. The formulation, comparison and outcome do not identify a rolled-oat effect.

fit: Oat-milk products and planned toddler sleep outcomes
assessment: The recruiting study compares different dairy and oat product regimens. The sleep records are pending and the exposure and population differ from the frozen claim.

fit: Mixed oat straw extract and adult sleep complaints
assessment: Final PSQI favored the combination containing oat straw extract, melatonin, valerian and other ingredients. No separate oat arm or Parkinson cohort.

fit: Whole grains and prevalent versus incident insomnia in a cohort
assessment: Fully adjusted odds ratio for highest versus lowest whole-grain quintile was 0.93 for prevalent insomnia and 1.00 for incident insomnia. Whole grains were pooled and no rolled-oat or Parkinson effect was estimated.

fit: Mixed granola and inconsistent subjective versus EEG sleep outcomes
assessment: In the uncontrolled UMIN000053189 cohort, subjective insomnia scores fell from baseline at weeks four and eight and EEG sleep outcomes did not change significantly. The test recipe does not establish rolled oats.

fit: Personalized granola and uncontrolled insomnia scores
assessment: Overall Athens Insomnia Scale change was inconclusive. A subgroup of 19 improved from baseline. The recipe supplement and any isolated oat contrast remain unavailable.

fit: Breakfast oat products with glycemic outcomes
assessment: The published UMIN000048192 breakfast experiments report glucose and no sleep results. Their relationship to the registry's oatmeal lunch and sleep narrative is unresolved.

fit: Extracted oat fiber doses and exploratory daily sleep duration
assessment: Two-week NCT06739941 study found no significant change in sleep duration over time or between three open doses. No inactive control, rolled-oat preparation or clinical Parkinson insomnia endpoint.

fit: Oat flour and bran products with a sleep item inside GHQ-12
assessment: NCT06393114 randomized 56 analyzed adults with mild metabolic deterioration to crossover oat gurt and porridge periods. Both used oat flour, bran and faba protein. Supplement Table 11 reports an inconclusive direct GHQ-12 comparison (P=.569). No sleep item estimate, plain rolled oat contrast or Parkinson population. The journal and EPO6_170 describe one trial.

fit: Oatmeal challenge shared by both randomized enzyme periods
assessment: In NCT06628869, sleep quality did not differ significantly between fructanase and placebo (P=.91). Both periods used the same oatmeal and inulin. The trial estimates an enzyme effect rather than an oat effect.

fit: rolled oats as the food comparator in chronic insomnia
assessment: For rolled oats the diary mean sleep time changed from 359 to 376 minutes in one week. Within-arm changes and the week-by-condition comparisons were inconclusive. There was no randomized no-oat control and no Parkinson cohort.

fit: Parkinson insomnia and diet-pattern scores
assessment: The pattern analysis reported no significant insomnia association and no individual rolled-oat comparison.

fit: wild green oat extract and actigraphic sleep in smokers
assessment: Wake after sleep onset changed by −0.7 minutes versus +5.4 with placebo at eight weeks (p=.047). The preparation, population and outcome differ from rolled oats and Parkinson insomnia severity.

fit: Oatmeal-rice lunch with numerical sleep estimates unavailable
assessment: The registry and DOI 10.11402/ajscs.36.0_58 report OSA-MA measurement with discordant sample counts. The sleep estimates and participant overlap remain open.

fit: combined dried fig oral exposure and maze behavior in a scopolamine memory model
assessment: The oral mixture included dried fig and olive oil. Maze behavior and hippocampal markers in rats provide no clinical visual hallucination frequency estimate.

fit: visual hallucinations and attributed pain in a Parkinson case

fit: visual hallucinations during unrelated medication intoxication
assessment: The exact letter reports visual hallucinations during acute intoxication in an individual with parkinsonism. The food hypothesis and episode frequency are outside the report scope.

fit: actual dried fig ingestion before elevated potassium, with no hallucination outcome
assessment: Pavletic described raised potassium during screening of an otherwise healthy 36-year-old volunteer. The case was uncontrolled and contains no documented visual hallucination or Parkinson diagnosis.

fit: dried fig in a pooled supplement and nonspecific adverse outcomes

No separate fig arm or hallucination-frequency measure was reported. The authors link the earlier report to the same cohort.

fit: first visual hallucination in a Parkinson cohort without food exposure

fit: dried fig intervention with perceived stress outcome in students

fit: visual hallucinations after levodopa in juvenile monogenic parkinsonism

assessment: Of 129 patients with idiopathic Parkinson disease, 32 reported hallucinosis or illusions and 30 of those reported a visual component. Episode rate and dried fig exposure were not measured.

fit: historical allergy symptoms after dried culinary fig
assessment: A case describes itching, angioedema and dizziness after fresh fig, then similar allergic symptoms with kiwi and dried fig. The narrated history and sensitization testing give no hallucination frequency or Parkinson diagnosis.

fit: safflower yoghurt comparator with non-swallowing allergy outcomes

fit: safflower and fish-oil crossover with lipid and inflammatory endpoints

fit: USP oil comparator and ALS scale items on swallowing

fit: safflower comparator and reflux total across college singers
assessment: The oil group's reflux questionnaire mean rose 0.33 points, with uncertainty across both directions. The swallowing item direction is unknown.

fit: traditional oral seed-oil uses with other indications

fit: exact cold-pressed oil in aged mice with immune measures

fit: oral safflower capsules and a blood-lipid measure
assessment: Thirty-four healthy adults ingested the load. Data represent triglyceride responses and do not include a clinical swallow test.

fit: oral capsule loads and chewed-and-spat sensory stimuli
assessment: Fifteen adults received 10 or 30 g safflower loads. Serum triglycerides were measured. Separate mastication and expectoration were used for the cream cheese stimuli.

fit: original article and linked trial context
assessment: The original review describes dysphagia as a nutritional barrier in neurodegenerative disease. Its separate safflower-fed amyloid mouse comparison measured brain inflammatory gene expression and lipid mediators, with no swallowing or bradykinesia result.

fit: formulated safflower and texture without a swallowed test

fit: whole oil comparator in Glut1 deficiency
assessment: The clinical crossover reports episodic movement events and baseline dystonia, with no distinct swallowing measure.

fit: swallowing endpoint with a different oil comparator

fit: original article and linked trial context

fit: safflower oil comparator and reflux questionnaire with swallowing item
assessment: The safflower total reflux score fell by 1 point on average, and the contrast interaction was p=0.509. Swallowing item outcomes and Parkinson dysphagia were unavailable.

fit: unrefined oral oil and a firsthand sensory report
assessment: One person reported less numbness and tingling after unrefined oil. A copied version and serving clarification duplicate the report. The record supplies no diagnosed Parkinson disease, movement endpoint or verified cold pressing.

fit: independent veterinary series of whole kernels
assessment: Thirteen Australian field cases described hindlimb weakness, recumbency and pain after reported raw or roasted kernels. The case series differs from the US poison-center lineage. It supplies no separate rest-tremor outcome.

fit: macadamia-olive blend and gastric emptying in healthy adults
assessment: The dissertation reports the registered oil-blend comparison. Eight people entered the macadamia arm and seven contributed interpretable hydrogen transit. The groups did not differ significantly in transit response. No movement outcome or pressing grade.

fit: macadamia oil in matched mental-health study drink
assessment: The distinct BRAVO comparison enrolled 125 and stopped early. It used macadamia-oil placebo against omega-3 and planned affect and cognitive assessments. The official registry has no posted results or Parkinson tremor outcome.

fit: topical macadamia oil and nickel dermatitis control
assessment: Pure macadamia-oil application did not significantly change skin flare or erythema in the author abstract. The comparison involved skin application and no tremor assessment.

fit: same oil meal in two human family-history groups
assessment: Seventeen participants per family-history group ate the same macadamia-oil meal. Postmeal metabolic responses did not significantly differ across groups. Pressing grade and tremor were unreported, and no oil-free comparator was included.

fit: macadamia oil as an oral krill-oil control and cognition
assessment: 555 were randomized and 245 completed. Cognition, mood and resilience did not show clear group-by-time effects. The 2019 protocol, 2021 outcomes and later trainee analysis share a cohort. No untreated arm, pressing grade or rest observation is established.

fit: kernel oil and tissue markers after rat chemical brain injury
assessment: The abstract reports cerebellar staining and oxidative or inflammatory biomarker changes in a potassium-dichromate rat model. Full dosing, pressing grade and denominators remain unverified. The accessible text gives no interpretable motor or tremor result.

fit: room-temperature pressed oil and alternative extraction properties
assessment: The Methods specify room-temperature hydraulic pressing. Comparative physicochemical and fatty-acid results establish process differences. The body and abstract attribute one percentage to different comparators. No participant or motor measure.

fit: oral macadamia-rich formulated diet and blood lipids
assessment: The recovered original compares three oil-based diet periods using processed drinks and margarine. LDL was 0.17 mmol/L higher than the oleic period. Two participants reported transient GI discomfort. Pressing method and resting tremor were not reported.

fit: whole macadamia kernels and acute canine tremor reports
assessment: Poison-center reports include tremor and weakness after whole kernels. The same investigator observed no tremor in four experimentally exposed dogs. The overlapping series and trial are one lineage. Neither studied expressed oil, resting phenotype or Parkinson disease.

fit: community consultation on cultural food and trade uses
assessment: The published conservation consultation records traditional uses of the kernels for food and trade. No pressed oil preparation, symptom or comparative response is described.

fit: planned percutaneous macadamia-oil comparison
assessment: Protocol compares macadamia and coconut oils in a skin-absorption and metabolic context. Target enrollment was 16. Results and actual participant counts are absent from the official record. No food intake or tremor measure.

fit: oral oil meal and acute sleepiness and fatigue
assessment: The paper and reports describe two crossover samples of 16 and eight healthy students with separate figures. Acute alertness and fatigue contrasts do not estimate tremor. Outcome reports and the registry belong to the same family, and grade is unreported.

fit: oral lemon balm extract and general motor performance in MPTP mice
assessment: Rotarod and activity improved at the two higher tested levels. Dystonic posturing was unmeasured and the intervention was ethanolic extract.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: PDF page 23 identifies Melissa as a source of phenolic acids. The experiment tests isolated acids in perfused rat liver rather than brewed leaf tea.

fit: lemon balm tincture and temporal muscle contraction categories
assessment: Final categories gave an inconclusive arm comparison (p=.551). Children with bruxism, no fresh leaf, dystonic posture or Parkinson disease.

fit: chives in a mixed Parkinson diet and a facial-expression item in UPDRS III
assessment: The motor total improved at one year in both groups. The article names the facial item but does not report its change. Chive preparation, participant amounts, and a chive-free comparison were unavailable.

fit: nasal oil and chronic rhinosinusitis sleep domain
assessment: The published record covers SNOT-22 sleep and emotional domains, while separate Sleep Quality Scale results remain open. Route, comparator and population differ.

fit: black cumin seed oil protocol and registered PSQI
assessment: An oil intervention outside Parkinson includes sleep quality in a questionnaire panel. The registry has no posted results and does not test ground seed.

fit: oily nigella seed extract and postmenopausal sleep quality
assessment: Table 2 shows PSQI 7.2 to 6.6 versus 11 to 9.5 on placebo, with overall p=.45. Narrative scores, change sign and amounts disagree. Ground seed exposure is unverified.

fit: oral oil extract and PSQI in nonrestorative sleep
assessment: The PSQI and sleep component comparisons favored the oil at 45 and 90 days. The oil extract and non-Parkinson population differ from ground nigella and Parkinson insomnia.

fit: oral oil extract and seven-day actigraphy
assessment: The oil group had better sleep efficiency, latency and duration versus placebo. The corrigendum corrects a placebo p value. The study measured nonrestorative sleep outside Parkinson disease.

fit: Nigella sativa in a twelve-botanical insomnia formula and PSQI
assessment: The formula group mean PSQI fell from 12.25 to 6.60, with p=.27 for overall three-arm comparison after treatment. There is no isolated ground nigella or Parkinson estimate.

fit: oil extract versus melatonin and actigraphy
assessment: Both crossover treatments improved actigraphy from baseline. Melatonin favored sleep latency and duration relative to oil. The study used an active comparator and excluded the frozen population and preparation.

fit: tart cherry and cocoa mixture with unresolved exertion comparison
assessment: The abstract describes a randomized athlete trial. The Methods describe laboratory formulations and sensory panel work. Table 3 lists ungrouped before and after RPE values without an identified comparator or verified trial allocation.

fit: freeze-dried sweet cherry beverage and self-rated fitness
assessment: Selected mood and fitness ratings favored the cherry drink in some age groups, without a fatigue scale or a Parkinson cohort.

fit: dried cherry capsules and cycling time trial
assessment: Time trial completion was inconclusive across interventions (p = .115). Exercise performance in athletes differs from Parkinson fatigue.

fit: diluted Montmorency juice and exercise pain in women with fibromyalgia
assessment: Pain and day-one strength comparisons were inconclusive. The fibromyalgia questionnaire characterized participants at enrollment. The original does not report a treatment comparison for fatigue.

fit: oral tart cherry concentrate and mental fatigue during a task battery
assessment: Mental fatigue treatment means favored concentrate by 9.5 points (95% CI 2.5 to 16.5, p=.009). The treatment-by-repetition comparison was inconclusive (p=.257). The concentrate, session scale and population differ from the frozen claim.

fit: concentrated cherry juice and clinical fatigue scale in ulcerative colitis
assessment: Thirty-five completers. The published secondary IBD fatigue severity and impact differences were inconclusive. The concentrated preparation and population differ from the Parkinson dried-cherry claim.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: S7.519 describes sweet cherry among fruit trees used for grafting work. No dietary cherry or measured neurologic symptom is present.

fit: veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison
assessment: The Prunus entry describes animal hazards of leaves and seeds and includes cultivated sour cherry. Cherry eye and cherry laurel are distinct hits. The phloridzin entry gives a historical attribution, not a fruit study.

fit: reported food categories and overeating
assessment: LBP2.005 groups cherry together with strawberry and grape in an overeating report. Dried cherry and fatigue were not studied separately.

fit: Tart cherry and apple juice crossover in older adults with insomnia
assessment: The 15-person study reported an inconclusive secondary fatigue comparison after two weeks of mixed juice or placebo. The formulation and population differ from dried cherries and Parkinson fatigue.

fit: freeze-dried Montmorency skin capsules and half-marathon time
assessment: The trial reported faster finish time with cherry. Predicted-versus-actual pace and postrace soreness contrasts were inconclusive. Performance differs from the frozen Parkinson fatigue outcome.

fit: Montmorency concentrate and perceived athletic recovery
assessment: Table 3 and the main results report inconclusive tests of perceived recovery and soreness in nine water polo players. No separate clinical fatigue comparison was reported.

fit: acute tart cherry concentrate and mental-fatigue VAS outside Parkinson disease
assessment: In 27 healthy adults in an acute crossover, the fatigue treatment p=.690 and treatment-by-repetition p=.288. The matched cordial comparison is an independent inconclusive contrast in acute task fatigue, using concentrate.

fit: Capsule Montmorency powder and 15 km cycling performance
assessment: The powder-capsule trial reported faster completion with cherry. Time-trial performance differs from Parkinson fatigue after eating whole dried cherries.

fit: Freeze-dried Montmorency powder and cycling exhaustion
assessment: Time to exhaustion did not clearly differ in this 12-man healthy cohort (p=.36). Powder capsules and exercise endurance differ from the frozen symptom and preparation.

fit: tart cherry drink and aggregate well-being in professional soccer players
assessment: The author abstract reports an inconclusive group-by-time effect for subjective well-being, p = .874. Full methods and any individual fatigue item or estimate remain unverified.

fit: Concentrate and one-item match-recovery fatigue scale
assessment: Eleven rugby players in a crossover had no clear difference in fatigue ratings. This is one cohort together with the 2019 thesis.

fit: Tart cherry capsules and time to exhaustion in hypoxia
assessment: Cycling time to exhaustion was longer in 13 healthy adults under cherry than placebo. The 2024 recovery report uses overlapping participants. Capsule supplementation and exercise endpoints differ from the frozen claim.

fit: Juice and stimulation-based muscle fatigue after cycling
assessment: The 12-cyclist crossover found no clear drink difference in low-frequency fatigue or perceived exertion versus a sports drink.

fit: Vistula product and post-marathon fatigue scale

assessment: Parkinson apathy was associated with composite odor outcomes. No isolated clove odor association or dietary exposure was verified in the accessible source.

fit: Human Parkinson randomized multi-odor trial with a nonmotor composite
assessment: The study evaluated depression and anxiety instruments and Part I composite scores. No separate apathy score or isolated clove consumption result was reported.

fit: Rhus coriaria extract in induced diarrhea and intestinal contraction models
assessment: Crude extract suppressed chemically induced diarrhea in mice and relaxed isolated rabbit intestine. It did not establish constipation from ground sumac.

fit: sumac aqueous extract and constipation subscore in non-Parkinson dyspepsia
assessment: The two sumac extract arms improved more than omeprazole at week eight only in the adjusted model (p < .001 and p = .002). There were no adverse events. Ground spice and Parkinson constipation were outside the trial.

fit: Huntington total motor comparison includes dystonia item
assessment: The six-month active-minus-safflower total motor difference was +0.6 (95% CI −1.0 to 2.5). The separate dystonia result is unreported. The repeated 2025 records share this cohort.

fit: safflower oil comparator and paroxysmal movement events in Glut1 deficiency
assessment: The trial’s difference in grouped paroxysmal events was inconclusive. No no-oil group, isolated Parkinson dystonia measure or refining grade was reported.

fit: original article and linked trial context
assessment: The TRIHEP3 row uses safflower oil against triheptanoin in Huntington disease. Its motor total includes dystonia but no separate estimate is reported. The dysphagia rows are distinct tablet and swallowing skill trials without a safflower arm.

fit: original article and linked trial context
assessment: The repeated TRIHEP3 row identifies the same whole oil comparator. It supplies no separate dystonia or swallowing outcome. The two swallowing studies elsewhere in the table use a drug or training, with no safflower allocation.

fit: macadamia oil in rat diet during experimental SCD inhibitor pharmacology
assessment: The oil was in mixed chow and grade and individual intake were unreported; biochemical fatty-acid outcomes do not measure Parkinson or levodopa-induced dyskinesia.

fit: freeze-dried cranberry powder and attention in healthy older adults
assessment: The group-by-time interaction for Addenbrooke attention was inconclusive (p = .467). Delayed recall improved, a separate endpoint. No cooked cranberry or Parkinson arm was included.

fit: cranberry juice crossover with cognitive performance and planned attention context
assessment: Registration lists beverage and placebo arms, planned COMPASS composites and no posted results. It does not identify a cooked whole cranberry exposure or Parkinson cohort.

fit: cranberry juice and a computerized attention domain in healthy students
assessment: The attention domain showed no clear contrast and two selected short-term memory measures favored the juice. The study does not test cooked cranberry in Parkinson disease.

fit: cranberry beverage and attention-related tests in healthy older adults
assessment: Trail Making and Stroop test changes were inconclusive over six weeks. The intervention was a beverage and the participants did not have Parkinson disease.

fit: oral fruit methanol extract and mouse bar test
assessment: Oral methanolic fruit extract shortened experimenter-imposed bar posture. The assay did not score tremor.

fit: roasting chemistry only
assessment: Roasting changed the volatile profile, including lower fennel estragole. Full time, heat and sample-specific composition are open. No biological outcome was tested.

fit: cultural practice under falij and preparation mismatch

fit: fennel aerial juice and injected mouse toxicity
assessment: Repeated injections of leaf-and-stem juice were associated with convulsions. Route and dose units vary in the paper. No tremor outcome matches the claim.

fit: fennel essential oil and motor tests in a rat model
assessment: Oil group III shortened the bar posture relative to reserpine-only group II descriptively. Group IV was levodopa/carbidopa. Figures do not annotate the oil versus model comparison, and there was no item-level tremor.

fit: aqueous fruit extract and motor proxies
assessment: Conference abstract gives rotarod, open-field and passive-avoidance results. Extract dosing and specific effect sizes remain open. The 2024 paper tests a separate in vivo challenge.

fit: oral fruit extract and neuroinflammation motor proxies
assessment: Oral fruit extract under LPS improved late coordination with no clear early result. No tremor assessment exists in the studied outcome set.

fit: fennel seed extract and lesion-model coordination
assessment: Peri-lesion oral methanol extract favored coordination and grasp. Post-lesion-only comparisons were inconclusive. Neither was a tremor measurement.

fit: fennel essential-oil and pamphlet safety lineage
assessment: Regulatory review records tremor at the highest essential-oil toxicity exposure. The original case protocol and identity of the 2000 pamphlet animals remain open. Acute intoxication and toasted-fruit intake differ.

fit: essential oil in cake and a clinical seizure report
assessment: Generalized seizure followed exposure to an unknown amount of fennel essential oil in cake in a person with epilepsy. No frozen outcome was recorded.

fit: nitrate-associated tremor in cattle consuming plant waste
assessment: Tremors followed contaminated produce in cattle. Nitrate was measured in green and white plant waste and ruminal contents. No toasted seed or Parkinson exposure was isolated.

fit: fresh-leaf essential oil and mouse behavior
assessment: Fresh leaf oil changed open-field and maze behavior in healthy mice. Separate five-animal limit screen disclosed no overt toxicity and gave no tremor count.

fit: whole crushed seed in diet and general mouse activity
assessment: Whole crushed seed pellets lowered home-cage crossings and increased open-field center crossings. Toasting and resting tremor were outside the experiment.

fit: unroasted fennel accessions and chemistry
assessment: Cultivated and wild accessions differ greatly in starting volatiles, with a separate quantitative estragole estimate. The study has no roasting condition or symptom outcomes.

fit: isolated fenchone and acute toxicity signs
assessment: The acute Table 1 records no convulsions or tremors in either fenchone or vehicle group. Methods and later table sample counts differ. The isolated compound comparison leaves the culinary Parkinson direction open.

fit: isolated anethole and rotarod or stride in rotenone rats
assessment: Anethole given before rotenone improved rotarod and selected stride results. Resting tremor appears in the introduction as a disease feature.

fit: methanolic extract in acute and repeat rat toxicity
assessment: A different methanolic extract had no reported deaths and no separately reported tremor outcome in the author abstract.

fit: fennel in composite rapeseed oil processing
assessment: Fennel was held in a bundled seasoning oil during frying comparisons. The study measures aroma and composition without a separate fennel contrast.

fit: healthy mouse rotarod and grip
assessment: Concentrated fruit extract reduced rotarod retention and grip in healthy mice. This does not identify a tremor phenotype.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: PO1.165 summarizes genuine quinoa, rice and quinoa-flake comparisons for intake, satiety and metabolic markers. No Parkinson gait or rigidity result is shown.

fit: red quinoa ethanol extract and fly movement measures
assessment: The public dissertation and 2025 abstract report the same study. Extract co-exposure attenuated rotenone-related changes in climbing and crossings. The exposure was an extract and the study did not measure human walking.

fit: acute allergic hypotension after pepper exposure
assessment: Chinese case report documents blood pressure around 60/45 mmHg during an allergic reaction. It supplies adverse-event context without an orthostatic assessment.

fit: formula comparator and resting blood pressure
assessment: The randomized crossover detected higher mesenteric flow with formula, with no significant resting blood pressure change. Standing symptoms were unmeasured.

fit: fruit extract and isolated vascular relaxation
assessment: Nepalese pepper fruit extract relaxed rabbit aortic rings. The assay did not measure standing pressure or human symptoms.

fit: low-fat mixed diet includes nutmeg in a baked recipe; aggregate motor exam
assessment: The total exam includes a multidimensional speech item, but no separate loudness or nutmeg comparison is reported; grated preparation and actual intake are unverified.

fit: saffron extract and Insomnia Severity Index in older adults
assessment: Insomnia severity interaction p=.3. Other sleep measures differed. No ground saffron or Parkinson comparison.

fit: Asthma waking with a multi-extract syrup
assessment: Original pediatric asthma trial tested five extracts in honey added to standard asthma drugs. The ACQ asthma-associated night-waking item favored the combination. There is no insomnia scale, isolated ground saffron or Parkinson group.

fit: secondary sleep outcomes and exploratory sleep subgroup
assessment: Overall secondary outcomes did not clearly separate. The favorable higher-sleep-disturbance subgroup was exploratory. The standardized extract population had no Parkinson disease.

fit: saffron extract and primary Insomnia Severity Index
assessment: Randomized non-Parkinson poor-sleep group, group-by-time p=.017. Standardized extract differs from culinary powder.

fit: saffron extract and sleep quality with ISI at screening
assessment: ISI selected participants. Reported results use other subjective sleep scales and actigraphy; no separate insomnia severity change.

fit: saffron extract and Insomnia Symptom Questionnaire
assessment: Original randomized comparison abstract reports improvement in ISQ totals and classification. Different exposure and cohort.

fit: saffron extract and Athens Insomnia Scale
assessment: Pooled extract arms favored lower AIS by −0.95 (95% CI −1.79 to −0.11). Separate adjusted dose contrasts inconclusive. Preprint same cohort.

fit: powder tablet and general sleep quality
assessment: The global sleep score favored saffron. Insomnia severity was not isolated in the accessible report.

fit: Affron sleep disturbance and related impairment
assessment: Secondary PROMIS Sleep Disturbance contrast 0.38 (95% CI −2.40 to 3.16) is inconclusive. Impairment improved by 2.99 points, a different endpoint. Extract and non-Parkinson population.

fit: roasted pressed kernel oil and skeletal muscle cell development
assessment: Sections 2.2–2.4 verify roasted-then-pressed kernels. Figure 7 distinguishes Ordu oil with larger myotube diameter from cuticle-oil-related length. The exposed cells did not undergo rigidity assessment.

fit: whole hazelnuts offered and Parkinson motor composite includes rigidity
assessment: Appendix A lists whole hazelnuts separately from the supplied oils. The full motor score includes rigidity, with no separate rigidity values or hazelnut oil contrast.

fit: exceptionally bitter zucchini and acute gastrointestinal toxicity
assessment: The source links poisonings to unusually bitter fruit. Dream enactment and preparation were outside the comparison.

fit: zucchini ingestion challenge in selected allergy patients
assessment: Oral and gastrointestinal reactions establish a separate acute adverse outcome. No sleep measures were reported.

fit: whole Parkinson diet including unspecified zucchini
assessment: The intervention grouped ingredients and the publication did not measure dream enactment.

fit: historical oral wild lettuce case
assessment: The first-person original describes visual symptoms and a child jumping during delirium. It gives no tremor, Parkinson cohort or cultivated romaine exposure. The later reprints describe the same patients.

fit: acute oral wild lettuce toxicity
assessment: The eight case descriptions report ataxia and other acute signs without a separate tremor estimate or Parkinson group. Wild Lactuca virosa differs from cultivated romaine.

fit: unverified wild lettuce species and injected extract
assessment: The reported hand and foot tremor belongs to a separately cited valerian case. The three wild-lettuce extract cases do not establish an oral romaine or Parkinson resting-tremor effect.

fit: raw romaine meal compared with a cellulose meal
assessment: Postprandial outcomes were measured without rest tremor assessment.

fit: red lettuce extract in a Parkinson fly model
assessment: Reported climbing is a locomotor proxy. No rest tremor or verified romaine exposure.

fit: rat motor behavior during injected clove essential oil
assessment: The rat study reports actimetry and cylinder posture outcomes after injected essential oil. It did not measure muscle rigidity or oral ground clove.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: Abstract 65 identifies eugenol in clove oil and tests the oral isolated compound or its labeled analogue, without a tested clove food.

fit: isolated oral eugenol and levodopa-related behaviors in toxin model
assessment: Isolated oral compound did not improve lesion-model abnormal behaviors induced by levodopa. Different motor measures and no clinical rigidity or ground clove.

fit: oral isolated eugenol and catalepsy in MPTP mice
assessment: Higher pretreatment exposures lowered catalepsy while post-treatment had no clear benefit. Clinical rigidity and ground clove were untested.

fit: clove essential oil and cell oxidative outcomes
assessment: Hydrodistilled oil was tested in a cellular stress model. No behavioral rigidity measure or oral ground clove.

fit: celery stalk reactions after ingestion
assessment: The selected cohort reported oral allergy and swelling. No motor swallowing measurement or Parkinson population.

fit: healthy participants chewing celery
assessment: The study measures parotid secretion and does not test dysphagia severity.

fit: cooked mixed-vegetable ratatouille containing celery
assessment: Ready-to-swallow bolus properties and mastication measured in healthy adults. No raw-stalk comparison or Parkinson dysphagia measure.

fit: celery stalk in the airway after a meal
assessment: Choking and direct visualization establish an adverse food event in stroke/vascular dementia. Preparation was unstated and no Parkinson dysphagia comparator was available.

fit: contaminated carrot-millet dish and acute auditory hallucination
assessment: Investigators identified a Jimson weed contaminant in millet. The report does not implicate carrot or examine recurrent visual hallucinations in Parkinson's.

fit: raw carrot identified in Parkinson case-control questionnaire
assessment: Raw carrot was a questionnaire item. No hallucination-frequency comparison was reported.

fit: nanocurcumin and barium-swallow Penetration-Aspiration Scale after chemoradiotherapy
assessment: Two 2025 journal reports and the 2026 conference abstract describe the same trial. In 64 completers, post-treatment PAS was 2.91 versus 3.72 with placebo from equal 2.91 baselines. Nanocurcumin and radiation-related swallowing differ from the frozen claim.

fit: oral curcumin capsules and binary dysphagia symptom in oral fibrosis
assessment: Table 1 reports 4/50 to 0/50 with curcumin and 4/50 to 4/50 with placebo. Small event counts and a discordant printed p-value limit inference. No grated rhizome or Parkinson cohort.

fit: curcumin phytosome combination and oral regimen tolerability
assessment: The registry reports difficulty swallowing a multi-supplement regimen containing curcumin in Parkinson disease. It supplies no symptom severity estimate or separate effect for turmeric.

fit: curcumin extract alongside a weight-loss diet in PCOS
assessment: No separate Parkinson symptom or culinary turmeric result was recorded. Within-group metabolic changes do not establish a between-group clinical response.

fit: turmeric-colored bread and child sensory preference
assessment: Children chose yellow bread less often. The study concerns colour and liking, without a swallowing or other relevant clinical endpoint.

fit: oral processed turmeric extract and grade 3 chemoradiotherapy dysphagia
assessment: Both doses had fewer grade 3 dysphagia events than placebo in the original abstract. Chemoradiation injury and the extract formulation differ from neurologic dysphagia and grated turmeric.

fit: thyme oil used as an EEG biometric odor stimulus
assessment: The indexed conference abstract describes odors used to identify individual EEG responses. It supplies no clinical olfaction or ingested thyme comparison.

fit: thyme among mixed odorants in long COVID smell rehabilitation
assessment: The protocol uses thyme as one of several scent stimuli and measures olfaction after COVID-19.

fit: thyme and cinnamon among inhaled spices in post COVID smell training
assessment: The completed protocol identifies thyme among smell training stimuli and does not supply an isolated dietary effect.

fit: thyme sniffing in multi-odor postinfectious smell rehabilitation
assessment: A separate postinfectious cohort had better combined smell scores after rotating odors. The schedule placed thyme in one of three blocks with other scents. The groups were allocated in order, and the contrast estimates the whole training schedule.

fit: thyme-containing multi-ingredient product and measured olfaction in acute rhinosinusitis
assessment: An indexed study abstract reports better smell outcomes for a multi-ingredient sinusitis treatment containing thyme extract. The isolated effect of fresh thyme remains unmeasured.

fit: inhaled thyme extract in a fixed four-odor post-traumatic regimen
assessment: Original Methods identify Thymus vulgaris extract and three other odors. Follow-up composite smell scores were 18.35 in the trained arm versus 13.06 in controls, p<.033. No isolated or oral thyme effect in Parkinson disease. Cohort overlap with Rezaeyan is unresolved.

fit: confirmed thyme odor in multi-odor post-traumatic training
assessment: The 2024 original Methods confirm thyme in fixed training and in the first rotating month. They explicitly identify the same cohort as the 2021 report. The whole sniffing program does not estimate an isolated or oral thyme effect in Parkinson disease.

fit: thyme odor within a 12-scent post-COVID protocol
assessment: The nonrandomized comparison favored the odor program on total smell function. The study does not isolate thyme or test fresh thyme by mouth.

fit: uncontrolled piperine blend and digestive symptom reports
assessment: Piperine, curcumin, virgin coconut oil and counseling. Age subgroup counts are inconsistent and there is no isolated or controlled constipation contrast.

fit: oral isolated piperine and slowed gastric and upper-gut transit in rodents
assessment: Oral compound slowed solid gastric emptying and intestinal transit. No clear lower-dose liquid-emptying contrast. Isolated compound and distinct endpoints.

fit: oral black pepper powder and orocecal transit
assessment: Upper gut transit 90 ± 51 to 122 ± 88 min (p=.09) with powdered capsules. No stool or clinical constipation result. Distinguish separate red pepper contrast.

fit: crude pepper extract and mixed gut model responses
assessment: Stimulatory and inhibitory findings depend on assay. No ordinary cracked pepper or Parkinson constipation rating.

fit: culinary seasonings in a constipation case
assessment: Multiple dietary and other interventions leave the contribution of the individual seasoning unresolved.

fit: isolated piperine and bowel proxies in rats
assessment: The study assessed fecal water under an isolated constituent in a lesion model, which differs from clinical constipation after cracked black pepper.

fit: chamuangone-enriched rice bran oil and rat locomotion
assessment: Stride, ladder and open-field outcomes generally improved in haloperidol-treated rats. Enrichment and the absence of plain oil and human gait-speed arms limit interpretation.

fit: isolated rice-bran constituent and fly locomotion
assessment: The gamma-oryzanol diet reduced rotenone-related climbing and mobility deficits in flies. The 2016 thesis and 2015 article describe the same experiment. No whole oil or clinical walking-speed comparison.

fit: extracted rice bran oil and rat open-field movement
assessment: Pairwise open-field and home-cage locomotion differences were inconclusive. Rotarod coordination improved in a haloperidol model. Grade and Parkinson walking speed are unverified.

fit: hexane rice bran extract and rat movement
assessment: Oral bran extract partly reversed locomotor changes in a rotenone model. Refined rice bran oil and human walking speed were untested.

fit: optional coconut oil in whole-diet military crossover with ANAM fatigue
assessment: The ketogenic arm favored lower fatigue during 36 hours of extended wakefulness in seven healthy men (thesis diet effect p=.001). In a separate phase of the same trial, weekly fatigue was similar between diets. The optional recipe oil lacks individual consumption and grade, and the study cannot isolate oil or Parkinson fatigue.

fit: virgin versus refined coconut oil and acute perceived exertion
assessment: The institutional annual report describes 15 healthy elite men receiving virgin oil, refined oil and no added test oil in a crossover. Time to exhaustion and perceived exertion did not differ significantly across conditions. Full estimates, masking procedures and the original seminar abstract remain unverified. Acute exertion is distinct from Parkinson fatigue severity.

fit: virgin coconut oil and motor tests in a rotenone mouse model
assessment: Original P90 reports qualitative improvements in grip, gait, kyphosis, clasping and pole activity versus untreated model animals. It gives no route, treatment quantities, numeric effect or fatigue measure and no clinical comparison.

fit: oil-choice phases and qualitative fatigue direction
assessment: Preliminary fatigue direction runs opposite to the claim. The deck permits coconut oil or MCT oil and gives no grade, product-stratified scores, participant counts or comparative fatigue estimate.

fit: oral MCT oil in mixed nutrition case series
assessment: One of four patients had Parkinson. Energy intake and laboratory outcomes were pooled. The MCT oil source, grade and fatigue outcome were unreported.

fit: unspecified coconut oil use and separately reported Parkinson fatigue
assessment: Small inverse graphical association. No numeric coefficient, model, uncertainty or preparation detail.

fit: extra-virgin coconut oil with EGCG and multiple sclerosis outcomes
assessment: The trial family compared a bundled oil and EGCG intervention and reported anxiety, disability and biomarker endpoints. The original registration and linked results disagree on EGCG dose. There is no oil-only or separate Parkinson fatigue comparison.

fit: coconut-derived triglycerides and combined diet
assessment: In the later report, nine of 37 improved and nine worsened on a fatigue global-change question in the MCT diet period. The between-diet comparison was inconclusive. The study does not isolate virgin coconut oil.

fit: optional coconut oil and whole-diet crossover with mood and morning alertness
assessment: Eleven healthy completers compared whole diets. Evening mood p=.18 and morning freshness p=.29 across both diets and washout. No quantified individual oil intake or separate fatigue scale in the original article. The linked metabolic supplement schema did not supply either variable.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: P-20-006 uses coconut oil as an in vitro substrate for microbial lipase activity. No oral oil or Parkinson symptom comparison occurs.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: PO2.063 compares coconut-oil high-fat rat chow with a cafeteria-style diet. Intake, weight and biochemical outcomes provide no isolated culinary Parkinson symptom comparison.

fit: coconut oil in an acute fat and endotoxin study
assessment: Postmeal serum endotoxin was higher after the coconut-rich meal than after the DHA-rich meal. Fat composition and amount vary and the trial supplies no separately measured Parkinson outcome.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: Reference 81 traces a genuine coconut-oil meal crossover compared with meals dominated by other fats. The measured endotoxin response is distinct from the frozen Parkinson clinical outcome.

fit: extra-virgin coconut oil with caffeine and acute exercise exertion
assessment: The thirteen-runner crossover compared four conditions. The original methods place coconut oil only with caffeine and coffee, and the four-way Borg exertion comparison has p=.99. This outcome and population differ from daily Parkinson fatigue.

fit: oral virgin coconut oil and overall symptoms during hospitalization
assessment: Usual care with oil versus usual care alone had mean overall symptom resolution time 6.8 versus 6.74 days in 77 randomized inpatients. More adverse events were reported with oil. The publication provides no individual fatigue result or Parkinson subgroup.

fit: liquid coconut oil vehicle and fatigue event counts in healthy adults
assessment: Both groups received oil. Fatigue was listed in 1 of 6 low-dose drug recipients and 0 of 10 pooled placebo recipients. Repeated-dose groups had no listed fatigue. The oil grade, Parkinson population and stand-alone fatigue severity contrast were absent.

fit: virgin coconut oil and measured fatigue in a randomized chemotherapy study
