assessment: Clinicians judged the named foods permissible after rehabilitation in a single Parkinson patient with prior aspiration pneumonia. No food-level rates or baked-potato exposure.

fit: rice cracker and other food textures in one case
assessment: Coughing or choking diminished after a switch from porridge with chopped foods to puréed meals. A senbei cracker in the therapy room elicited good mouth opening and chewing. The original abstracts describe one case and no baked-potato exposure.

fit: food temperature and first swallow in unspecified parkinsonism
assessment: The four-person study reported a favorable result for hot food but supplied no food identities, absolute values or measured choking. The rice ball belongs to a cited secondary-parkinsonism case.

fit: potato patty and perceived eating ease outside a verified Parkinson group
assessment: A potato oyaki patty ranked highly on perceived eating ease in a nursing-home recipe evaluation. A separate simmered tuber ranked higher, with species unspecified. There was no Parkinson subgroup, baked potato, or clinical swallowing outcome.

fit: silent aspiration with water and rice porridge
assessment: In one Parkinson and lacunar stroke case, videofluoroscopy documented silent aspiration with both 3 mL water and rice porridge after vertebral fracture. No potato exposure or measured choking rate.

fit: boiled potato oral processing in healthy volunteers
assessment: The experiment included 12 healthy participants and measured bolus texture and oral workload across five foods. It did not test baked potato, patients with Parkinson disease or swallowing difficulty severity.

fit: whole-swallowing regular side dishes and choking in advanced Parkinson disease
assessment: The patient had choking with unnamed side dishes and low intake of a rice-ball staple. No potato exposure was identified and the clinical changes followed combined care.

fit: crushed thickened cup ramen in Parkinson swallowing evaluation and training
assessment: One patient with stage III Parkinson and aspiration pneumonia underwent VF and conditional direct training with crushed thickened cup ramen. Intake improved under combined care. No potato preparation was identified.

fit: soft-cooked egg and preferred snacks in a stage V Parkinson case
assessment: One patient received soft-cooked onsen egg, unnamed formula and later rice crackers, cookies and manju after clinical assessment. Aspiration was not attributed to a specific food and baked potato was not reported.

fit: sweet potato mousse in unstratified care-facility reports
assessment: The menu included sweet-potato mousse. Care-facility feedback pooled foods and provided no Parkinson-specific outcome or baked potato test.

fit: porridge retention and water aspiration in two Parkinson cases
assessment: Water alternation reduced esophageal porridge retention in one case. Water silently aspirated in the other, whose porridge retention improved with jelly alternation. Neither case assessed baked potato.

fit: different potato preparation and bench outcome
assessment: The study measured texture of gelled, printed mashed potato powder without a clinical cohort, baked potato or swallowing symptoms.

fit: tuber paste sensory evaluation with population unresolved
assessment: The title names a paste made with an unspecified tuber and a sensory evaluation. Species, diagnosis and results remain behind the individual abstract access barrier. It gives no estimate for baked potato in Parkinson disease.

fit: meat-and-potato stew paste rheology and healthy-participant sensory work
assessment: A 2007 conference title and related 2008 university study concern a puréed stew. Eight healthy assessors rated a beef paste easier to swallow after 10% MCT addition. There is no separately served baked potato or Parkinson effect.

fit: postoperative dysphagia and dry food guidance
assessment: The report documents ordinary and soft meal textures and repeat endoscopy. It gives no baked potato or confirmed obstruction.

fit: inpatient choking and aspiration during subsequent tube feeding
assessment: The patient had a choking and aspiration event. The obstructing food was unidentified. Later enteral changes and mosapride accompanied fewer vomiting episodes.

fit: qualitative dysphagia response during vinegar and levodopa coadministration
assessment: After total gastrectomy, one person with stage V Parkinson disease reportedly had less dysphagia when taking three fragrant vinegar capsules with levodopa. No dysphagia score, meal food or potato exposure.

fit: confirmed foods in a hospital choking series including Parkinson disease
assessment: Five of 15 acute choking cases had Parkinson disease. Fourteen food identifications did not include potato, one was unknown, and food identity was not linked to diagnosis.

fit: family observation during a baked potato and chili meal
assessment: The account describes brief coughing after a sneeze while eating baked potato and chili in a person with Parkinson disease and existing dysphagia. There is no verified aspiration, comparative meal or swallowing-severity measure.

fit: indirect
assessment: One man with stage 5 Parkinson had cough and marked residue during a pork mousse trial; later videofluoroscopy found better handling of a different meat texture and alternating jelly cleared residue. Timing and rehabilitation differed. No baked potato was served.

fit: levodopa response during swallowing across consistencies
assessment: Ten participants completed a modified-barium swallow in ON and OFF conditions. The report does not identify individual foods.

fit: swallowing assessment with named foods in Parkinson disease
assessment: Five of seven participants had oral residue on the cracker test. No residue was seen for vanilla yogurt or water. Potato was not a test bolus.

fit: contrast-mixed sugar solution, agar and cookie in a swallowing series
assessment: Small amounts of liquid entered the trachea in 3 of 10 clinically labeled participants, only on unthickened cup drinking. Per-bolus denominators and diagnostic status of the three are unavailable. The fixed protocol did not name potato.

fit: observed choking during chopped buttered baked potato consumption outside documented Parkinson disease
assessment: The state surveyor observed coughing and choking after a resident had eaten about half the chopped baked potato. Repeated tags refer to the same event. The resident had recurrent difficulty on other meals, no documented Parkinson diagnosis and no instrumentally confirmed airway obstruction.

fit: observed baked-potato flesh consumption in dysphagia without documented Parkinson disease
assessment: The inspector saw a person with dysphagia and prior aspiration eat about half a baked potato without its peel and with no difficulty during the mixed meal. No Parkinson diagnosis or food-specific comparison is documented.

fit: within-person swallowing assessment across five liquid viscosities

assessment: The article reports 27 randomized and inconclusive pain comparisons. The registry gives 26 actual enrollees, names weekly SF-MPQ-2 and daily VAS, and has no posted results. The figure and table of arm-specific pain estimates remain unverified.

fit: black-pepper fruit in a four-plant arthritis trial
assessment: Final joint pain VAS difference 3.00 mm (95% CI −1.82 to 7.84); the full noninferiority analysis and arm-level table remain unavailable.

fit: isolated piperine and distinct thermal and mechanical outcomes in mice
assessment: Thermal response latency was higher in all piperine groups. Mechanical withdrawal threshold was higher only in the two higher-dose groups, with an inconclusive low-dose test. No clinical outcome.

fit: dried multiherb blend and massage in chronic low-back pain
assessment: The combination arm had a lower day-seven NRS than either component arm. Many ingredient exposures and no pepper-only comparison. Daily-dose reporting conflicts.

fit: commercial ground black pepper added to fixed turmeric in adults with chronic pain
assessment: 29 analyzed, repeated 0–10 pain. Added pepper p=.157 and pepper-by-period p=.5508. NCT05206266 is the same trial. Unknown particle size relative to cracked pepper and no PD-specific estimate.

fit: topical isolated piperine and chronic oral pain
assessment: 14 completers showed a 1.93-point mean paired NRS reduction with a topical rinse, CI .88 to 2.98. No concurrent comparator, PD cohort, or cracked pepper ingestion.

fit: dried leaf capsules and questionnaire esophageal motility symptoms in diabetes
assessment: Any esophageal complaint changed from 3 to 5 of 21 under dill and stayed at 5 of 21 under placebo. Within-arm p was .317 for dill. No between-arm estimate, fresh herbs, Parkinson population or separate swallowing measure was available.

fit: culinary dill and allergy-associated throat swelling
assessment: The case reported throat and tongue swelling after food cooked with dill and a positive fresh-dill skin test. Fresh-leaf consumption, a swallowing endpoint and Parkinson disease were unconfirmed.

fit: pumpkin seed oil in a Parkinson diet and facial-expression item within a motor scale
assessment: The menu names pumpkin seed oil. The paper gives no individual intake, preparation, facial-expression item change or separate effect of oil.

fit: coriander listed among seasonings of a mixed Parkinson vegetarian diet
assessment: Coriander plant part, fresh preparation and individual consumption were not reported; the study gives no apathy outcome or ingredient-specific effect.

fit: living coriander plant visual and smell exposure with POMS in healthy adults
assessment: Participants did not eat cilantro; POMS mood and vigor do not establish a Parkinson apathy effect.

fit: seed extract memory in scopolamine rats
assessment: Passive avoidance and water-maze results concern seed extract, a non-Parkinson model, and memory tasks.

fit: carotenoid food recalls and macular pigment measurements
assessment: The participant records name several food sources and the authors report no detected association with optical pigment density. No assigned food preparation or relevant Parkinson symptom was measured.

fit: whole Parkinson diet including unspecified zucchini
assessment: Aggregate motor changes do not establish grilled zucchini exposure or executive response.

fit: seed extract motor outcomes in haloperidol rats
assessment: Motor changes followed methanolic seed extract. No grilled fruit or executive task was studied.

fit: healthy volunteers; celery plant part unspecified; salivary flow during chewing
assessment: Increased salivary flow during chewing is not clinical drooling severity in Parkinson disease; exposure is not established as dried leaves.

fit: lovage in a shared Parkinson vegetarian menu and composite motor outcome
assessment: The menu lists lovage and the motor examination includes rigidity. The paper does not identify fresh leaf, isolate lovage or report change in the rigidity item.

fit: comparative healthy-volunteer report with unverified chervil placebo
assessment: The original abstract reports self-rated cognition, and a later dissertation identifies chervil through author correspondence. Original ingredient identity, culinary preparation and standardized executive testing remain unverified.

fit: garden chervil leaf and stem chemical analysis
assessment: Fresh-cut chervil leaves and stems were extracted for chemistry and cellular assays. Executive performance was not measured.

fit: methanol extract of culinary chervil in enzyme and cell assays
assessment: The enzyme and docking experiments do not measure executive performance after eating chervil.

fit: isolated capsaicin and MPTP mouse stepping abnormalities
assessment: The conference abstract describes abnormal steps and no significant aggregate gait change after MPTP. It gives no stride lengths or preparation match. A likely same-family thesis lacks a gait result.

fit: topical capsaicin and heat with measured step-length retention
assessment: Next-day retention of a trained asymmetry was reduced after capsaicin-plus-heat pain. Baseline walking was comparable. The outcome was not clinical stride shortening, and the route was topical.

fit: topical capsaicin and heat with human step-length learning and retention
assessment: Three groups acquired the gait task. Both pain groups retained less step-length asymmetry the next day. Healthy volunteers used a topical mixture rather than consuming smoked paprika.

fit: topical capsaicin and heat with step-length learning in older and younger adults
assessment: Training and next-day retention of a visual step-length asymmetry were lower with topical capsaicin plus heat. Neurologic disease was excluded, and the measured outcome was not ordinary stride length.

fit: rectal sesame oil in a multimodal regimen and facial motor item
assessment: Facial scores improved from baseline in an uncontrolled parkinsonism series. The preparation and route differ from toasted sesame oil consumption.

fit: protein-rich meals and reported levodopa fluctuations
assessment: A chart study associated protein-rich meals with motor fluctuations in a subset. It did not estimate boiled shrimp or falls.

fit: total dietary protein and reported falls
assessment: A cross-sectional comparison did not show a clear association with any or recurrent falls. It did not estimate boiled shrimp intake.

fit: heat-processed soup with fresh lovage in healthy adults
assessment: The cooked soup contained fresh lovage as an input. Reflux and GI distress were reported without insomnia severity measurements.

fit: individual Parkinson symptoms and diet scores
assessment: Diet scores were not significantly associated with insomnia and do not identify fresh lovage intake.

study: BNA2019 injected oil or preference member
fit: animal vehicle or flavored-milk preference outside the frozen preparation
assessment: PT080 and another member report injected corn oil as vehicle or control in a perimenopause model. The oil route, associated interventions and measures differ from oral corn oil.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and measured walking and trotting stride
assessment: Randomized horse comparison recorded similar walking stride changes. The omega-3 arm had a larger descriptive trot-stride change, between-arm p=.08. Animal, diet and gait differences limit clinical transfer.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: P233 is appended in the complete PMC HTML for this oral-key record and separately printed in the poster supplement. It compares corn and fish oil during shared exercise for strength and mechanistic outcomes. One study family.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: Printed P233 reports an omega-3 versus corn-oil comparator during shared resistance training. Its strength findings are distinct from the frozen clinical outcomes. The other PMC key reproduces this member.

fit: corn-oil control during exercise training
assessment: The final isometric interaction is p=.015 and the corn arm changed −1.4%. P233 uses −0.3%. Body strength during shared training does not measure any frozen Parkinson endpoint in these claims.

fit: NUTRIMAL mixed oil control and exploratory gait speed
assessment: Neither postintervention gait-speed contrast resolves direction, and the control and protein-only drinks both contain high-oleic sunflower and corn oil. Gait speed does not identify stride length.

fit: COPD blend includes corn oil and protocol measures gait speed
assessment: The supplement establishes the 50:50 blend while the abstract names four-metre gait testing. Accessible source material has no arm-specific gait estimates or stride data.

fit: corn oil comparator and measured walking distances in claudication
assessment: Walking distances did not clearly change in the available abstract. Refined oil, stride length and Parkinson cohort are unverified.

fit: shared Parkinson trial vehicle and aggregate mobility
assessment: The mobility score does not give stride length, and both CBD arms also used corn oil.

fit: measured mouse stride with matched corn oil vehicle
assessment: Exposure group comparisons estimate PCB effects on matched oil backgrounds. The most shortened strides were in PCB-treated wild-type animals.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and 400-m walking speed
assessment: Fish oil versus matched corn-oil gelcaps gave +0.010 m/s, 95% CI −0.025 to +0.044. Usual walking speed in mobility-impaired older adults does not estimate Parkinson stride length.

fit: corn oil plus maltodextrin comparator and 4-m gait speed
assessment: The corn-oil regimen had +0.12 m/s within-arm gait speed change with a rehabilitation co-intervention. The small pilot did not estimate stride length or an isolated oil effect.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and timed mobility
assessment: Timed Up and Go was slower at follow-up in the corn arm and faster in the fish arm. The task combines several components and no stride lengths were reported.

fit: corn and soy oil comparator with measured walking performance in COPD
assessment: The mixed-oil arm also used maltodextrin. The abstract gives no stride estimate or positive functional outcome. The linked registry does not isolate corn oil, and the primary tables remain open.

fit: repeated kindergarten vegetable exposure, intake and liking
assessment: Vegetables were offered in conjunction with a reward. The sample was children, and neither adult symptoms nor the matched preparation were assessed. The registration gives n = 82, while the two arm counts in the poster add to 84.

fit: reported food categories and overeating
assessment: LBP2.005 includes carrot as a named candidate in Table 1. Neither group reported an overeating occurrence for carrot. Its thermal preparation and the frozen symptom were not assessed.

fit: pasteurized carrot juice as a human comparator with an executive outcome
assessment: Trail Making B change in the seven-person carrot arm was inconclusive (p=.804). The study tested juice in healthy adults, without roasted carrot or a no-carrot control.

fit: multicomponent capsule including carrot and executive testing
assessment: The capsules contained carrot among numerous dehydrated fruit and vegetable ingredients. TESEN within-period changes were favorable. Roasting, the carrot quantity, and outcomes in diagnosed Parkinson disease are unresolved.

fit: purple carrot extract and memory in reserpine rats
assessment: Novel object recognition is a model memory test. The abstract does not measure human executive function or roasted carrot.

fit: ALS three-arm diet and exercise pilot with preliminary combined-arm swallowing burden
assessment: The preliminary result describes the combined intervention. An estimate isolating the diet-only contrast remains open.

fit: whole Mediterranean diet and planned chewing or swallowing measure after STN DBS

fit: topical olive oil, betaine and xylitol versus usual care in crossover dry-mouth cohort
assessment: The crossover measures swallowing attributable to dryness and reports a benefit on the overall dry-mouth score. The swallowing item was not among the significant comparisons.

fit: experimental local pharyngeal infusion and time between voluntary swallows
assessment: The original abstract reports longer voluntary swallowing intervals during olive oil pharyngeal stimulation than with water stimulation. Grade, an ordinary eating exposure, and a clinical dysphagia estimate remain unverified.

fit: historical dysphagia lecture on peptic esophageal ulcer with mixed treatment advice
assessment: The lecture attributes a mixed atropine and olive oil regimen to earlier clinicians treating peptic esophageal ulcer. It reports no isolated olive oil outcome.

fit: chewable olive oil, betaine and xylitol versus sorbitol in xerostomia crossover
assessment: The article describes better swallowing in its conclusion and reports only an aggregate questionnaire change in its results.

fit: swallowed extra-virgin olive oil and lycopene spray versus water, dryness-related swallowing VAS
assessment: A water-controlled trial measured swallowing complaints after an extra-virgin olive oil and lycopene oral spray. The reported item comparison was inconclusive. The higher initial symptoms on active and the combined product limit interpretation of the larger raw decline.

fit: companion English report of first reported 2014 uncontrolled topical radiation cohort
assessment: Dryness-related difficulty swallowing improved in uncontrolled pre/post data. The matching 2014 and 2016 reports describe one likely cohort. Multiple topical ingredients and radiation context prevent dietary olive-oil attribution.

fit: matched topical olive and parsley oil products in primary Sjogren syndrome
assessment: The swallowing VAS comparison was inconclusive (p=.57), with a numerically larger raw improvement in the control. Several active ingredients and oral-care route limit transfer.

fit: original animal physiology abstract with locally infused extra-virgin olive oil
assessment: Extra-virgin oil elicited swallowing in an anesthetized rat preparation where ordinary olive oil did not. The experiment assesses a local reflex, with no clinical dysphagia estimate.

fit: postoperative oral olive oil and cola with measured dysphagia grades after stenting
assessment: Swallowing grades improved after stenting plus bundled care. Neither the oil's own effect nor dietary extra-virgin oil in Parkinson disease can be estimated.

fit: oral organic extra-virgin olive oil and weekly dysphagia ratings in a cancer case
assessment: The case measures a swallowing symptom while the patient used EVOO. Concurrent treatment and recovery prevent an isolated effect estimate.

fit: usual olive oil frequency and concurrent swallowing assessment in a Parkinson cohort
assessment: Daily unspecified-grade olive oil and dysphagia are both reported. The analyzed contrast is by weight group and does not yield an oil-specific swallowing comparison.

fit: reported olive oil intake by swallowing symptom status
assessment: Reported intake averaged 37 versus 29 mL/day in Parkinson participants with and without swallowing disturbances, respectively. The oil grade was unspecified and this comparison measured intake alongside existing symptoms.

fit: transdermal capsaicin and focal eyelid dystonia
assessment: An uncontrolled blepharospasm case reported a severity score of 4 at baseline and 1 at six months. The intervention was a patch and the disease and dystonia phenotype differ from the frozen claim.

fit: fennel capsule and daytime dysfunction component
assessment: Among 50 postmenopausal women, mean PSQI daytime dysfunction changed from 0.36 to 0.25 with anethole-standardized fennel capsules and 0.28 to 0.16 with placebo (week 12 p = .439). The daytime wakefulness item was not reported separately. Exposure was a capsule and not toasted seed.

fit: eggs in an example menu and falls in a separate protein timing comparison
assessment: Nutri-Park compared falls across reported protein timing groups with no clear difference. An example dinner included eggs among several options. Poached egg intake and its effect were not estimated.

fit: observational tea analysis or prediabetes egg program
assessment: Three members identify the EGGSPDITe egg intervention program in prediabetes, including protocol and remote-delivery snapshots. They do not report a relevant egg effect on the frozen symptom.

fit: unspecified egg frequency and subjective Parkinson falls
assessment: Near-zero inverse plotted sign. No coefficient, uncertainty interval, poaching item or temporal estimate.

assessment: P-09-013 studies egg-white fibrils as dye sorbent and P-14-013 uses ovalbumin as a digestion substrate for isolated polyphenols. Other matches concern ova or embryos.

assessment: P1013 uses an isotope-labeled egg emptying test, P1018 records egg sensitization and the intravenous lecithin excipient, and P1595 measures reported food intake. Electrogastrography uses EGG as an acronym.

assessment: A designed-enzyme abstract uses hen egg-white lysozyme as a laboratory comparator. Other eggs are hamster gametes. Neither is a dietary intervention.

assessment: A mouse sensitization member uses egg-derived ovalbumin as a laboratory antigen. Another egg mention identifies helminth antigen.

fit: boiled eggs with a labeled phosphatidylcholine challenge
assessment: The egg challenge concerns gut microbial and blood metabolites. The outcome and preparation are separate from the frozen claim.

fit: egg within varied nonseafood dietary proteins
assessment: Egg is a bundled exposure in the nonseafood dietary pattern. The trial reports lipids instead of falls or gait, and does not isolate poached egg.

assessment: Genuine egg exposures appear in food intake surveys and the varied nonseafood arm of PO2.144. The student surveys overlap, and no isolated poached or Parkinson outcome is reported.

fit: shared collection original source context

assessment: The adjusted model treats egg frequency as one predictor of estimated low protein intake. Egg preparation and Parkinson falls and walking speed were not studied. The conference presentation and full article share the same data.

fit: reported chicken and egg label use
assessment: The survey identifies consumer attention to product labels. It does not measure consumption at a controlled preparation or fatigue, falls or gait.

fit: carotenoid food recalls and macular pigment measurements
assessment: The participant records name several food sources and the authors report no detected association with optical pigment density. No assigned food preparation or relevant Parkinson symptom was measured.

fit: processed egg yolk and tissue synthesis

assessment: Reference 350 explicitly links Tang's meal with two hard-boiled eggs and labeled phosphatidylcholine. Microbial and cardiovascular outcomes do not estimate poached egg or Parkinson falls.

fit: dietary questionnaire grouped by fat sensitivity
assessment: The proceedings include egg intake and egg white dietary mentions. The fat-sensitivity poster reports eggs and fried eggs, without poaching-specific intake or fall counts.

fit: weekly eggs and injurious falls in older adults
assessment: Mean weekly portions 2.03 in fall-with-fracture cases and 2.21 in controls (unadjusted p = .07). No preparation-specific or adjusted egg estimate.

fit: fresh cilantro leaf oral allergy challenge
assessment: A patient developed oral itching and a systemic allergic reaction during a fresh cilantro leaf challenge. Dysphagia and Parkinson disease were not reported.

fit: mixed meal containing coriander and exercise-associated dysphagia
assessment: Dysphagia developed after a mixed meal followed by running. Skin testing implicated fresh coriander and tomato. The food exposure and exercise cannot isolate cilantro in Parkinson disease.

fit: parsley flavonoid preparation and exertional fatigue model
assessment: Concentrated flavonoid preparations improved fatigue-related physiological measures and gastrocnemius morphology in an excessive-fatigue mouse model. The source did not test fresh leaf or Parkinson fatigue.

fit: veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison

fit: mixed fresh/heated parsley human feeding
assessment: Two one-week randomized feeding periods with or without culinary parsley measured apigenin and antioxidant endpoints. Fresh parsley fatigue was unmeasured.

fit: reported parsley preparations and pooled fatigue frequency
assessment: Parsley appears in two use citations and fatigue appears in a separate aggregate figure. Neither exposure preparation status nor within-person fatigue changes were reported.

fit: topical sunflower oil and salivary outcomes in medication-induced dry mouth
assessment: A crossover measured stimulated and unstimulated salivary flow and reported subjective dryness benefits within groups with oil. The oil versus water dryness comparison was p=.067. The route, oil and symptoms differ.

fit: sesame-based topical rinse and reports of reduced saliva
assessment: At eight weeks, a 40-person randomized trial reported no between-group difference in subjective saliva reduction or mouth dryness. The oil blend was spat out and no Parkinson drooling was measured.

fit: specified clinical Parkinson drooling and salivary-flow outcomes
assessment: The case-control study found lower unstimulated saliva flow and higher symptom prevalence for drooling and dry mouth. There was no oil exposure; flow alone cannot assign clinical drooling direction.

fit: watermelon and acute oropharyngeal reactions in an allergy-selected group
assessment: Six of 29 watermelon-sensitive patients had symptoms after ingestion. No speech or Parkinson outcome was measured.

fit: sunflower food frequency and composite Parkinson symptom burden
assessment: The poster reports +2 total PRO-PD points per intake frequency category (95% CI −10 to 13, p=.787). The cross-sectional exposure did not specify an oil grade. It gives no individual bladder symptoms estimate.

fit: acute poisoning; multi-ingredient powder; dysarthria eligibility only
assessment: Dysarthria was an entry sign, not a treatment outcome; no Parkinson or ground caraway-only speech comparison.

fit: ground sumac powder capsules with captopril in hypertension
assessment: Blood pressure decreased relative to placebo plus captopril. The report gives no orthostatic symptom or Parkinson outcome.

fit: sumac capsules in adults with hyperlipidemia
assessment: Small reported reductions in systolic and diastolic pressure provide non-Parkinson cardiovascular context. No orthostatic symptoms were measured.

fit: combined sumac and pomegranate in nonspecific acute dizziness
assessment: Both arms had fewer reports of dizziness. Table 4 contains inconsistent percentages and denominators. There is no distinct orthostatic outcome, isolated sumac effect or Parkinson population.

fit: grapeseed oil carrier in a topical eucalyptus animal experiment
assessment: The topical mix delayed response to heat. No isolated carrier or oral-oil pain contrast.

fit: topical grapeseed oil mixture in Gua Sha and pain
assessment: A randomized comparison favored bundled Gua Sha with lotion on a Parkinson pain scale. It did not estimate the effect of eating the oil.

fit: reported blood-pressure drop after a hazelnut-containing food
assessment: A blood-pressure drop was reported in the second acute allergy case. There was no standing challenge, assessment of orthostatic lightheadedness, or verified hazelnut oil ingestion.

fit: shared hazelnut flake vehicle in human orthostatic challenge
assessment: In ten healthy men, presyncope occurred after 18 ± 7 and 17 ± 6 minutes in the astragalus and placebo periods, with no significant difference. Both drinks contained hazelnut flakes. There was no hazelnut-free or oil comparison.

fit: pooled hypotension outcome in pediatric food-allergy cohort with hazelnut challenges
assessment: Four children of 88 had hypotension in a pooled cohort covering several foods. The report does not attribute these cases to hazelnuts or measure postural lightheadedness, oil intake or Parkinson disease.

fit: gavage of cumin fruit extract and passive avoidance retention in MPTP mice
assessment: The experiment assessed passive avoidance learning and retention. It does not isolate attention or test toasted cumin in people.

fit: cumin seed roasting and comparative volatile retention
assessment: The analytical comparison shows preparation-dependent aldehyde retention. It cannot estimate an attention response or equate food servings with an essential-oil capsule.

fit: relative cuminaldehyde abundance in dry-roasted cumin odor profile
assessment: This analysis verifies that the marker compound in the essential-oil trial is present after dry roasting. Odor fractions do not establish comparable exposure.

fit: oral steam-distilled cumin oil and simple or complex Cognitrax attention
assessment: Both measured attention contrasts descriptively favor the distilled oil, with inconclusive interaction results. The population and concentrated preparation substantially limit transfer to the frozen claim.

fit: synthetic cumin odor and EEG theta in healthy volunteers
assessment: The original study measured electrical responses to synthetic cumin odor. It gives no behavioral attention contrast after consumption.

fit: Parkinson survey recording cumin use with aggregate nonmotor measures
assessment: Cumin intake was recorded and exploratory nonmotor comparisons were inconclusive after correction. No preparation or cumin-specific attention estimate is reported.

fit: dietary isolated cuminaldehyde and mouse water-maze performance
assessment: Spatial learning and memory measures differ from attention, and the compound is separate from toasted cumin.

fit: aqueous muskmelon peel and two motor proxies
assessment: Table 3 gives shorter rotarod retention and Table 4 higher actophotometer activity. The abstract characterizes the rotarod as improved. The exposure is rind extract.

fit: healthy adult concentrate trial and companion registration
assessment: A 61-participant healthy-adult comparison registered as NCT01767922 reports stress and fatigue. The proprietary freeze-dried concentrate and its endpoints cannot inform the frozen tremor outcome.

fit: melon-derived SOD capsule and frailty protocol
assessment: The capsule protocol lists frailty and quality-of-life outcomes. Registry results are absent and a named raw-fruit or resting-tremor comparison is not planned.

fit: rock melon crossover glycemic protocol
assessment: Rock melon is a named exposure in a registered crossover. Planned outcomes are glycemic index and load, and as of the review no results were available.

fit: melon SOD extract and stress-model cognition
assessment: GliSODin favored memory in the restraint stress experiment. The supplemented mice were assessed for spatial learning and tissue endpoints.

fit: pooled cucurbit intake and occurrence of Parkinson disease
assessment: Same cohort as PMID23661325. Adjusted occurrence RR 1.00 (95% CI 0.72–1.38) combines four cucurbits. The indication is diagnosis occurrence and there is no separate raw-fruit comparison.

fit: melon concentrate, fatigue and exercise outcomes
assessment: Healthy men trained during a human supplement trial. The dried melon concentrate comparison did not give a clear between-group physical-fatigue difference or a separate tremor outcome.

fit: cultivar-specific juice and postprandial glucose
assessment: A ripe pickling-melon versus muskmelon juice contrast concerns glycemia in people with diabetes. Neither a resting-tremor nor isolated raw flesh effect was reported.

fit: traditional sweating ingredient and separate tremor term
assessment: Mahlouji lists historical tremor and melon together only at the review level in separate tables. The Dadmehr textual analysis concerns a broader condition. Shared textual sources are plausible and no independent first-person response is established.

fit: melon enzyme capsule, non-Parkinson mobility and fatigue
assessment: In mobility-limited older women, motor and fatigue differences are inconclusive. Capsules contain a Vauclusien melon extract and wheat gliadin.

fit: cultivar seed extracts, general behavior and rotating rod
assessment: Table 5 has a dose- and time-dependent pattern of rotarod means. Methods describe falls and the table gives time. Table 1 describes general behavior depression with no tremor item.

fit: broader traditional textual practice
assessment: Table 1 lists Cucumis melo under a broader historical condition with unspecified plant part and no firsthand response. Preserve as a companion to the Persian textual lineage.

fit: unripe melon landrace crossover and consumer survey
assessment: Crossover exposes volunteers to servings of separate unripe melon landraces or cucumber. Measured appetite and food reward without a tremor assessment.

fit: Parkinson mixed menu and composite motor examination
assessment: Shared diet in 16 patients includes cantaloupe. Supplement S2 and body Figure 4 score composite motor change. No fruit-level contrast, preparation or separate tremor estimate.

fit: injected black mustard seed extract and mouse tail suspension
assessment: At the highest extract dose mean immobility was 109.16 seconds versus 233.00 with saline. The experiment used an injected ethanolic extract and did not measure clinical depression.

fit: topical mixed botanical patches and PHQ-9 in subthreshold depression
assessment: The controlled comparisons favor mixed topical formulas. Neither arm isolates orally consumed mustard seed.

fit: white mustard seed oil and mouse stress-related behavior
assessment: Behavioral effects favored mustard seed oil in mouse stress models. The study also examined isolated allyl isothiocyanate. Clinical depressive symptoms after ground seed were untested.

fit: extra-virgin olive oil in a multidomain trial with planned anxiety scale
assessment: The protocol schedules DASS and recommends extra-virgin olive oil in a bundled lifestyle intervention. The oil processing method and standalone anxiety effect stay open, and the trial provides no posted outcome estimate.

fit: optional ungraded olive oil and trial-reported anxiety in a different population
assessment: The protocol lists olive oil as a choice within stratified support for older adults with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment. The results abstract reports a favorable SAS direction for the program. The full numeric results, individual exposure and independently assigned oil effect remain unavailable.

fit: verified cold-pressed olive oils in young male rats
assessment: High-phenol oil increased elevated plus-maze open-arm time compared with water. Center time and direct high-versus-low oil contrasts were inconclusive.

fit: Injected shared olive oil vehicle in rat liver injury
assessment: The full seven-group report has three injected oil control groups and four injury groups receiving injected vehicle with toxicant. FEBS poster scope and cohort overlap are uncertain. No anxiety or oral cold-pressed comparator.

fit: olive-oil frequency and self-reported Parkinson anxiety
assessment: Duplicate baseline plots show a small inverse relationship. The graph gives no adjustment or numeric result for the pair, and the questionnaire leaves pressing grade unspecified.

fit: generic cooking and dressing oil within dietary program and Parkinson anxiety
assessment: The intervention assigns a complete Mediterranean diet plus standard care, without oil grade or a separate oil dose. The anxiety interaction is p=.745 and the supplement records nutrient totals only.

fit: shared olive-oil advice and ordinal anxiety change during Parkinson diet phases
assessment: In a local count of the released file, the ketogenic phase had 10 improved, 20 unchanged and four worse anxiety ratings (n=34), and the MCT phase had nine, 22 and six (n=37). fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: S9.664 uses olive oil as the injected rotenone vehicle in mice, and S2.132 as a vehicle for astaxanthin. The vehicle is not an assigned dietary treatment.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: P-14-015 applies olive-leaf extracts and oleuropein to a neuroblastoma cell model. P-14-024 and P-14-026 use a constituent or an oil extract in other cells. No cold-pressed oil anxiety result is supplied.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: P1106 studies extra-virgin olive phenols in macrophages and P1678 compares parenteral lipid formulations in vitro. A separate gastric study records habitual exposure. No Parkinson anxiety or constipation contrast is supplied.

fit: topical ozonized extra-virgin olive oil and pressure wound resolution
assessment: The paired human wound comparison reports no significant resolution difference between topical oils. It does not address dietary cold-pressed or extra-virgin oil or a Parkinson symptom.

fit: topical extra-virgin oil comparator and rat wound microbiology
assessment: No difference between the topical product groups was detected for microbial colonization. The population, route and endpoint differ from the frozen claim.

fit: topical extra-virgin olive oil comparator and rat tail withdrawal
assessment: The different topical products gave no significant separation in thermal latency. Sample independence from the related microbial abstract is unresolved, and the model supplies no oral oil or Parkinson symptom estimate.

fit: olive oil as part of Mediterranean diet adherence by young volunteers
assessment: Among female respondents, anxiety was inversely associated with total diet adherence. Olive oil is a dietary component and its isolated effect, oil grade and Parkinson fit remain unverified.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: T1:PO.26 compares a virgin-olive-rich Mediterranean pattern with conventional low-fat guidance for antioxidant capacity. T2:PO.11 is a metabolic-syndrome dietary score; neither isolates the frozen symptom or preparation.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: A lipid-comparison passage includes olive oil with butter and sunflower oil. It supplies no Parkinson symptom outcome.

fit: olive-oil-enriched diet and incretin response in normal rats
