fit: cinnamon consumption and mood-apathy domain in a Parkinson survey
assessment: The report gives no estimate for cinnamon and the individual apathy item.

fit: cinnamon-containing Kampo and NPI apathy
assessment: Median NPI apathy remained zero at week 24 in an uncontrolled cohort. Baseline floor and mixed treatment prevent cinnamon-specific inference.

fit: cinnamon-containing Kampo formula and apathy in Alzheimer or Lewy body dementia
assessment: Apathy improved within the active arm but the between-group comparison was inconclusive. No separate cinnamon arm.

fit: oral perilla leaf extract and rat REM and NREM duration
assessment: The rat EEG experiment found no clear duration difference in either stage separately. REM duration is not dream enactment and the experiment did not use a Parkinson model.

fit: strawberry-flavored milk reward in a mouse learning task
assessment: The later paper identifies the shared milkshake formulation. D1 receptor manipulation altered reward-associated learning while the motivation measure was relatively preserved. The treatment, food preparation and endpoints do not establish a direction for raw strawberry.

study: BNA2019 injected oil or preference member
fit: animal vehicle or flavored-milk preference outside the frozen preparation
assessment: An object-recognition methods member reports flavored milk in a separate mouse preference test. It contains neither a raw strawberry arm nor a fall outcome.

fit: Other population, active whole-fruit doses, chair-rise outcome
assessment: Ten-week five-arm older-adult trial. Compared fresh fruit at lower and higher doses directly, with other arms adding dried strawberries or capers. Pooled 30-second chair rises improved by about two. Model interaction p=0.999. All groups consumed strawberries. The endpoint was not falls and the trial did not enroll for Parkinson disease.

fit: Isolated phenolic in cell lines; strawberry as one food source
assessment: The study used purified ellagic acid in cancer and comparison cell lines. Apparent p53 and PTEN changes in cancer lines were nonsignificant. No strawberry exposure or measured mobility.

fit: Food composition survey including strawberry
assessment: The survey describes phenolics and antioxidant properties by food source. It does not assign fruit to participants or report a clinical outcome.

fit: garden-strawberry leaf extract given to rotenone-exposed cells
assessment: The original poster reports cell viability and oxidative-stress results. Raw fruit, Parkinson patients and fall frequency were not assessed.

fit: freeze-dried strawberry and prospective registered gait in older adults
assessment: NCT03162913 enrolled 47 older adults with overweight or obesity. The randomized comparison assigned freeze-dried strawberry powder or control over 90 days and registered preferred gait speed. Recent falls and fall-risk conditions were among eligibility restrictions. The completed record lists no posted results or fall-incidence outcome. It is distinct from NCT02051140, which reported fear of falling.

fit: fall adverse events under single-arm strawberry-flavored cannabidiol
assessment: Two of 21 people had a Fall adverse event in the Rett safety report. Its window starts at the preceding randomized trial baseline. Strawberry flavoring is an excipient and there is no separate fruit comparator or recurrence measure.

fit: isolated fisetin and a planned recalled fall count
assessment: The protocol and active recruitment registry describe one non-Parkinson study. The intervention is isolated fisetin and the fall questions are planned without posted outcome data.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: P-15-016 exposes colorectal cell lines to wild strawberry extract. P-03-007 and P-35-069 are plant or fruit-quality experiments. None measures falls after fruit consumption.

fit: different reward formulations in likely linked aged-mouse cohorts
assessment: ASN labels its 13-mouse milkshake cohort ongoing. The companion SfN poster reports more completed touchscreen trials for milkshake than peanut oil. Cohort overlap is plausible, and no raw fruit or fall outcome is reported.

fit: food reaction and descriptive morphology scope
assessment: Entries discuss strawberries in a possible food reaction context and separately use strawberry terms as morphology. There is no named intake or fall contrast.

fit: strawberry extract versus other feeds in rats
assessment: In the primary article Figure 3 and motor results show that only the blueberry arm improved rod walking and rotarod performance. Strawberry had distinct neurochemical results. Aged rats and extract do not identify raw fruit effects in Parkinson disease.

fit: strawberry extract feeding and aging mouse motor tests
assessment: The author abstract reports no reversal of aged-mouse rod, wire, plank or screen deficits with strawberry extract. Extract levels and arm-specific estimates require the original report.

fit: strawberry or blueberry extract and conditioned taste avoidance after irradiation
assessment: Both extracts preserve learned avoidance in the amphetamine condition. Dietary groups do not separate in the lithium chloride condition. The authors measure conditioned learning rather than falls.

fit: strawberry extract and operant response after 1.5 Gy irradiation
assessment: The author abstract reports a favorable twelve-month contrast and no six-month separation. This exposure and behavioral task do not measure Parkinson falls. Full methods and estimates remain open.

fit: strawberry extract, spatial retention and tissue dopamine after irradiation
assessment: The original abstract reports preservation of place information and measured dopamine release. The related behavior is spatial learning. Independence from other same-dose irradiation cohorts remains open.

fit: strawberry fruit-extract applied to model membranes
assessment: The poster and full report appear to share a comparison lineage. Changes depend on the tested membrane property and do not supply an oral or fall outcome.

fit: Whole fresh fruit in a historical clinical narrative, other disease
assessment: Cantlie describes an unspecified subset improving on temporarily exclusive fresh strawberries for tropical sprue. The narrative gives no denominator or comparator and did not measure Parkinson disease or falls.

fit: strawberry leaf extract and membrane assays
assessment: The poster and related article concern leaf extract applied experimentally to lab preparations. No raw-fruit fall endpoint is measured.

fit: strawberry intake frequency and cognitive decline
assessment: In 16,010 older women the adjusted global cognitive slope favors higher strawberry intake. The questionnaire leaves raw preparation unverified and the article reports no Parkinson fall measure.

fit: modeled contaminants from reported foods
assessment: Strawberries contribute to modeled dietary contaminant estimates. Residue and dietary modeling are the exposures and no falls or Parkinson endpoint was assessed.

fit: strawberry extract and operant bar presses after 2.0 Gy irradiation
assessment: Early operant response patterns favor the strawberry diet. Comparisons at 13 and 18 months are inconclusive and irradiated controls are depleted. Primary task performance does not measure fall frequency.

fit: strawberry plant challenge cited in sulfur review
assessment: A plant pathology example explicitly includes strawberry challenged with fungi and reports no observed sulfur accumulation under the tested conditions. This review contains no human ingestion or falls comparison.

fit: freeze-dried strawberry and provoked time-to-fall tasks in aging rats
assessment: Strawberry stayed on the plank longer than blueberry and the stationary rod for less time than blueberry. Strawberry and unsupplemented feed did not differ clearly on rod, rotarod or plank. The study gives no clinical fall rate.

fit: wild berry processing assays and underlying strawberry citations
assessment: The original comparison covers four other wild berries. The strawberry cognition and rodent results are separate previously identified studies.

fit: strawberries pooled with other fruit in falls-hospitalization cohort
assessment: In 1,429 older women followed for up to 14.5 years, the adjusted HR for other fruit including strawberries was 1.00 (95% CI 0.98 to 1.03) per 20 g/day. No strawberry-specific estimate, Parkinson stratum or recurrent fall count.

fit: Parkinson gait and disability context without food assignment
assessment: The clinical report classifies severe abnormal gait in 84 of 214 assessed participants. It provides no frequency of recurring falls or fruit exposure.

fit: combined food category and previous-year fall report
assessment: Cross-sectional public-housing study estimates adjusted OR 0.55 (95% CI 0.37 to 0.83) for a prior-year fall with daily fruit and vegetable consumption. No individual fruit or Parkinson comparison.

fit: preference for a strawberry-flavored nutritional drink
assessment: A survey of 148 older adults reports 32.9% strawberry flavor preference. The vitamin-D falls analysis is a separate poster, with no flavor-related fall contrast.

fit: complete original index and separate plant-development reference
assessment: The genuine strawberry fruit entry indexes small auxin-up RNAs. The indexed source is a plant gene-expression chapter, with page 133 still outside the available body. No assignment or falls estimate.

fit: strawberry-flavored formula in both rehabilitation assignments
assessment: Mobility improved with the nutrient formula among 127 analyzed. Strawberry and vanilla flavors were available in both assignments. No flavor-isolated or fall-frequency estimate.

fit: low
assessment: In healthy older adults freeze-dried strawberry versus placebo did not improve gait or balance; fear of falling did not differ, and recent falls were screened at baseline. No intervention-period fall-frequency comparison or Parkinson population was reported.

fit: Parkinson diagnostic strawberry odor in freezing groups
assessment: Nominal strawberry odor item p=.039 in Table 2 for Parkinson freezer versus non-freezer discrimination. Strawberry was not in the final three-item panel. There was no fruit consumption intervention or falls endpoint.

fit: purified strawberry-associated constituent with repeated rotarod event counts
assessment: High-dose purified procyanidin B2 reduced the number of falls back onto a rotating-apparatus trial within five minutes. The reagent was not shown to come from strawberry, and the study used an experimental demyelination model. Fig. 2D and its prose disagree about the comparator latency.

fit: strawberry milkshake used as common cue-learning reward
assessment: The outcome is conditioned approach behavior and associated neural signaling in mice. Milkshake is a shared task reward rather than an isolated strawberry comparison.

fit: total fruit frequency and falls with fracture in a case-control study
assessment: Case-control analysis compares aggregate fruit consumption among fracture-associated fall cases and controls. It does not isolate strawberries, recurrent events or Parkinson disease.

fit: shared strawberry extract and randomized Parkinson drug comparison
assessment: Table 3 reports at least one fall in 4 of 31 participants on cannabinoids and 3 of 30 on placebo. Both arms were given strawberry extract and no separate food effect or fall frequency was measured.

fit: reported seasonal strawberry consumption in healthy adults
assessment: The 57-person dietary reanalysis confirms strawberry intake timing. The study measured gut outcomes without a separate strawberry exposure comparison or fall count.

fit: traditional wild strawberry food use and access
assessment: The assessment documents wild strawberries as First Foods in a food-security discussion. It reports no firsthand symptom observation.

fit: optional strawberry or blackcurrant jam in a mixed-food endurance study
assessment: Eight participants tested chili versus control pancakes. Jam was optional and not assigned by type. Plank endurance cannot be attributed to strawberry or translated to falls.

fit: Same ErdBEHR participants, food intervention subset, microbial outcomes
assessment: Analysis of 69 healthy older adults from DRKS00026998 reports microbial results. It supplies a distinct outcome from the same trial family and no fall counts or Parkinson endpoint.

fit: combined dietary produce and retrospective fall injury
assessment: Inadequate combined fruit and vegetable intake had adjusted OR 1.41 (95% CI 1.05 to 1.90) for prior-year fall injury. Cross-sectional design, no fruit-specific effect and no Parkinson stratum.

fit: randomized six-fruit whole-food crossover and postural sway
assessment: Strawberries were one of six supplied fruits then were among those blended before the final evaluation. In 37 adults with balance measurements, the time-by-phase sway comparison had p=.457. No fall counts or separate strawberry effect.

fit: strawberry agriculture and fruit quality
assessment: The primary horticultural study treats strawberry plants with foliar melatonin under aluminum stress and reports plant performance and fruit quality. No patient or dietary falls outcome is studied.

fit: isolated lupeol in a mouse model
assessment: Strawberry is listed among food sources of lupeol. The mouse intervention uses the isolated compound and has no raw strawberry arm or clinical falls.

fit: strawberries grouped with cherry and grape in an overeating survey
assessment: The poster groups three fruits and gives a retrospective reported food category rather than separate intake or recurring fall effects.

fit: leaf extract in Parkinson-related cells and a mouse motor model
assessment: Rotenone-treated mice fed strawberry leaf extract had longer day-28 rotarod latency at high dose and shorter pole T-turn. The report has no edible raw fruit arm or spontaneous Parkinson fall frequency.

fit: whole-fruit aqueous extract in a distinct rat prevention cohort
assessment: Eight-month strawberry extract exposure changed a tissue dopamine response with no reported strawberry maze benefit or spontaneous fall outcome.

fit: Historical strawberry citation and separate mixed fruit case
assessment: The case used fruit and attempted liver extract. Strawberries appear in a historical discussion. The recorded administration did not specify a particular berry or track falls.

fit: Repeated strawberry phases in one person with other disease and cointerventions
assessment: Improved weight and stool outcomes occurred during the most sustained strawberry period while diet and other care changed, and improvement continued afterwards. The author noted intestinal intolerance in some other recipients. A sternal injury during transfer supplies no fall outcome.

study: Van der Burg 1880 tropical sprue monograph
fit: Historical whole fruit discussed in mixed sprue treatment
assessment: The clinician personally observed Sonius's practice and reported both tolerability and possible digestive irritation. The documented pediatric case used other fruit. There are no raw-strawberry-specific fall data.

fit: marjoram infusion and composite nonmotor symptom score
assessment: The tea arm improved on aggregate NMSS. No separate urinary urgency comparison or fresh-leaf exposure was verified.

fit: oral cold-pressed avocado oil and open-field crossings in obese mice
assessment: Figure 3B does not mark a clear direct effect on crossings with oil. Crossing counts measure activity, not walking speed, and the mice did not have parkinsonism.

fit: maternal oral avocado oil and offspring open-field activity
assessment: Adult offspring in the oil arm showed lower overall locomotion. Maternal exposure, unverified oil processing and the animal activity outcome do not establish clinical walking slowness.

fit: oral avocado oil and movement asymmetry in a Huntington model
assessment: A matching conference report recorded roughly 89% fewer ipsilateral turns in lesioned rats. The exposure's pressing method and clinical walking-speed effect are unresolved.

fit: summer savory topical gel and dental outcomes
assessment: The original placebo comparison measures palatal erythema and Candida, without a recorded acoustic volume outcome, Parkinson cohort or ingestion of fresh savory.

fit: saffron capsules and total Parkinson motor score
assessment: The randomized Tehran trial analyzed 52 people across arms and reports motor Part III total p=.424. The public results give no separate rigidity comparison and the capsule preparation was not specified.

fit: saffron plus chamomile and composite outcomes
assessment: Registered combination and constituent comparisons. No posted results.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: P-15-013 assays hydromethanolic Crocus sativus tepal extracts and performs molecular docking. The floral waste preparation differs from ground stigma, and no symptom was measured.

fit: isolated injected crocin and catalepsy in a rat toxin model
assessment: The public Figure 3 visually shows shorter descent latency after three injected crocin doses, roughly 7–12 versus 58 seconds with malathion alone. Full methods and exact inference remain unavailable. This nonhuman catalepsy comparison does not transfer directly to culinary ground saffron.

fit: saffron in a shared vegetarian menu and composite motor outcome
assessment: The pilot lists saffron in the menu. It provides no isolated ground saffron and rigidity estimate.

fit: saffron extract combination and aggregate motor score
assessment: The uncontrolled chart review reported lower total UPDRS III after the supplement. It provides no separate rigidity estimate or ground saffron comparison.

fit: isolated intraperitoneal safranal and hindlimb catalepsy in MPTP mice
assessment: Figure 3A reports shorter hindlimb release time versus the untreated MPTP group. The model stiffness proxy and injected constituent do not provide a clinical rigidity comparison for ground saffron.

fit: isolated constituent and composite motor score
assessment: Within-group composite motor improvement. No ingredient-level or symptom-specific treatment estimate was available.

fit: injected crocetinate derivative and animal catalepsy
assessment: High dose reduced catalepsy versus BPA. Preparation and route differ from eating ground saffron, and animal catalepsy does not measure human rigidity.

fit: flaxseed oil in an omega-3-adequate rat diet and odor discrimination
assessment: Second-generation rats on the deficient diet made more errors in two-odor learning than rats receiving the flaxseed-oil-containing diet. The result tests developmental omega-3 adequacy without a Parkinson population or documented cold-pressing.

fit: ALA-varied developmental diets and olfactory behavior in mice
assessment: The lower-ALA blend reduced electroolfactogram amplitudes but did not clearly change olfactory behavior. The blends did not include flaxseed oil and the mice had no Parkinson model.

fit: EPA and DHA with olfactory training and postviral odor threshold
assessment: Odor threshold favored adding long-chain omega-3 to training. The product does not test alpha-linolenic acid or cold-pressed flaxseed oil.

fit: turmeric-containing formula and speech fluency
assessment: A combined Parkinson granule improved a secondary nonfluent speech rating. It did not isolate ground turmeric or measure acoustic volume.

fit: nanomicelle curcumin and composite Parkinson scale
assessment: The accessible MDS-UPDRS results do not separate speech from other motor findings. Acoustic loudness was not reported.

fit: reported use of turmeric products for voice care
assessment: The survey records turmeric use among 69 of 253 responding herbal users. It gives no ground specification or acoustic voice-volume change.

fit: oral mustard rice and short-term whole-saliva collection in healthy volunteers
assessment: Author abstract reports approximately fourfold fasting secretion with mustard rice versus threefold with unspiced rice in five participants. Exact mustard form and Parkinson drooling outcomes are unavailable.

fit: unstimulated salivary flow in Parkinson disease without a food intervention
assessment: Parkinson participants had reduced unstimulated secretion compared with matched controls. Salivary flow and patient complaints about excess saliva do not provide a food-specific drooling result.

fit: rat salivary secretion after perfusion of a mustard constituent
assessment: Arterial allyl isothiocyanate reduced carbachol-induced saliva secretion in the rat preparation. Drooling severity after dietary mustard and Parkinson disease were not studied.

fit: injected thyme extract in a rat brain ischemia balance test
assessment: Two extract doses improved rotarod balance in the reported comparison. No dried culinary leaf, oral exposure or Parkinson postural-instability assessment.

fit: isolated carvacrol and coordination tasks in lesioned rats
assessment: Published July 2019 online. The study reports motor task improvement after carvacrol in 6-OHDA rats. Clinical postural instability after dried thyme was untested.

fit: isolated thymol injection and rat motor tasks
assessment: Rotarod retention was inconclusive, with greater distance in one test setting. The experiment did not test culinary thyme or clinical postural instability.

fit: thyme extract and coordination tests in paraquat mice
assessment: Ladder, footprint and wire-hanging tests were included in the reported broad behavioral improvement. Task-specific contrasts and clinical postural instability were not reported in the public abstract.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: S7.478 orally administers oat-stem lignin to irradiated mice and S6.415 studies oat seed germination. Neither is a prepared oat-grain or Parkinson motor comparison.

fit: oatmeal and total Parkinson symptom burden
assessment: The aggregate estimate is inconclusive and apathy severity was not analyzed against oatmeal alone.

fit: diet-pattern scores and measured Parkinson apathy
assessment: The cross-sectional study did not report a significant apathy association or isolate an oat item.

fit: meal timing and Parkinson levodopa concentration variability
assessment: With and without lunch differed in levodopa concentration variability in ten people with Parkinson disease. The meal data supply no sumac attribution or diary-based daily OFF duration.

fit: sumac extract applied to Parkinson donor skin cells
assessment: No oral exposure, levodopa coadministration or medication-state outcome was included.

fit: marjoram infusion and composite nonmotor symptom score
assessment: The tea arm improved on aggregate NMSS. No separate drooling comparison or fresh-leaf exposure was verified.

fit: mixed fermented garlic and ginger capsules using grapeseed oil
assessment: The filing reports combined diarrhea-and-constipation improvement among 27 adult respondents. Oil processing, separate constipation change and controlled attribution were absent.

fit: grapeseed oil enema and colon tissue injury in rats
assessment: Microscopic lesion score was 0.88 after grapeseed oil enema and 2.67 in untreated colitis. Bowel frequency and constipation were unreported, and the oil route was rectal.

fit: oral combined grapeseed oil carrier and colitis stool composite
assessment: The carbon-60 and grapeseed oil combination lowered a disease activity composite containing loose-stool and bleeding scores (p < .05). The study had no oil-only arm or constipation outcome.

fit: Leaf-enriched rice bran oil and rodent immobility outcomes
assessment: Haloperidol catalepsy and locomotor tests used a mixed Garcinia formulation without a plain oil arm. Dystonia and clinical Parkinson physiology were not measured.

fit: Solvent-extracted oral rice bran oil in a neuroleptic movement model
assessment: Improved vacuous chewing and rotarod performance do not quantify dystonia. Cohort overlap across companion studies and the oil's commercial refining grade remain unresolved.

fit: Rice bran oil placebo and clinical Parkinson motor complications
assessment: Part IV was prespecified. The sources give no item 4.6 painful OFF-state dystonia estimate or isolated dystonia severity, and do not specify oil grade.

fit: chives on a Parkinson pilot diet menu and composite motor score
assessment: The Appendix A menu names chives and the pilot reports changes in UPDRS III. It gives neither chive preparation nor an ingredient-specific stride measure.

fit: chemical measurements in culinary oil pressed from roasted pumpkin seeds
assessment: Some overlapping phenolic compounds were measurable in roasted oil. Quantities were small and variable and the study contains no gait data or extract-dose equivalence.

fit: isolated p-coumaric acid and measured stride length in a haloperidol mouse model
assessment: Two higher purified-compound groups showed longer stride versus disease control. Oil concentrations are much lower than the tested isolated doses, with no established transferable effect.

fit: pumpkin seed extract and narrow-beam traversal in rotenone mice
assessment: Day-28 crossing time was 8.0 or 4.85 seconds with extract versus 29.25 seconds with rotenone alone. Traversal time differs from stride length, and the two publications describe one seed-extract experiment.

fit: methanolic Cucurbita pepo seed extract and measured stride length in a haloperidol rat model
assessment: Publisher Figure 4 shows longer stride at ascending extract levels than disease control. This applies to the extracted seed and animal model, with no toasted-oil or patient contrast.

fit: Cucurbita maxima seed ethanol extract and differing rod-task results
assessment: Favorable rotarod retention contrasted with slower stationary-rod arrival for the highest dose on day 21. The study gives no stride length or oil comparison.

fit: pumpkin seed oil in a Parkinson diet and a composite motor score
assessment: Gait contributes to the composite scale. The trial reports no instrumented stride length, individual oil intake or toasted preparation.

fit: fermented red cabbage blend and DASS depression in healthy adults
assessment: No between-group DASS depression difference (p=.607). Within-group stress and total scores improved. Product also contained beetroot and caraway and was fermented.

fit: repeated kindergarten vegetable exposure, intake and liking
assessment: Vegetables were offered in conjunction with a reward. The sample was children, and neither adult symptoms nor the matched preparation were assessed. The registration gives n = 82, while the two arm counts in the poster add to 84.

fit: oral red cabbage anthocyanin extract in aging mice
assessment: Cognitive benefit reported; depression was not measured. Exposure is an enriched extract.

fit: sumac extract in Parkinson-derived fibroblasts
assessment: The extract changed cellular measurements. No participants ingested sumac and bradykinesia was not measured.

fit: Recorded void frequency in a likely overlapping healthy-adult publication series
assessment: The 2014 and 2018 reports share the 105 participants' sample design, preparations and days. Voids increased relative to baseline in all dose groups at day 10. Neither report measured sudden urgency or had a separate control group or Parkinson cohort.

fit: Self-reported urinary volume symptom after brewed leaf tea
assessment: Four of 11 reported polyuria after a single dose. This uncontrolled observation provides neither a sudden-urge measure nor a Parkinson cohort.

fit: eight-oil oral blend during acute cystitis and measured void count
assessment: All three observational groups reported less frequent urination. The original abstract does not give a standalone urgency or brewed leaf comparison.

fit: Placebo-controlled concentrated leaf extract with kidney endpoints
assessment: The registered Thai comparison reports safety and biomarkers after oral capsule dosing in CKD, without brewed tea or a Parkinson urinary urgency measure.

fit: pooled spices and Parkinson freezing item
assessment: Small inverse plotted sign from unspecified aggregated spices. Ground turmeric, episode frequency and pairwise uncertainty cannot be established.

fit: curcumin and walking speed outside Parkinson
assessment: The 400-m walking speed change was numerically smaller on curcumin than placebo, with no posted group comparison. Speed differs from freezing frequency.

fit: turmeric-containing granule and composite gait context
assessment: Composite conventional UPDRS motor and activities scores do not give individual freezing frequency. The formulation contains multiple botanicals.

fit: curcumin formulation and automated paw gait
assessment: Oil-formulated curcumin improved several mouse paw-contact and stance outcomes more consistently than the saline suspension. Neither arm measured freezing events.

fit: curcumin with levodopa and beam walking
assessment: Neither curcumin nor drug combinations clearly altered time to cross a beam versus rotenone control. No freezing episodes were recorded.

fit: reported asparagus avoidance and perceived choking risk
assessment: Parkinson family focus groups described avoiding stringy asparagus. The report does not identify a steamed preparation, observed exposure or measured change in swallowing severity.

fit: asparagus exposure and acute allergic dysphagia in an occupational case
assessment: A cook with positive sensitization tests reported difficulty swallowing after eating asparagus. The acute allergic case and unknown preparation leave the steamed-asparagus claim open.

fit: asparagus-and-chicken soup in a sensory tasting by older adults with dysphagia
assessment: The dysphagia pilot includes an asparagus-and-chicken soup among foods rated for liking. It does not isolate asparagus or assess a change in swallowing severity.

fit: asparagus in a tube complication
assessment: Citing clinical literature describes undigested asparagus at a knotted PEG-J tube. The accessible material gives no oral swallowing outcome for steamed asparagus.

fit: low
assessment: The thesis separately reports contralateral forepaw use after injected carvacrol and a unilateral rat lesion. The lower dose did not clearly differ from sham and the higher dose still did. The source does not report a significant treatment-versus-lesion control comparison for this endpoint, handwriting, or herb ingestion.

fit: low
assessment: An isolated compound reduced forelimb-use asymmetry in a unilateral mouse lesion model. Cylinder wall contact does not measure handwriting size or fresh summer savory exposure.

fit: extra-virgin olive oil in the background diet of a Parkinson case
assessment: Reported hypomimia improvement after addition of different foods. The pre-existing oil was extra-virgin and its intake change was unspecified.

fit: dried perilla leaf powder and home systolic pressure in healthy adults
assessment: The full-group home-pressure comparison was inconclusive. A subgroup selected by month-six pressure showed lower changes. No standing pressure drop, lightheadedness or fresh leaf estimate was reported.

fit: shrimp scampi and acute dysarthria
assessment: One case developed dysarthria after shrimp scampi with confirmed bacteremia and a suspected toxin diagnosis. Cooking method, toxin confirmation and speech intelligibility testing were absent.

fit: mixed raw seafood exposure and dysarthria
assessment: One of 27 cerebral angiostrongyliasis cases reported dysarthria after pooled raw or undercooked shrimp or snail histories. The patient's food was unreported.

fit: mixed seafood exposure and confirmed botulism with descriptive speech signs
assessment: Shrimp was present in a meal containing roe with the outbreak toxin. Acute toxin-associated speech signs do not attribute an effect to boiled shrimp.

study: BNA2019 injected oil or preference member
fit: animal vehicle or flavored-milk preference outside the frozen preparation
assessment: PT080 and another member report injected corn oil as vehicle or control in a perimenopause model. The oil route, associated interventions and measures differ from oral corn oil.

fit: corn oil as active lipid comparator in a Parkinson trial
assessment: The accessible result covers aggregate UPDRS, with no rest-tremor item or isolated oil estimate. Original full table remains inaccessible.

fit: cannabidiol in corn oil in an open-label Parkinson pilot
assessment: The six-person pilot reports an aggregate motor comparison with no rest item. Matching placebo is mentioned, but no separate oil-only group or placebo phase is reported.

fit: corn oil shared by all groups in a Parkinson cannabidiol trial
assessment: Corn-oil placebo and cannabidiol groups report only UPDRS III changes. The common carrier, unknown refining and absent rest-tremor item preclude an isolated directional estimate.

fit: corn oil as a shared carrier
assessment: The tremor contrast favored cannabidiol during public speaking. The intervention did not isolate corn oil or measure resting tremor.

fit: soybean oil-containing pea protein and alginate gel beads designed for oral delivery
assessment: The authors report mechanical gel behavior and in vitro release. There is no patient swallowing comparison or known oil grade.

fit: soybean oil vitamin D gel and tested texture classification
assessment: Texture and consistency tests place a formulated soybean-oil carrier in IDDSI levels 4–5 according to the authors. No observed swallowing event or refined-oil contrast.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: P1018 describes intravenous soybean oil in propofol or Intralipid and P1121 compares intragastric soy milk with cow milk. These are distinct preparations and neither tests culinary soybean oil in Parkinson disease.

fit: food-related material in an imaging report
assessment: The original MR colonography study places excised pig colon specimens in soybean oil for imaging. This is a nonoral laboratory medium with no dose, grade or Parkinson symptom comparison.

fit: soybean oil in both softgel formulations and subjective swallowing adaptation
assessment: Some participants reported mild difficulty swallowing large capsules. Oil grade and arm counts were unreported. Both arms contained oil and there was no Parkinson dysphagia comparison.

fit: soybean oil in graded fish-gel formulations
assessment: Higher oil concentration reduced measured hardness but affected shape stability. The bench outcomes do not measure patient swallowing.

fit: soybean oil gradient and texture modification for a model dysphagia food
assessment: The selected soybean-oil and gum formulation lowered hardness and adhesiveness and the final mooncake met IDDSI texture level 4. It gives no patient swallowing severity result and no oil grade.

fit: separate gastrointestinal conference member and ingredient context
assessment: P0635 groups recipients by intravenous soybean or other lipid emulsion. A different member reports soybean sensitization. Neither uses the frozen culinary preparation or Parkinson outcome.

fit: cinnamaldehyde preparation and Parkinson model rigidity and catalepsy
assessment: The conference abstract reported less catalepsy and rigidity with pretreatment and did not report dystonic postures.

fit: cinnamon leaf preparations and rotenone rat catalepsy
assessment: Bar-test times were lower with some leaf formulations. Ground bark and clinical dystonia were unmeasured.

fit: Ambient grapeseed carrier and PSQI in long-term care
assessment: The dissertation reports ambient grapeseed as the control for lavender plus the same oil, with no clear baseline-adjusted arm difference. It does not isolate a grapeseed effect or report processing, ingestion or dream enactment.

fit: Grapeseed massage carrier and generic sleep difficulty
assessment: The comparison tested adding rose oil to grapeseed massage and did not isolate grapeseed. Oil refining, dietary exposure, Parkinson disease and dream enactment were unmeasured.

fit: oral grapeseed cookie; healthy adults; registered sleep questionnaire correlation; no posted results
assessment: The registry describes 10 g grapeseed oil in daily cookies, and a blood linoleic acid-sleep questionnaire correlation; study lot refining, dream enactment and Parkinson cohort are not established. Official results were absent on 2026-11-15; published lipid outcomes are not sleep outcomes.

fit: Gua Sha and dream enactment outcomes with unspecified oil
assessment: The randomized trial measured REM sleep behavior outcomes. The accessible methods did not identify the scraping oil, and the intervention was topical.

fit: Grapeseed inhalation and polysomnography in primary insomnia
assessment: The author abstract reports no significant grapeseed-only difference from untreated on listed sleep measures. Whole article tables, refining and oral exposure are unverified. Neither Parkinson disease nor dream-enactment frequency was measured.

fit: sweet potato test bolus in a primate model
assessment: Sweet potato served as a shared chewing stimulus. Dyskinesia was outside the experiment.

fit: Curry leaf extract and coordination in a rat model
assessment: The primary report gives rotarod falls and imposed posture outcomes. It uses aqueous extract rather than cooked leaves and does not measure Parkinson rest-tremor severity.

fit: Safety reporting for curry-leaf iron extract in anemia
assessment: The iron product is a botanical extract rather than cooked curry leaves. The primary publication reports no adverse events but does not separately measure rest tremor and does not enroll Parkinson participants.

fit: curry leaves in a Parkinson diet menu with composite motor score
assessment: The menu lists curry leaves and UPDRS III includes resting tremor. Cooked preparation and the individual tremor score are unreported.

fit: PD pooled bean category and whole-diet drool association; no pinto exposure estimate
assessment: The drool association concerns total MIND score, not canned pinto beans or an ingredient-specific effect.

fit: reported fish intake and aggregated psychotic-like experiences among Swedish women
assessment: The published fatty-fish category shows associations in both directions across intake levels, with a broader psychotic-like symptom outcome.

fit: Parkinson clinical charts compare motor-fluctuation groups by reported high-protein meal interaction; hallucination occurrence recorded
assessment: The motor-fluctuation subgroup reports less charted hallucination in patients with protein-related motor fluctuations. Food species, preparation, modality and episode frequency are not established, and the retrospective association does not isolate salmon.

fit: Parkinson diet plans list canned and pan-cooked salmon; a visual hallucination event occurred in ketogenic assignment
assessment: No grilled preparation or individual salmon consumption is established. Hallucinations resolved after a pramipexole reduction; symptom frequency and meal timing are unreported.

fit: sumac fruit extracts and cholinesterase inhibition in vitro
assessment: Water extract inhibited AChE and BChE, with a null dichloromethane result. There was no attention task.

fit: medicinal Rhus javanica galls and exploratory attention measures
assessment: ASRS and Tower of Hanoi time favored the gall extract. Number count outcomes were inconclusive. Species, plant part, preparation and population differ from the frozen claim.

fit: injected sumac fruit extract and avoidance learning in adult male rats
assessment: The abstract identifies longer dark-compartment entry latency with the lower extract dose. The task did not measure attention after eating ground sumac.

fit: injected sumac extract and avoidance learning in gonadectomized rats
assessment: Injected sumac extract lengthened avoidance-related latency in a gonadectomy model. Learning was measured in a shuttle box.

fit: olive oil grades and older adult gait speed
assessment: No clear difference in four-meter gait speed. The trial did not measure stride length or enroll Parkinson participants.

fit: extra-virgin olive oil in a factorial diet study with planned stride measures
assessment: The full protocol and schedule verify planned same-foot and height-normalized stride measures. The registry and protocol report no actual intake, verified pressing method or results.

fit: topical ozonized extra-virgin olive oil and pressure wound resolution
assessment: The paired human wound comparison reports no significant resolution difference between topical oils. It does not address dietary cold-pressed or extra-virgin oil or a Parkinson symptom.

fit: topical extra-virgin oil comparator and rat wound microbiology
assessment: No difference between the topical product groups was detected for microbial colonization. The population, route and endpoint differ from the frozen claim.

fit: topical extra-virgin olive oil comparator and rat tail withdrawal
assessment: The different topical products gave no significant separation in thermal latency. Sample independence from the related microbial abstract is unresolved, and the model supplies no oral oil or Parkinson symptom estimate.

fit: olive oil as part of Mediterranean diet adherence by young volunteers
assessment: Among female respondents, anxiety was inversely associated with total diet adherence. Olive oil is a dietary component and its isolated effect, oil grade and Parkinson fit remain unverified.

fit: olive oil comparison arm and measured stride length
assessment: Single- and dual-task stride time-by-group p values were .753 and .537. Both groups received the same exergame training; the olive oil grade was unspecified.

fit: olive oil diet and mouse footprint outcomes after focal stroke
assessment: Oil alone gave no clear improvement in reported footprint measures. The model was ischemic stroke and processing was unspecified.

fit: uncontrolled gastroresistant ground red pepper and abdominal pain diary in IBS
assessment: In ten adults with IBS, five weeks of 2.5 g/day pepper was followed by a reduction from 3.08 to 1.71 points (p<.05 within participants). There was no concurrent comparison, and the study did not verify ground cayenne or Parkinson pain.

fit: topical capsaicin and localized neuropathic pain
assessment: One person reported pain relief after a patch. Route differs and the case lacked a control.

fit: oral red pepper powder and epigastric pain in functional dyspepsia
assessment: In functional dyspepsia, week-five epigastric pain was 1.15 versus 2.32 after 2.5 g/day encapsulated ground red pepper or placebo. Two active participants stopped for pain. The paper and earlier letter describe one cohort. Cayenne cultivar and Parkinson pain were unverified.

fit: oral ground red chili and urgency thresholds in healthy adults
assessment: Three days of 5 g/day ground Capsicum frutescens in capsules lowered first, moderate and severe rectal urgency thresholds relative to placebo. The pressure range elicited no pain threshold, and there was no Parkinson population.

fit: meal with ground red chili and acute abdominal pain in IBS-D
assessment: Both 2 g oral chili conditions increased peak abdominal pain versus the standard meal (p<.05). A project manuscript records pain in 5/20 without chili, 11/20 with chili in food and 13/20 with chili capsules. The commercial chili cultivar and Parkinson pain effect remain unverified.

fit: colon-release whole ground red pepper and daily abdominal pain in IBS
assessment: The full Results report no significant between-group diary pain contrast. Active-arm late pain improved compared with its own baseline, six active patients discontinued for onset pain and eight patients reduced dose. The abstract conclusion and the personal overall effectiveness rating are distinct from the diary contrast.

fit: repeated red chili powder capsules and separate abdominal pain, burning and first rectal sensation endpoints in IBS-D
assessment: The 16-person crossover found lower meal-provoked abdominal burning and higher pressure at first rectal sensation. Maximum abdominal pain was inconclusive (p=.799 at week six, Figure 2B). Earlier ten-person reports appear to overlap and are counted once with the 2014 report.

fit: topical capsaicin and experimentally provoked localized hand pain
assessment: Study participants in the pain group averaged 3.5/10 before the training task. No participants in the NoPain group reported pain. Skin provocation cannot estimate Parkinson pain after consuming ground cayenne.

fit: commercial ground red chili and separate acute pain and burning outcomes
assessment: In a double-blind randomized crossover, 15 healthy adults and 15 people with nonerosive reflux disease consumed commercial ground Capsicum frutescens or placebo in capsules. The reflux group’s postprandial abdominal burning scores were 2.2 ± 2.5 versus 0.3 ± 0.8 (p < .05). Abdominal pain was collected separately and was inconclusive, as were both pain and burning comparisons in the healthy volunteers. The red chili cultivar and clinical context differ from ground cayenne and Parkinson pain in 0448.

fit: oral formulated red chili extract and abdominal pain reports
assessment: Results section 3.5 records four early abdominal pain reports in the higher-dose group. The discussion conflicts with this count. The report supplies no pain intensity, verified cayenne cultivar or Parkinson cohort.

fit: nigella oil in an MPTP mouse study family
assessment: The reports contain motor assays and describe a tremor difference. The study did not count gait freezing and the earlier version shares the animal approval.

fit: comparison of refined olive oil and extra-virgin olive oil in mild cognitive impairment
assessment: The primary publication identifies refined exposure and reports cognitive and imaging outcomes. It provides no visual hallucination count or oil-free control.

fit: olive oil comparator and aggregate positive symptom outcome
assessment: The trial prespecified positive psychiatric symptoms with an olive oil comparator. Oil grade and a visual hallucination endpoint are unverified, and the registry has no posted results.

fit: olive oil in a composite dietary score among older coronary patients
assessment: The outcome is reported by Mediterranean dietary score and diabetes status. No grade, oil-specific estimate or Parkinson symptom result was reported.

fit: olive oil comparison arm and psychiatric symptom scale
assessment: The trial tested omega-3 against olive oil with antipsychotic treatment in schizophrenia. No visual-hallucination frequency or verified refined grade.

fit: garden chervil leaf and stem chemical analysis
assessment: Fresh leaves and stems were lyophilized for chemical measurements with no behavioral testing.

fit: methanol extract of culinary chervil in enzyme and cell assays
assessment: Enzyme assays and docking do not determine attention after dried chervil.

fit: canola-containing diet and a measured Parkinson urinary item
assessment: Urinary problems favored ketogenic diet by 0.70 points over the low-fat diet listing canola. The broad ordinal urinary item does not count urgency episodes and the oil contribution was not isolated.

fit: whole green cardamom powder in randomized type 2 diabetes trial
assessment: Systolic blood pressure fell relative to placebo. The trial did not assess lightheadedness on standing or Parkinson’s.

fit: presyncope and hypotension in a cardamom-containing bun challenge case
assessment: The original event included presyncope and a mixed-bun challenge produced hypotension. The findings concern acute allergy, with no orthostatic Parkinson measure.

fit: cardamom food exposure and presyncope in allergy case
assessment: Presyncope occurred after a mixed dish in a person with cardamom reactivity. Standing pressure and Parkinson orthostatic symptoms were not measured.

fit: cardamom named in an adverse-event table and case-specific symptoms
assessment: Cardamom is recorded with finger numbness. Multiple-herb dizziness and blood-pressure reports are different cases. No specific postural symptom is attributable to ground cardamom.

fit: intravenous crude cardamom extract in anesthetized rats
assessment: The extract lowered arterial blood pressure. Lightheadedness on standing was outside the model.

fit: green cardamom powder in hypertension without a comparison arm
assessment: Resting systolic pressure decreased over 12 weeks. No standing measurement or Parkinson orthostatic symptom was reported.

fit: green cardamom powder in randomized prediabetes trial
assessment: No significant between-arm blood pressure change. Standing lightheadedness and Parkinson’s were unmeasured.

fit: resveratrol combination and total neuropsychiatric score in Alzheimer disease
assessment: The NPI total treatment-by-visit estimate was 0.368 (95% CI −0.584 to 1.319). Separate visual hallucination scores were unreported. Both groups received red grape juice and neither received grapeseed oil.

fit: cardamom listed in multicomponent Parkinson diet and composite UPDRS III
assessment: The composite improved and includes a speech item. The authors did not report speech intelligibility separately or isolate cardamom.

fit: Recovered Japanese pepper bark fraction source with injected animal motor-tone and toxicity outcomes
assessment: Original full Methods link the tested precursor to crude bark preparation rather than culinary fruit. Table 1 and adjacent prose disagree for akinesia at one dose. Reduced tone and convulsions were recorded in different toxicology contexts and give no clinical rigidity direction.

fit: Parkinson case with baseline rigidity and walking follow-up
assessment: The report describes severe baseline rigidity and improved walking under the formula and daily rehabilitation. It does not provide a repeat rigidity outcome.

fit: acute Parkinson medication syndrome and combination therapy
assessment: Clinical recovery after fecal impaction involved oral daikenchuto and intravenous levodopa. The report supplies no isolated ground-pepper comparison or rigidity estimate.

fit: PD pooled beans and motor symptom aggregate including handwriting
assessment: Generic bean intake and motor aggregate do not establish boiled pinto intake or a small-handwriting effect.

fit: spinach extract and practiced peg running
assessment: The spinach group showed greater improvement in normalized peg running with repetition but no clear difference in actual running times. Steamed spinach and Parkinson balance were untested.

fit: registered balance with spinach extract and exercise
assessment: Both the registry and the same-cohort thesis planned baseline and follow-up balance. The strength publication and the thesis give no located balance result, and the placebo is described as sucrose and maltodextrin in different documents.

fit: spinach extract chow and aging rat balance measures
assessment: Blueberry outperformed spinach on the rod and rotarod. The paper did not report a clear spinach-versus-control balance advantage.

fit: oral Parkinson trial vehicle and communication domain
assessment: The placebo group communication change was zero and groups were not clearly different. No speech intelligibility measure is available, and oil exposure was shared.

fit: oral tarragon extract and spatial learning in chronically restrained rats
assessment: The extract improved Morris water maze performance under stress. The experiment measured spatial learning and memory without isolating executive function.

fit: injected tarragon extract and mouse open-field distance
assessment: Figure 3 generally found unchanged travel, with a reduction at 100 mg/kg. An injected extract and aggregate exploration do not estimate gait speed after fresh tarragon in Parkinson’s.

fit: oral tarragon extract and a composite weakness scale in EAE mice
assessment: The ordinal weakness and paralysis score fell in the extract group. The outcome was not gait speed and the mice were not a Parkinson model.

fit: ground soybeans with levodopa and carbidopa
assessment: Acute crossover found longer on time and lower dyskinesia scores. Cooked edamame and rigidity were not isolated.

fit: sunflower oil vehicle with rat motor proxies
assessment: Injected sunflower oil served as vehicle in the rotenone design. No cold-pressed status, oral oil exposure or isolated oil effect was measured.

fit: sunflower food frequency and composite Parkinson symptom burden
assessment: The poster reports +2 total PRO-PD points per intake frequency category (95% CI −10 to 13, p=.787). The cross-sectional exposure did not specify an oil grade. It gives no individual rigidity estimate.

fit: sunflower oil original source context
assessment: PO2.161 lists refined sunflower oil in a mixed adolescent diet survey and gives no oil-specific IQ estimate. PO2.229 includes sunflower oil in a calorie-plus-probiotic menu and measures body composition.

fit: sunflower oil original source context
assessment: P169 appears in the complete PMC HTML for the oral record and separately in the printed poster supplement. The original oral PDF omits it. This is a duplicate sunflower capsule exposure family, with no separate oral-section result.

fit: sunflower oil original source context
assessment: P169 reports similarly measured sedentary time and steps for resistance-exercise groups with sunflower or fish oil capsules. The oil pressing grade is unspecified, no separate Parkinson outcome, and one comparison family with the duplicated HTML.

fit: sunflower oil in a sarcopenia comparison of strength and gait
assessment: Torque, gait and muscle area differ from rigidity. No Parkinson cohort, confirmed cold pressing or oil-free comparison.

fit: separate injected sunflower and saline controls for motor tests
assessment: The published Figures 5–8 give shared control significance letters on the marked behavioral comparisons. The abstract and methods conflict on saline route. A separate oil-only catalepsy estimate and dietary Parkinson rigidity outcome are unavailable.

fit: sunflower oil original source context
assessment: Study groups shared injected tamoxifen in sunflower oil. Gait and nonmotor tests include a buried-food olfaction task and operant sensation seeking, with no separate dietary oil comparison.

fit: sunflower oil original source context
assessment: The progressive dopaminergic-loss model used sunflower oil as a common injected tamoxifen carrier. Forebrain gene-expression outcomes concern subsequent L-DOPA and genotype.

fit: injected sunflower oil versus saline and rat catalepsy
assessment: Separate healthy control subgroups of four rats received sunflower oil or saline. The authors reported no clear difference in either bar or grid catalepsy, with no oral exposure, oil grade or clinical rigidity outcome.

fit: isolated eugenol and gait-related tasks in MPTP mice
assessment: Eugenol pretreatment improved narrow-beam crossing and post-treatment worsened it. The rodent task and constituent provide no estimate for ground allspice in people.

fit: seed extract and narrow-beam walking in a rat model
assessment: The author abstract reports better motor behavior on an assay set including narrow-beam walking. Gait-freezing episodes and grated nutmeg were unmeasured.

fit: pooled acidic fruit intake and incident urgency incontinence outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The adjusted comparison had a wide interval across both directions. Peach-specific exposure and urgency episode frequency were not analyzed.

fit: peach odor and a composite urinary score
assessment: The urinary domain association with identifying peach odor had q = .371. The model used no peach ingestion or separate urgency-frequency outcome.

fit: topical grapeseed oil mixture in Gua Sha and anxiety scores
assessment: Lower anxiety scores accompanied the bundled procedure. The trial did not test ingestion or determine the contribution or processing grade of the oil.

fit: isolated DHA compared with placebo for Parkinson levodopa-induced dyskinesia
assessment: Preliminary poster found 3/15 versus 7/15 cases by 12 months with no reported peak-severity difference. The posted forceplate denominator differs. Neither contrast estimates walnut oil or alpha-linolenic acid.

fit: cold-pressed walnut oil in a rotenone fly model
assessment: Oil with rotenone improved fly climbing compared with rotenone alone; the study does not measure human dyskinesia severity.

fit: saffron-containing three-extract formula and executive switching
assessment: After 12 weeks in older adults with mild cognitive impairment, reported switching difference was +1.42 points (95% CI -0.15 to 2.99) and contrast +1.56 (-0.09 to 3.20), with one-tailed p=.038 and .032. The 65 completers received a three-extract formula or placebo. No isolated dried saffron effect in Parkinson disease.

fit: powder tablet and general cognitive status
assessment: The global cognitive score favored saffron. Executive function was not isolated in the accessible report.

fit: dried aqueous saffron extract and specifically measured executive-related subtests
assessment: No significant randomized between-group working-memory or CPT reaction-time change. Formulation, adult Parkinson transfer, unblinded comparator and attrition limit scope.

fit: oral flaxseed oil and reported constipation adverse events in dyslipidemia
assessment: Table 5 reports 2 of 57 versus 5 of 55 with liquid paraffin. Small adverse reports do not give clinical severity. Pressing and Parkinson data remain unavailable.

fit: pure oral flaxseed oil compared with active oils in hemodialysis
assessment: Official NCT02103556 matches 50 patients, active mineral oil and Rome III. Flaxseed scores fell 9.6 to 6.0, with between-group interaction p=.15. Full article and thesis item values, grade and cohort overlaps remain open.

fit: oral solvent-extracted flaxseed oil and rodent wet stools
assessment: Wet feces increased at the two lower oil amounts but approached vehicle at the higher amount. The Methods document petroleum-ether extraction. No human symptom score or Parkinson cohort.

fit: plasma alpha-linolenic acid and Parkinson constipation score
assessment: The Wexner score showed no clear association with plasma alpha-linolenic acid. The cross-sectional analysis gives no estimate for cold-pressed flaxseed oil.

fit: enzymatic brown-rice protein hydrolysate and SPPB in older adults
assessment: SPPB total (p=.04) and chair stand (p=.02) favored active. Separate standing balance and cooked whole-brown-rice results are unavailable.

fit: germinated brown rice pretreatment and open-field ambulation and pole task after rotenone
assessment: Ambulation improved and mobility duration was inconclusive. Only the non-rice positive control showed clear improvement in both pole times. Rat motor assays and unresolved cooking method.

fit: cooked ground brown rice feed during iron exposure and fly climbing
assessment: Figure 2A reports better negative geotaxis than iron alone. The test is short-distance climbing in flies. Behavioral denominator differs across Methods and caption.

fit: brown rice after iron exposure and fly motor outcome
assessment: The primary abstract reports improved motor function after a different exposure schedule. Details of cooking and motor test remain unavailable. No patient, pull-test or postural instability estimate.

fit: chewed and swallowed named nigella seed and measured salivary pH
assessment: Salivary pH was higher after eating Nigella seed than after paraffin. No toasting method, salivary output measure, or severity of drooling in Parkinson disease was reported.

fit: oral oil gavage and salivary output after irradiation in mice
assessment: Oil-treated irradiated mice had more salivary output at day three than water-treated irradiated mice. The difference had resolved among survivors at day 60. The experiment did not test toasted seed or oral saliva leakage.

fit: cold-pressed oil rinse and reported saliva volume in healthy adults
assessment: Reported one-minute volume was 4.89 mL with cold-pressed oil and 1.43 mL with saline. Both rinse and saliva were collected, and the adjustment for retained rinse was unspecified. The fixed-order study gives no clinical drooling or toasted-seed result.

fit: summer savory extract and forced-swim immobility after stress
assessment: Higher dose shortened immobility in stressed rats. The outcome gives no clinical fatigue measure.

fit: savory extract and time moving after cisplatin
assessment: Intermediate extract dose attenuated cisplatin-related movement decline. The experiment gives no Parkinson fatigue estimate.

fit: cumin fruit extract in MPTP mice with motor task outcomes
assessment: The extract improved later balance and open-field tasks. Neither muscle tone nor an orally eaten toasted spice was assessed.

fit: multi-ingredient cumin formula and anthropometric measures
assessment: LBP4.128 reports anthropometric outcomes from a multi-ingredient cumin-containing formula. It does not isolate culinary cumin, its preparation or the frozen symptom.

fit: ground soybeans with levodopa and carbidopa
assessment: Acute crossover found longer on time and lower dyskinesia scores. Steamed edamame and olfaction were not isolated.

fit: chamuangone-enriched oil and drug-induced catalepsy
assessment: Catalepsy generally improved, with a higher low-dose mean at one early time point. The study lacks a plain rice bran oil arm and a human Parkinson rigidity estimate.

fit: hexane rice bran extract and rat catalepsy
assessment: Catalepsy and other motor outcomes improved after oral rice bran extract in rotenone rats. No refined rice bran oil or measured rigidity in people.

fit: oral tocotrienol isomers found in rice bran oil and rat paw retraction
assessment: Vitamin E alpha- and gamma-tocotrienols administered by gavage reduced forepaw retraction latency versus 6-OHDA alone on days 14–28 for both isomers (Figure 1). The material was approximately 97% pure, its oil origin was unspecified, and the test is an animal stiffness proxy. No refined rice bran oil or clinical rigidity estimate.

fit: rice bran oil placebo and aggregate motor ratings
assessment: The total MDS-UPDRS comparison was inconclusive. Rice bran oil was the placebo. There was no separate rigidity estimate or isolated rice bran oil comparison.

fit: fine ground bay leaf oral capsule without constipation endpoint
assessment: The four-arm trial documented the ingredient and adult oral preparation. Its endpoints were glucose and lipids, with no itemized constipation assessment.

fit: aqueous leaf extract and slower rat gastrointestinal transit
assessment: Injected extract slowed a charcoal meal and separate tests found antidiarrheal effects. These disease and route differences leave clinical constipation unresolved.

fit: ground bay leaf powder in oral cookies with short digestive assessment
assessment: Participants reported no digestive discomfort in the two-hour crossover. This does not address constipation severity or Parkinson.

fit: human extract tablets and constipation questionnaire
assessment: Median constipation scores fell from 2.0 to 1.0 (P=.021) in the extract arm and from 2.0 to 1.5 (P=.086) in placebo. Table 11 gives tests within each arm without a between-arm test or effect estimate. The trial enrolled healthy adults and used an extract tablet.

fit: food-related material in an imaging report
assessment: The original MR colonography study places excised pig colon specimens in soybean oil for imaging. This is a nonoral laboratory medium with no dose, grade or Parkinson symptom comparison.

fit: dystonia presentation before a systemic soybean-oil emulsion in a mitochondrial disorder
assessment: The Leigh syndrome case names dystonia and describes general response to an intravenous soybean-oil emulsion. Available text gives no dystonia-specific post-exposure finding, culinary refined preparation, or Parkinson disease.

fit: oral refined peanut oil and oral allergy symptoms
assessment: No allergic reactions occurred after refined oil in 60 peanut-allergic participants. Crude oil caused oral or throat itching, wheeze or swelling in six. Drooling and Parkinson disease were not measured.

fit: oral pumpkin seed oil added to tadalafil in chronic pelvic pain
assessment: The abstract reports an advantage only in the pain domain, while overall improvement was 11 of 25 with the oil combination versus 12 of 25 with tadalafil. Exact domain data and oil processing remain open.

fit: solvent-extracted pumpkin seed oil and evoked mouse pain
assessment: Hot-plate latency increased and chemical writhing decreased. These measures ran opposite to the worsening hypothesis in a non-Parkinson model using solvent-extracted oil.

fit: cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil combined with Solcoseryl for cancer-treatment oral mucositis
assessment: The matching 2024 paper reports lower aggregate PROMS with a topical combination containing 10% cold-pressed oil versus benzydamine. A mouth-pain item is part of the scale and was not reported separately. Solcoseryl and the adverse comparator prevent isolated attribution.

fit: registered one-arm oral Cucurbita pepo oil pilot and pelvic pain/urgency composite
assessment: Manufacturer describes the named product as cold pressed. The registry records completion and 40 enrolled with no posted results. The composite is broader than pain alone and no Parkinson or oil-free comparison was assigned.

fit: local pumpkin seed oil ultrasound and measured prostatitis pain
assessment: Mean pain fell 13.49 points with oil-coupled ultrasound and 12.59 with active ultrasound. The table supplies no pain-specific pairwise uncertainty. Local exposure and pelvic pain do not estimate clinical Parkinson effects of ingested cold-pressed oil.

fit: oral pumpkin seed oil and menopause-related joint pain
assessment: Joint-pain median fell from two to one in the oil arm, with no clear 12-week endpoint difference versus wheat germ oil. The processing method and Parkinson pain were untested.

fit: Parkinson diet-adherence whole nut item and planned swallowing outcome
assessment: The diet promotes olive oil and lists whole hazelnuts on the adherence tool. The planned nutrition-related motor item numbering and scoring differ from the original MDS-UPDRS. The official record displays Recruiting with an elapsed estimated completion and no posted results. No toasted hazelnut oil was assigned.

fit: whole roasted hazelnut and oral allergy reactions
assessment: Five of 17 raw-hazelnut-allergic participants reacted to the whole roasted nut challenge. This acute allergy outcome does not establish the effect of toasted hazelnut oil on swallowing in Parkinson disease.

fit: whole hazelnut challenge and swallowing symptom checklist
assessment: Difficulty swallowing was a subjective criterion in the clinical challenge study. The available report provides no specific swallowing estimate after toasted hazelnut oil and enrolled adults with suspected allergy.

fit: compound hazelnut-oil gargle and ex vivo tongue wetting
assessment: The combination increased liquid retention and reduced tongue adhesiveness in an ex vivo model. No swallowing function, oral intake or verified toasted oil was tested.

fit: Mixed berry allergy and throat edema in one case
assessment: Positive skin tests and acute throat swelling were reported after mixed berry intake. No oral challenge, freezing history, Parkinson cohort or loudness result was available. Plausibly overlaps 1999 same-author case.

fit: Recalled fruit-jam use for sore throat
assessment: Vouchered Rubus ulmifolius fruit jam drew six hill-area mentions for sore throat. Reported use and traditional belief provide no response measurement, freezing information or Parkinson voice outcome.

fit: Parkinsonism berry-frequency item with distinct self-rated speech endpoint
assessment: The MIND questionnaire pooled berry species and preparations; adjusted berry frequency association was for total PRO-PD. The presence of a speech slider elsewhere in the dataset does not supply that contrast.

fit: Throat irritation after boysenberry–apple powder in healthy adults
assessment: Throat irritation favored the mixed product in the journal abstract (p=0.04). A chemically provoked airway symptom in this sample does not supply a comparison of sound pressure levels or whole frozen blackberry.

fit: blackberry flower-bud assay and traditional external hoarseness context
assessment: The original proceedings study measures antioxidant assays with flower-bud preparations. It describes traditional external hoarseness use without a measured voice or oral berry comparison.

fit: Buccal exposure to freeze-dried blackberry powder in crossover
assessment: The gum trial used blackberry powder with a xylitol comparator. Researchers measured saliva and enamel bacteria. Journal and registry quantities differ. No speech, laryngeal or Parkinson endpoint is reported.

fit: PD intake questionnaire with recovered questions on berries and frozen meals
assessment: The official questionnaire records seven-day cups of unspecified berries and a separate count of frozen or ready-made meals. It does not identify blackberry, preparation of berries or voice volume.

fit: Caregiver or child report of talking as part of a function score
assessment: Seven-item function sum p=0.05 without an item-level talking or acoustic outcome in the body or supplements. Children had acute respiratory infection and received a prepared boysenberry–apple blend versus a heat-treated comparison.

fit: Black pepper leaf tea versus chamomile in adults with insomnia
assessment: The comparison used leaf tea rather than ground peppercorns, and insomnia severity and overall sleep quality rather than dream-enactment episodes; no Parkinson subgroup was reported.

fit: black pepper essential oil facial cream versus unscented cream and home sleep staging
assessment: Thirty-two healthy adults used 0.0025% pepper oil or control at bedtime. Mean REM duration was 75.8 versus 72.4 min and no significant sleep differences were reported. There was no ground pepper ingestion or dream-enactment outcome.

fit: Black-pepper-fruit-containing multi-botanical oral formula in adults with chronic insomnia
assessment: Multi-herb formula and sleep-quality composite cannot isolate pepper or estimate dream-enactment frequency; no Parkinson subgroup was identified.

fit: Oral black-pepper extract and EEG/EMG sleep staging in caffeine-exposed mice
assessment: No significant REM-duration difference was reported, but REM duration and bouts do not measure dream-enactment frequency; extract and mouse model differ from culinary ground pepper in Parkinson disease.

fit: low
assessment: A case linked aniseed liqueur consumption with episodic tongue swelling and difficulty swallowing and breathing. IgE studies support seed sensitization. This is an allergy-related oral symptom, without a speech intelligibility measure or ground-seed Parkinson comparison.

fit: perimenopausal fatigue after standardized saffron extract
assessment: Preprint reports POMS fatigue changes of minus 7.6 and minus 1.7 points; interaction p=.0003. Different formulation, scale and clinical population limit transfer.

fit: multicomponent saffron beverage and fatigue in multiple sclerosis
assessment: The endpoint difference favored a saffron, rose water and sugar beverage. It does not isolate saffron or report outcomes in Parkinson disease.

fit: standardized saffron extract and fatigue in subclinical low mood
assessment: The fatigue interaction was inconclusive. The intervention was a standardized extract and the participants did not have Parkinson disease.

fit: dry saffron extract and fatigue in COPD
assessment: The trial reports a repeated-measures difference favoring saffron on the COPD fatigue scale. The diagnosis and standardized extract differ from the frozen claim.

fit: dry saffron extract and fatigue in pulmonary sarcoidosis
assessment: At day 60 fatigue favored extract plus counseling over counseling alone. The population and preparation differ, and the control did not take a placebo capsule.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: P-15-013 assays hydromethanolic Crocus sativus tepal extracts and performs molecular docking. The floral waste preparation differs from ground stigma, and no symptom was measured.

fit: dried stigma powder in tablets and matching fatigue outcome
assessment: Fatigue scores favored saffron in the randomized Parkinson trial. The original registration omitted the standalone fatigue scale, and the first archived revision listing the scale follows manuscript receipt. The tablet regimen and outcome chronology limit transfer and confidence.

fit: isolated piperine plus levodopa and rat movement composite
assessment: The axial dystonia assessment was included in a total abnormal involuntary movement score, without a separate dystonia estimate. The model intervention used isolated piperine with levodopa.

fit: topical grapeseed comparator and sleep duration
assessment: Two-week wrist application showed no clear lavender-versus-grapeseed differences in tracker-derived total, light or deep sleep. There was no oral or untreated comparison, and insomnia severity was unreported.

fit: oral grapeseed oil cookie and registered sleep questionnaire
assessment: The oral cookie comparison registered correlations of blood linoleic acid with questionnaire sleep. The published reports do not provide those estimates. No Parkinson participants or insomnia endpoint were identified.

fit: nonoral grapeseed comparison and registered hospital sleep outcomes
assessment: Grapeseed oil on gauze was compared with lavender and usual care for planned hospital sleep quality and duration. The terminated study has no posted outcome estimates.

fit: oral grapeseed oil cookie and registered sleep quality
assessment: The healthy-adult pilot plans a correlation involving global sleep quality after an oral grapeseed oil cookie. No results are posted, and the study does not measure Parkinson insomnia severity.

fit: high-linoleic cookie and registered insomnia severity
assessment: The single-arm study plans an Insomnia Severity Index, actigraphy and EEG in adults with insomnia symptoms. The oil is unnamed. It is not yet recruiting and no results are posted.

fit: oral essential oil and measured whole stomach emptying
assessment: Nonsignificant gastric results across baseline and both drug contexts differ from the detected intestinal inhibition. The tested oil had no levodopa or clinical fluctuations arm.

fit: oral fruit tea and clinical postoperative bowel recovery
assessment: An earlier return of flatus and bowel movements cannot distinguish gastric emptying or levodopa wearing-off.

fit: fennel oil and anethole in drug delayed emptying
assessment: The oil and compound improved experimentally delayed emptying in mice. A normal-baseline anethole comparison did not indicate acceleration. No oral toasted seed or levodopa arm.

fit: oral extract and loperamide delayed stomach emptying
assessment: Reduced retention in drug-challenged mice is a relevant mechanistic lead. Whole seeds, levodopa and clinical daily OFF time remain unmeasured.

fit: fennel seed infusion on excised stomach muscle
assessment: Proximal relaxation and increased antral amplitude establish distinct regional muscle effects. The protocol cannot estimate whole-stomach emptying or clinical OFF time.

fit: registered external fennel and postoperative ileus
assessment: Topical heated fennel and planned ileus outcomes do not estimate oral exposure or Parkinson OFF time. Registry results are absent.

fit: peanut oil as injected carrier in a primate parkinsonism model

fit: anise extract and exploratory habituation

fit: anxiety-related behavior after a high-fat prenatal canola diet

fit: whole tarragon essential oil and abnormal gait during mouse toxicity observations

fit: fatigue and a branded capsule with uncertain study-era oil content

fit: oral avocado oil plus mint comparator and measured daytime sleepiness

fit: seed capsules and anosmia prevalence during COVID-19

assessment: There was no preparation-specific estimate on postural instability.

fit: bioprocessed oat bran/chickpea intervention and planned single-leg stance
