fit: Parkinson dietary intervention lists rosemary and UPDRS III includes rest tremor
assessment: Ingredient freshness, amount and individual intake are unreported; only composite motor scores for a multi-food diet are given, not a dried rosemary or rest-tremor comparison.

fit: depleted Syrian oregano stems in a bay leaf trial comparator
assessment: The 25-person Origanum syriacum stem comparator changed from 50.32 to 50.76 on the paper's STAI measure (reported p=.8846). The study compared it with bay leaf and did not include a no-oregano comparator. Species, plant part, depletion and population limit transfer to culinary dried oregano in Parkinson disease.

fit: reported oregano use and global nonmotor measures in a Parkinson cohort
assessment: Section 3.5 reports exploratory corrected analyses using HADS total and NMSS. No oregano-specific HADS anxiety estimate, preparation or amount was reported. Table 4 p=.506 compares exposure across ethnic groups.

fit: injected oregano extract and open-maze behavior in rats
assessment: Open-arm entries and time increased, while locomotor activity declined. Preparation, route and behavioral endpoints differ from clinical anxiety after dried oregano.

fit: forehead Origanum vulgare oil exposure and depression scales
assessment: Mean depression scores declined in a 200-person paired analysis without a concurrent control. Anxiety estimates, oral dried leaves and Parkinson status were outside the reported comparison.

fit: topical marjoram-containing blend and HADS anxiety in rheumatoid arthritis
assessment: HADS favored blended massage over usual care. No clear direct difference from almond-oil massage. The earlier and later reports belong to one trial. Matched effect estimates remain inaccessible.

fit: oral six-spice capsule with broad mental health outcome
assessment: The trial plans SF-36 mental health and excludes Parkinson disease. There are no posted outcomes and oregano is one of six ingredients.

fit: topical marjoram compared with carrier massage and planned GAD-7 after stroke
assessment: The completed pilot plans GAD-7 and PHQ-9 and supplies no posted outcomes. It uses sweet marjoram in a topical carrier and involves stroke survivors.

fit: marjoram tea oxidative biomarkers and published registry date discrepancy
assessment: The later report and official registry differ on the dates of conduct. Outcomes are biochemical and no clinical anxiety result is supplied. Participant overlap with the earlier symptom study is unverified.

fit: oral isolated carvacrol and mouse maze behavior
assessment: Abstract reports more open-arm exploration and inconclusive locomotor and sleep assays. Related thesis corroborates the model and route and disagrees on one sample size. Neither source tested a culinary herb.

fit: injected oregano leaf extract and mouse light–dark behavior
assessment: 60 mg/kg injection increased time in light by 35% (p = .046). Oral dosing tested a different behavior. Neither establishes the symptom after oral dried oregano.

fit: injected synthetic carvacryl acetate and mouse anxiety-like assays
assessment: The original Results report more open-arm behavior and fewer marbles buried. The abstract says more marbles were buried; Figure 4 remains visually unverified. This is a synthetic derivative and no culinary comparison was given.

fit: injected beta-caryophyllene and acute mouse behavior
assessment: More open-arm time and less immobility in behavioral tests followed injection of isolated beta-caryophyllene. This does not establish a clinical outcome from the food preparation.

fit: isolated carvacrol and safety measures outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The original abstract reports labs and pulmonary measures, without an anxiety analysis. A likely related 2019 paper names a registration and excludes psychiatric disorders. Full safety tables remain open.

fit: strained marjoram tea and total nonmotor and depressive outcomes in Parkinson disease
assessment: Among 51 completers, total NMSS and BDI declined within the tea group. The accessible data lack anxiety-specific outcomes and the dried marjoram was strained as an infusion.

fit: oral oregano extract and anxiety-related behavior in chronically stressed rats
assessment: Maze and open-field measures ran opposite to the worsening hypothesis in this model. The exposure was an extract and the experiment did not measure anxiety in Parkinson disease.

fit: oregano leaf hexane extract and rat anxiety-like behavior in hepatic encephalopathy
assessment: The extract attenuated anxiety-like changes in the toxicant model, which differs from the frozen preparation and disease.

fit: dried ground oregano in healthy soldiers and exercise blood biomarkers
assessment: The 500 mg dried plant capsule is close to the named preparation. In 24 healthy soldiers, creatine kinase was lower than starch at 60 and 120 minutes (both p < 0.0001). The study measured no anxiety or patient fatigue scale and did not specify plant part. No symptom direction transfers.

fit: inhaled marjoram oil and human state anxiety
assessment: No significant between-arm difference in state anxiety or anxiety VAS. Species, route and population differ.

fit: five-herb oral extract and locomotor-confounded rat behavior
assessment: The high-volume mixture gave more open-arm entries (p<.05) but inconclusive open-arm duration (p>.05). Activity also increased. No single-herb contrast or clinical endpoint.

fit: dried oregano leaf infusion and motor-confounded mouse exploration
assessment: Leaf infusion reduced mouse hole exploration at 750 and 1000 mg/kg; the higher dose also impaired motor coordination in rotarod and chimney tasks. Sedation or motor impairment confounds behavioral interpretation, and no clinical anxiety was measured.

fit: pomegranate formulation and adverse-event time ordering after stroke
assessment: A psychiatric event with auditory hallucinations is reported in one of eight assigned POMx. It began before the first administration. No visual-hallucination outcome, raw arils or Parkinson group.

fit: nanoemulsified pomegranate seed oil and planned Parkinson hallucinations measure
assessment: The planned NMSS covers hallucinations and combines frequency with severity. No item-level data or outcomes publication were verified. The intervention is a nanoformulated oil capsule.

fit: aquatic fennel oil and immobility in scopolamine zebrafish
assessment: Fennel oil did not clearly change immobility duration in the novel tank assay. The outcome was swimming immobility in a scopolamine cognitive impairment model, without gait, oral seed or Parkinson measurements.

fit: aqueous fennel fruit extract and locomotor tasks in an MPTP model
assessment: The conference abstract reports improvement across open-field, rotarod and passive-avoidance results without endpoint estimates. No freezing episodes or toasted seed ingestion were reported.

fit: oral fennel essence and locomotion in reserpine rats
assessment: The oil plus reserpine group III had an open-field mean of 332.17 versus 4.25 in reserpine-only group II. The previous 32.50 came from levodopa/carbidopa group IV. This is a descriptive locomotor comparison without a freezing measure or toasted seeds.

fit: fennel seed in shared Parkinson diet and composite motor examination
assessment: Appendix A lists fennel seed in a two-week diet offered to both intervention groups. The one-year composite UPDRS III result gives no separate freezing episodes or isolated toasted fennel exposure.

fit: fennel seed methanolic extract and motor coordination in 6-OHDA rats
assessment: Peri-lesion gavage improved rotarod and wire-grasp outcomes at day 14 (p < .05), while the course started after the lesion had no clear effect. These tests did not track freezing episodes and the extract was not toasted seed.

fit: culinary sumac extract against bacterial urinary isolates
assessment: Laboratory inhibition of urinary bacterial isolates supplies no participant-level urgency data.

fit: fragrant sumac bark pumpkin oil and hop trial with planned urgency diary
assessment: Only seven active and two placebo participants received treatment. Early termination left urgency efficacy analysis unreported. The 2019 uncontrolled report is a separate cohort and the bark differs from culinary ground fruit.

fit: fragrant sumach bark in an overactive bladder combination
assessment: Urination frequency changed in a noninterventional study of a mixture containing a different Rhus species and bark.

fit: injected sumac extract and mouse open-field activity
assessment: No significant open-field activity change was reported. The assay did not measure shortened stride.

fit: sumac fruit drink during exercise in healthy volunteers
assessment: Pain during an exercise program was measured without instrumented stride assessment.

fit: sumac fruit fractions in stressed muscle cells and zebrafish embryos
assessment: The muscle progenitor and embryo experiments did not measure limb gait or stride.

fit: single-blind oral flax oil pain comparison in osteoarthritis
assessment: Rest and movement pain favored oral flaxseed oil. The paper gives inconsistent dosing and no grade, and possible overlap with the investigators’ later positive report is unresolved.

fit: combined flaxseed-derived omega-3 and vitamin E with Parkinson total score
assessment: The randomized combination improved the published total score. The primary report gives no pain item result, verified cold-pressing method or oil-only effect.

fit: flaxseed-derived omega-3 plus vitamin E
assessment: The combination trial assessed overall UPDRS and biomarkers. No separate cold-pressed oil pain effect was reported.

fit: oral flaxseed oil versus vitamin E and mastalgia
assessment: Both improved, with inconclusive between-arm pain comparison p=.142. No placebo or specified oil grade.

fit: oral flaxseed versus corn oil and ACL pain
assessment: At two years KOOS pain was 87.6 vs 87.3 (p=.96). Function measures are distinct from the pain subscale.

fit: pelvic pain trial with unresolved seed, oil and dried extract terminology
assessment: The report describes lower pain, but its own methods specify dried ethanol extract and the registry alternates oil and flaxseed. Actual oil formulation is unconfirmed.

fit: flaxseed oil plus vitamin D and SF-36 pain in type 2 diabetes
assessment: Table 7 gives large baseline differences and unclear change and significance labels. The abstract reports improved pain, but the result cannot isolate flaxseed oil or give a clear directional contrast.

fit: flax oil versus linoleic acid preparation in rheumatoid arthritis
assessment: Original abstract gives an inconclusive 22-person clinical comparison including pain measures. Arm values and grade are unavailable.

fit: single-blind oral flax oil pain comparison in rheumatoid arthritis
assessment: Both rest and movement pain favored oil, reported p<.001. Grade and dose are unclear and several numbers are inconsistent. The same investigators’ other report is not assumed independent.

fit: ground cayenne served in a controlled breakfast without target clinical measurements
assessment: The same-accession thesis names cayenne powder and compares metabolic outcomes in healthy adults. Fixed meal order conflicts with registered random allocation. Dyskinesia was unmeasured.

fit: levodopa dyskinesia and a TRPV1 antagonist combination in rats
assessment: URB597 plus capsazepine reduced graded abnormal movements. The protocol did not administer capsaicin or cayenne. Isolated capsaicin in the related Lee report measured different hyperactivity outcomes.

fit: capsaicin as a receptor probe in a dyskinesia mouse model
assessment: Capsaicin blocked the reduction in dyskinetic movements associated with a separate experimental agent. The study did not test ground cayenne consumption.

fit: optional spinach intake and objective postpartum attention
assessment: Spinach entries were documented in both intervention groups and the MANT accuracy interaction was significant. The intervention varied a bundle of foods without a cooking or spinach-specific contrast.

fit: low
assessment: Mouse pretreatment with spinach ethanol extract or separate linoleic acid improved working and aversive memory measures in a trimethyltin model. The article gives no cooked-spinach comparison or dedicated Parkinson attention result.

fit: thawed spinach and direct attention tests in healthy people
assessment: Power of attention and continuity of attention comparisons were inconclusive (p=.70 and .84). A cooked preparation and Parkinson’s were not verified.

fit: red spinach extract and Stroop outcomes in resistance-trained men
assessment: The crossover found no clear Stroop difference. The product was an extract and is distinct from cooked common spinach in Parkinson disease.

fit: formulated curcumin and 400-meter walking speed
assessment: Posted change +.014 vs +.103 m/s, n=9 and n=8, without a posted between-group test. Parkinson excluded.

fit: curcumin extract alongside a weight-loss diet in PCOS
assessment: No separate Parkinson symptom or culinary turmeric result was recorded. Within-group metabolic changes do not establish a between-group clinical response.

fit: turmeric-colored bread and child sensory preference
assessment: Children chose yellow bread less often. The study concerns colour and liking, without a swallowing or other relevant clinical endpoint.

fit: turmeric rhizome extract without boswellia and 40-meter fast gait
assessment: Extract speed change +.08 versus +.01 m/s, marked p<.05. A separate intergroup number conflicts, and clinical sample had knee osteoarthritis.

fit: lipid curcumin and four-meter speed
assessment: Four-meter gait speed group-by-time p=.9 and six-minute distance p=.6. Healthy adults and formulated curcumin.

fit: combined turmeric and tamarind extracts and walking speed
assessment: Changes favored the two mixtures over placebo. No turmeric-only effect.

fit: water-dispersible turmeric extract and 80-meter walk time
assessment: Mean time change −11.0 vs −6.8 seconds; median −.2 vs 0 and reported Mann–Whitney p=.0011. Chronic knee pain and formulation limit transfer.

fit: Curcugen and walk tests in osteoarthritis
assessment: 40-meter walking p=.604; 6-minute endurance difference p=.013 in Table 4. The narrative gives a different p value.

fit: oral curcumin and levodopa combination and open-field speed
assessment: Open-field speed differed for the combination versus rotenone. The reported pairwise tests gave no clear speed effect of curcumin alone.

fit: curcumin formulation and six-minute walk with or without exercise
assessment: Matched exercise comparisons favor formulation. Both nonexercise arms decline by 4 m after rounding despite adjusted p=.002 and substantial baseline imbalance.

fit: historical oral lovage root use for pain and a separate leaf tea use
assessment: Two interview reports describe root decoction for joint pain and two leaf tea for inflammation. No dried-leaf pain response, comparator, or Parkinson diagnosis is reported.

fit: isolated pulverized lovage root and mechanical nociception in rats
assessment: The root arm reduced mechanical nociception versus vehicle. Species matches, while organ and clinical pain context differ.

fit: dried lovage leaves in in vitro enzyme comparisons
assessment: Dried leaf extracts altered inflammatory enzyme inhibition after simulated digestion. Neither animals nor patients had pain assessed.

fit: pooled legume or bean intake and whole-diet daytime sleepiness scores
assessment: Table 2 reports daytime sleepiness against whole diet scores. Table S4 evaluates pooled bean or legume intake against aggregate symptom burden and does not identify species or preparation.

fit: mixed evening meal with lentils and next-morning Epworth sleepiness
assessment: The 20-participant comparison found no clear Epworth difference (p=.45). Ingredients and calories changed together, and canned lentil and Parkinson effects were unmeasured.

fit: brewed spearmint crossover and subjective smell in nasal polyposis
assessment: High and low rosmarinic acid teas showed no diary smell difference. The comparison used two active teas in a non-Parkinson population.

fit: mint scent in a bundled olfactory training protocol
assessment: The protocol uses a mint label and conventional menthol stimulus among four odorants. The population has olfactory dysfunction and subjective cognitive decline. There is no independent mint arm, established culinary spearmint species or brewed preparation.

fit: spearmint test odor in Parkinson and drug induced parkinsonism
assessment: The original reports less accurate spearmint odor recognition in 78 Parkinson participants versus 31 with drug-induced parkinsonism. The groups differed by age. The ingredient served as a test odor, with no brewed ingestion or treatment contrast.

fit: fresh and convectively dried red cabbage extracts and fibril-exposed cells
assessment: Extracts reduced alpha-synuclein-fibril-associated cytotoxicity in SH-SY5Y cells under some drying and exposure conditions. The study tested no cooked food intake or rigidity outcome.

fit: oral red cabbage anthocyanin preparations and behavior in aging mice
assessment: The paper reports no motor effect, but the available abstract does not identify a rigidity measure.

fit: asparagus in a tube complication
assessment: The case trail concerns a feeding tube complication. The accessible material gives no drooling estimate for steamed asparagus.

fit: asparagus oral liquid with mecobalamin and reported unstimulated saliva
assessment: A later systematic review extracts a positive salivary-flow comparison in 28 burning-mouth patients with high risk of bias. The original body is unavailable, and drooling, steamed food and Parkinson effects are unverified.

fit: clove oil odor detection during an oxytocin crossover
assessment: Clove oil was a detection probe in a schizophrenia study of oxytocin. The abstract reports no clear clove threshold change. The later journal report has no clove threshold. Neither route nor endpoint matches the frozen culinary comparison.

fit: standardized clove oil with rice bran oil and self reported cognitive failures
assessment: Cognitive Failures Questionnaire scores moved from 39 to 27 in the higher-dose arm (within p≤.005). The randomized design has two active doses and no placebo. Participants did not have Parkinson and the study does not isolate ground clove or objectively measured executive change.

fit: clove scent within four odorants and Trail Making cognition assessment
assessment: Journal protocol verifies intended Trail Making assessments and bundled odors, including eugenol for clove in conventional training. No isolated clove intake or clinical Parkinson results are reported.

fit: clove odor kit and Trail Making Test B in an HIV protocol
assessment: The recruiting study lists a conventional odor kit that includes clove and a cognitive task measuring executive performance. Results are not posted. The intervention bundles odors and has no identified ingested ground-clove or Parkinson arm.

fit: isolated inhaled eugenol and healthy-volunteer executive inhibition
assessment: Twenty-five healthy volunteers performed manual Stroop tasks. Eugenol versus air was not associated with a detected change in reaction times. The study did not test culinary clove or Parkinson executive function.

fit: clove as one of six odorants in a diabetes cognition training trial
assessment: The original abstract reports MoCA change +1.9 versus +0.4 (p=.001) and executive-domain gains with the training package. Exact executive estimates remain open. Clove is one inhaled stimulus and the participants had diabetes with mild cognitive impairment.

fit: eugenol in multi-odorant training and composite cognition
assessment: General cognition favored training. The study did not isolate ingested clove or executive function.

fit: acute food overdose and subjective dry mouth
assessment: The patient reported xerostomia after accidental excess ingestion. Drooling and saliva flow were not measured.

fit: acute loss of speaking ability after kernel anaphylaxis with prior topical oil use
assessment: A child was unable to speak after chewing and spitting out a macadamia kernel. The prior oil exposure was topical. The report does not measure speech intelligibility or establish an oral oil effect in Parkinson disease.

fit: oral macadamia oil and postmeal sleepiness in healthy adults
assessment: The 2025 study family reports less acute postmeal sleepiness and fatigue with macadamia oil. The companion figures report a trend for sleepiness at 30 minutes in the larger experiment. Prior-night sleep timing and daytime ratings do not measure REM dream enactment. The oil pressing method is unknown.

fit: spearmint extract and sensor hits or reaction time
assessment: These outcomes are indirect motor measures. There was no clinical hand dexterity scale or Parkinson population.

fit: mint leaves named in a Parkinson diet with hand tasks in its motor scale
assessment: Species and preparation were unspecified. No isolated mint exposure or item-level dexterity estimate was reported.

fit: oral summer savory oil and rotarod balance after lead
assessment: Improved retention on a rotating rod does not count clinical falls.

fit: aqueous oral Sichuan pepper preparation in MPTP mouse model
assessment: Example 1 reports shorter pole-task times at three decoction levels. Exposure began before model induction. This offers a species-specific motor proxy with no toasted culinary exposure or clinical bradykinesia comparison.

fit: related pepper species and animal movement-speed proxy
assessment: Distilled Japanese pepper given intranasally shortened pole descent in mice. It did not test culinary Sichuan pepper in humans.

fit: optional walnut oil and planned depression scale in a non-Parkinson trial
assessment: The program offered walnut oil as a dietary option. The protocol prespecified a geriatric depression scale. Public results material supplies neither the depression comparison nor participant-specific intake, processing grade or oil allocation.

fit: mixed-nut Mediterranean diet and onset of depression in cardiovascular-risk adults
assessment: PREDIMED 2013 incident depression adjusted HR was 0.78 (95% CI 0.55 to 1.10), with a diabetes subgroup estimate of 0.59 (0.36 to 0.98). The trial supplied whole mixed nuts and a diet pattern; prevention of diagnosis is distinct from symptom severity.

fit: whole-walnut bread and depression-dejection subscale in healthy students
assessment: Mean POMS Depression-Dejection scores were 9.7 with walnuts and 12.1 with control (n=49, p=.103). Sex subgroups and overall depression comparison were inconclusive; male total mood is a separate endpoint. Whole ground nuts in bread differ from cold-pressed oil.

fit: walnut-oil milkshake and fear extinction in young adults
assessment: The author abstract reports faster extinction of learned fear. The secondary acute Total Mood Disturbance difference was -4.99 (95% CI -10.75 to +0.07). The recovered supplement has no POMS component scores, and the original body, clinical symptom measure and oil processing remain open.

fit: avocado and soybean unsaponifiables in a probable aspiration case
assessment: An older adult with severe reflux and hiatal hernia developed lipoid pneumonia during long-term oral use. The case does not isolate avocado oil or measure clinical swallowing difficulty in Parkinson disease.

fit: Confirmed frozen dill product contamination notice without patient data
assessment: The recall is for a microbiological contaminant and supplies no patient exposures or symptoms. It cannot establish hallucinations, their frequency, or an effect of fresh foliage.

fit: Dill fruit survey and literature-based toxicity attribution
assessment: The individual fruit row does not report hallucinations. The grouping of toxic plants in prose cannot establish a hallucination case or incidence attributable to fresh dill.

fit: dried Perilla leaves processed into aqueous extract and used in an ocular accommodation trial
assessment: Binocular near-point distances changed from 7.96 to 7.27 cm versus 9.00 to 9.67 with placebo. The article inconsistently reports sample size and has no Parkinson fatigue measure. NCT02641470 identifies another plant study.

fit: perilla leaf flavonoid extract and exercise endurance in adolescents
assessment: The abstract reports longer exhaustion time in male track athletes. It provides no clinical fatigue score, Parkinson population or culinary dried-leaf exposure.

fit: mixed oral formula with unresolved perilla and prospective fatigue items
assessment: Registry says 10 g/day and includes perilla. The linked protocol says 30 g/day and omits perilla from Table 1. Termination and absent results leave fatigue effects and actual formulation unresolved.

fit: oral dried summer savory powder and knee osteoarthritis pain
assessment: Of 60 randomized participants, 39 were analyzed. The between-group pain change was inconclusive (p=.38). This used dried powder and measured osteoarthritis pain.

fit: topical summer savory gel and chemotherapy-induced mucositis pain in children
assessment: Sixty children were analyzed. Pain fell faster with the extract gel plus routine treatment than with placebo gel plus routine treatment. This measured local mucositis pain after topical gel.

fit: summer savory extracts or oil and evoked pain in rodents
assessment: Formalin scores improved with all preparations and writhing with some. The tail-flick test gave negative results. Fresh leaves and Parkinson pain were not tested.

fit: summer savory seed fractions and evoked mouse nociception
assessment: Hajhashemi, Zolfaghari and Yousefi compared summer savory seed oil and two seed extracts in mouse experiments. All three preparations reduced acetic-acid-induced abdominal responses (p < .001). Oil and polyphenolic extract affected the late formalin phase, while the hydroalcoholic extract affected both phases. The study varied administration route across preparations and tested seed fractions, not fresh leaves. The rodent outcomes provide indirect context for claim 0659.

fit: isolated carvacrol and evoked thermal hyperalgesia in Parkinson rats
assessment: Haddadi and colleagues tested isolated carvacrol in a 6-hydroxydopamine-lesioned rat model. The higher tested condition improved passive-avoidance memory. The original report found no clear effect on tail-withdrawal hyperalgesia or rotations. This is a competing model result for 0659. It concerns an isolated constituent and evoked thermal responses.

fit: cocoa in rice beverage
assessment: The pilot tested fatigability and left its effect uncertain. It supplies no speech outcome estimate.

fit: mixed vegetables and device adverse event
assessment: The case describes a bezoar with a jejunal tube. Parkinson symptom severity was reported stable.

fit: pooled leek and spinach intake in a Parkinson cohort
assessment: The single weekly leafy-green category cannot identify roasted leek or estimate effects on clinical rigidity.

fit: culinary seasonings in a constipation case
assessment: Multiple dietary and other interventions leave the contribution of the individual seasoning unresolved.

fit: dried basil powder trial and adverse-event scope
assessment: Adverse effects do not give a constipation score or bowel-frequency estimate.

fit: hairy basil seed and stool outcomes
assessment: Thirty adults in a one-group study reported more frequent and softer stool after seven days of soaked hairy basil seed. Gastrointestinal adverse effects were reported. This was seed from a differently identified herb, with no Parkinson comparison.

fit: pooled non-fried fish and self-rated Parkinson anxiety
assessment: Inverse baseline graphical association. Species, cooking method, numeric coefficient and uncertainty not given.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: T1:PO.58 assigns a hypocaloric fish menu allowing salmon, anchovy, tuna or sardine to assess inflammatory markers. A different poster has an author named Salmon. The fish comparison has no preparation-specific Parkinson anxiety outcome.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: PO2.001 and PO2.006 have matching salmon/veal meal comparisons and distinct thermogenesis and appetite results. No isolated poached salmon and anxiety estimate.

fit: salmon melanin-concentrating hormone in a receptor assay
assessment: The species-derived peptide elicited calcium mobilization in a laboratory assay with a cloned porcine receptor. Poached salmon intake and anxiety were outside the study.

fit: salmon meals plus fish-oil supplement
assessment: The before-and-after study reports lipid and inflammatory markers after a combined intervention. It cannot identify a separate dietary salmon or anxiety effect.

fit: fatty fish advice including salmon and Derogatis anxiety in angina
assessment: Advice with optional fish-oil substitution gave an adjusted anxiety difference of +0.82 (95% CI −0.57 to 2.22). The study reported no separate salmon or cooking contrast.

fit: oily fish including salmon and antenatal anxiety
assessment: Lower combined oily-fish frequency was associated with higher odds of antenatal anxiety. The questionnaire grouped species and the outcome was in a pregnancy cohort.

fit: grilled or boiled Atlantic salmon and STAI state and trait in forensic inpatients
assessment: State anxiety improved in the salmon arm relative to control over time, p = .043; trait anxiety gave no reported significant result. Preparation was pooled and there was no Parkinson-specific estimate. Sleep paper PMID 24812543 describes the same trial.

fit: mixed oily fish including salmon and SDQ emotional symptoms in adolescents
assessment: The full school sample showed no clear change in SDQ emotional symptoms. A small high-baseline subgroup improved more with meat. Fish species and preparation were not isolated.

fit: mixed oily fish including salmon and SDQ internalizing in children
assessment: The oily-fish arm improved the broad internalizing subscale by 0.63 points versus poultry. The analysis gave no standalone anxiety or cooking effect.

fit: Parkinson anxiety by overall diet score and fish by total symptom score
assessment: Anxiety models used overall diet scores, while fish-item models used total Parkinson symptom severity. The study provides no isolated salmon or poaching estimate for anxiety.

fit: Parkinson anxiety by Mediterranean diet score including fish
assessment: Higher Mediterranean diet adherence was associated with lower odds of anxiety in the Parkinson group. The symptom model used the whole score, without an estimate for the fish item, species or preparation.

fit: separate gastrointestinal conference member and ingredient context
assessment: A food analytical member identifies salmon among measured microRNA sources. Salmon elsewhere is an investigator surname. Food composition does not measure a consumed poached-salmon effect.

fit: bedside walnut-oil comparator and bathroom-related sleep interruption
assessment: Bathroom awakenings mean 2.42 with walnut vs 2.18 with active blend (p=.046). No inert arm, oral ingestion, identified cold-pressed grade, Parkinson cohort or urgency score.

fit: common bean pod extract and rat catalepsy
assessment: Catalepsy means were lower with methanol pod extract than with haloperidol alone. Pod cultivar and cooking were unverified. Catalepsy is a pharmacological motor proxy and human rigidity was untested.

fit: mixed garden produce distribution
assessment: The garden reported distribution of green beans, kale, chard and watermelon within a mixed harvest. The evaluation concerns program delivery without an ingredient-specific intake or clinical symptom measurement.

fit: common bean pod and seed levodopa concentrations
assessment: Validated mass spectrometry found 0.020 to 2.34 micrograms per gram dry weight across uncooked pod and seed samples. The study did not measure clinical rigidity or prepare cooked snap beans.

fit: green beans in a Parkinson menu and aggregate motor scores
assessment: Green beans were offered within a mixed intervention. Aggregate motor change was inconclusive. Neither green bean consumption nor a separate rigidity estimate was reported in the primary article or supplement.

fit: dried summer savory infusion and awake rat activity
assessment: Distance surrogate fell by day seven. Neither sleep nor clinical insomnia was measured.

fit: diet pattern and composite outcome
assessment: Protein timing and motor activities were tested. Raw pear and daily off time were not isolated.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: S7.519 includes pear in fruit-tree grafting work, with no pear feeding or levodopa off-time measure.

fit: low-protein dietary regimen and matching off-time outcome
assessment: An 18-person crossover found shorter OFF time with low-protein products. The separate seven-day study reused six participants and listed equal unspecified fruit portions across diets. Neither supplies a raw pear contrast.

fit: oral peanut oil placebo and planned falls in a sarcopenia trial family
assessment: TEMPUS-FUGIT specifies a 1 g peanut-oil placebo and planned falls surveillance. Published ENHANce feasibility results and accessible publisher supplement cover mobility and sarcopenia measures without a verified arm-specific falls estimate. Parkinson disease was excluded and refining was unreported.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: The arsenic model compares a chelator in peanut oil with a saline carrier. Peanut agglutinin is a separate laboratory reagent.

fit: peanut-oil carrier and vehicle controls in a related rat experiment
assessment: The published methods list vehicle-injected controls. The comparison addresses corticosterone-related biochemical outcomes and does not estimate oral peanut oil or Parkinson fall frequency. Cohort overlap with the meeting abstract remains open.

fit: intraperitoneal peanut oil as the carrier for corticosterone in rats
assessment: The verified poster measures hippocampal choline uptake and acetylcholine release. The oil is a non-oral vehicle, with no separately measured oil result for Parkinson fall frequency.

fit: peanut butter and lower-limb function in older adults at risk of falls
assessment: Five-times sit-to-stand improved by an adjusted 1.23 s with peanut butter. The gait-speed result was inconclusive. The study gives no verified prospective fall-frequency result and did not use isolated oil.

fit: cayenne frequency and combined mood and apathy domain
assessment: The exploratory analysis did not provide a cayenne-specific coefficient on the mood and apathy domain or standalone apathy.

fit: oral dried dill aerial-part and black rice extract and open-field center entries
assessment: After ischemia, the low dose on day 7 and middle dose on day 14 increased center entries compared with stroke vehicle. Total crossings showed no clear change, and no distinct anxiety severity scale, single herb arm or Parkinson population was studied.

fit: boiled dill seed and postpartum anxiety
assessment: The childbirth trial reported fewer severe anxiety ratings at six hours with boiled dill seed versus oxytocin. The seed preparation, comparator and postpartum population differ from the frozen dried leaf and Parkinson claim.

fit: maternal oral dill extract and offspring elevated-plus-maze behavior
assessment: Figure 4 shows more open-arm entries and time after extract in nicotine-exposed mice. Pairwise symbol definitions, n and plant part remain access-limited. Supplementary F and p values have apparent inconsistencies.

fit: oral sowa extract and open-arm exploration during alcohol withdrawal
assessment: Open-arm entry proportion increased under extract versus withdrawal alone at 24 hours. Rotarod performance also improved. The extract, plant part and rodent withdrawal population differ from the hypothesis.

fit: dill extract beverage and registered anxiety scale outside Parkinson disease
assessment: Thai DASS-21 is the primary outcome. The official completed registry gives no arm results or clear leaf preparation.

fit: injected Perilla constituents and conditioned defensive behavior
assessment: Original abstract reports dose-specific direction in defensive freezing and unchanged spontaneous movement at active doses. It measures a rodent fear proxy after isolated compound injection. The earlier forced-swim experiment and later review are separate reports.

fit: intranasal perilla leaf essential oil and anxiety-like behavior in mice
assessment: Open-field and elevated-maze exploration increased in stressed mice after essential oil. Nasal delivery, the stress model and behavior measures differ from fresh leaves and clinical anxiety.

fit: seed oil and open-field behavior in a rotenone mouse model
assessment: The highest seed oil diet was associated with more center entries and less grooming. Mouse locomotion and anxiety-like behavior cannot establish clinical anxiety after fresh leaves.

fit: perilla-containing formula and anxiety in major depression
assessment: The waitlist-controlled abstract reports improvement on anxiety outcomes without separate numerical estimates. Perilla was one component and participants had major depression.

fit: hydroalcoholic celery leaf extract and animal nociception
assessment: Evoked writhing decreased and thermal responses changed. No fresh-leaf meal or Parkinson pain severity measure.

fit: celery leaf decoction in uncontrolled gout care
assessment: The abstract reports two cases and a score of 5 to 3. The original body specifies one patient and 5 to 2. Boiled preparation, concurrent advice and no control limit causal attribution.

fit: celery leaf and stalk decoction in two uncontrolled gout cases
assessment: Both recorded pain scores moved from 5 to 2. The collection dates and intended regimen do not establish follow-up timing. Differences in setting and overlapping outcomes with a later report leave independence unresolved.

fit: transdermal capsaicin and spontaneous healthy eye blinking
assessment: Five healthy volunteers had no statistically clear change in spontaneous blink rate. Blinking and focal blepharospasm do not measure overall Parkinson facial expressiveness.

fit: dizziness mentioned after oral cumin essential oil in an uncontrolled IBS series
assessment: The original mentions dizziness without count, posture, associated blood pressure or control. The abstract and Results give inconsistent enrollment counts. Concentrated essential oil and uncharacterized dizziness do not establish a ground cumin effect on Parkinson standing lightheadedness.

fit: Parkinson survey recording cumin use with aggregate nonmotor measures
assessment: Cumin intake was recorded and exploratory nonmotor comparisons were inconclusive after correction. No preparation or cumin-specific orthostatic lightheadedness estimate is reported.

fit: cumin essential-oil softgels and resting blood pressure in metabolic syndrome
assessment: Diastolic pressure was lower at follow-up and systolic comparisons were inconclusive. The study did not measure standing change or lightheadedness.

fit: ground cumin seed infusion with diet and resting blood pressure
assessment: Resting systolic pressure fell in both groups, with a larger reduction for the infusion. Standing blood pressure and orthostatic lightheadedness were not measured.

fit: isolated eugenol and evoked detrusor contractions
assessment: Eugenol suppressed phasic and sustained rat bladder contraction ex vivo. The result addresses neither urinary urgency frequency nor ingested clove.

fit: PD grouped beans and composite motor burden; no black-bean or postural-instability estimate
assessment: Grouped bean question and total symptom outcome do not measure the effect of boiled black common beans on postural instability.

fit: uncooked common bean composition; no clinical outcome
assessment: Analytical levodopa concentrations in uncooked varieties cannot establish a clinical effect or its direction after boiling black beans.

fit: trained sensory panel for roasted button mushroom
assessment: Panelists rated mushroom product aroma and flavour. The design gives no longitudinal effect on participants' smell.

fit: cooked button mushroom volatile composition
assessment: Volatiles and an electronic nose characterize the food stimulus. No consumer smell test was performed.

fit: exact mushroom species fraction in a Parkinson model
assessment: Beam-walking results used an isolated protein fraction in mice. No olfactory test was reported in the abstract.

fit: Trained human panel evaluated rice bran oil during eating
assessment: Reported differences concern flavour and perceived aroma of the test oil, without a diagnosed olfactory impairment or pre-post olfactory performance measure.

fit: Named rice bran oil odor control and measured sensory ratings
assessment: The rice oil had lower perceived intensity than the active cypress stimulus in healthy adults. Relative stimulus intensity is distinct from change in Parkinson olfactory impairment.

fit: oral coriander aerial-part ethanol extract and movement tests in mice
assessment: The 2014 dissertation and three patent disclosures report the same experiment. The extract reduced normalized pole descent time from 178.44% to 102.58% of control and increased normalized rotarod retention from 29.68% to 84.84%. Lee's later experiment used different exposure arms within the same research program.

fit: aqueous freeze-dried cilantro leaf and stalk extract in developmental toxicant model
assessment: Toxin plus extract offspring covered 20.47 m versus 14.35 m with toxin alone. Spontaneous open-field distance is not measured walking velocity. Exposure was maternal.

fit: coriander in a shared Parkinson vegetarian menu and composite motor outcome
assessment: The menu lists coriander without specifying the plant part and the motor examination includes gait. The paper does not establish dried cilantro exposure or report walking speed.

fit: coriander fruit extract and rotarod performance in MPTP mice
assessment: There was no clear early rotarod benefit. A longer time to fall was reported on day 20. The tested plant part was fruit and the result does not measure clinical walking speed.

fit: cilantro leaf extract and motor tests in two mouse models
assessment: In MPTP mice, grip strength rose from 2.31 ± 0.05 N to 2.65 ± 0.08 N and 2.75 ± 0.06 N with oral leaf extract. The preview names rotarod and pole tests without a verified effect estimate for those outcomes. Dried culinary leaf and clinical walking speed remain untested.

fit: topical cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil in a combination and a speech-containing oral mucositis composite
assessment: The combination improved the aggregate PROMS score versus benzydamine. PROMS includes speaking difficulty and speech restriction from mouth sores. The study reports no individual item changes, listener speech intelligibility or toasted oil exposure.

fit: pumpkin seed oil on a Parkinson diet menu and motor-scale speech item
assessment: The published score combined motor items. The trial did not identify toasted oil intake or report a separate speech or intelligibility result.

fit: crushed nigella seed capsules and timed human attention tasks
assessment: Timed letter cancellation and Trail Making favored nigella. Cancellation accuracy was inconclusive. The authors did not report toasting and participants did not have Parkinson disease.

fit: oral ground fruit powder and Beck Depression Inventory in non-Parkinson randomized trial
assessment: Table 4 reports mean BDI-II changes −10.41 ± 11.08 with powder and −9.74 ± 8.50 with placebo (p=.78). Both received calorie restriction. IRCT20131228015968N6 and the later appetite paper are from the same trial family.

fit: injected ethanolic Rhus coriaria extract in mice
assessment: Tail-suspension immobility fell while open-field locomotion showed no significant change. The study used an injected extract in a non-Parkinson model.

fit: onion-containing mixed extract and catalepsy in mice
assessment: Bar catalepsy reductions versus MPTP alone did not meet the reported significance criterion. The blend was processed and does not isolate raw onion or clinical rigidity.

fit: veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison
assessment: The poisoning entry reports onion among foods hazardous to dogs and cats. It supplies no measured oral onion effect on Parkinson rigidity.

fit: onion odor and motor progression classification
assessment: Recognizing onion odor had an inconclusive association with rapid versus slow motor progression (OR 1.56, p = .477). Neither raw onion intake nor individual rigidity change was assessed.

fit: onion odor and examiner-rated rigidity
assessment: The cross-sectional odds of identifying onion odor were lower at higher rigidity scores with q = .119. Participants smelled the stimulus and no raw onion intake effect was estimated.

fit: lentils among Parkinson menu options and motor examination total
assessment: The plant menu group had a lower four-week motor total. The comparison does not isolate lentils or preparation, and facial expression was not reported separately.

fit: shared Parkinson vegetarian menu with lentils and motor composite
assessment: The two small groups improved on total UPDRS III. The study gives no lentil preparation, isolated intake or facial expression item contrast.

fit: lentils among prebiotic menu options and composite motor score
assessment: A four-week menu and lactulose intervention produced an inconclusive motor total change. Published data do not isolate lentil preparation or intake and omit individual facial expression changes.

fit: paprika xanthophyll supplementation and executive tasks
assessment: Open UMIN000055963 crossover with 21 analyzed. Trail Making B and two Stroop interactions gave p=.877, .495 and .581. Extract and ground paprika differ, and participants did not have Parkinson disease.

fit: red bell pepper extract and before–after Trail Making B
assessment: Before-exercise Trail Making B moved from 50.1 to 45.2 seconds (p=.039) and after-exercise from 42.2 to 41.7 (p=.061). All 31 participants received extract with repeated testing and exercise. UMIN and article are the same cohort.

fit: paprika xanthophyll with eye exercise and executive outcomes
assessment: The registry describes a controlled crossover in healthy participants. Clinical Parkinson executive impairment and ground paprika exposure are not specified.

fit: heat-processed soup with fresh lovage in healthy adults
assessment: Feasibility and pooled gastrointestinal adverse events were reported, without a fatigue severity estimate.

fit: individual Parkinson symptoms and diet scores
assessment: Diet scores were associated with fatigue at the pattern level, without a preparation-specific lovage estimate.

fit: cilantro leaf fractions and mouse anxiety tests
assessment: The aqueous fraction gave the strongest anxiety-like behavioral signal. The study used concentrated fractions in mice without Parkinsonism.

fit: injected cilantro leaf extract and mouse anxiety behavior
assessment: The extract produced a favorable signal on exploratory anxiety-like behavior. The preparation was injected and the mice did not have Parkinsonism.

fit: coriander seed capsules and anxiety in students
assessment: The publication abstract reports lower anxiety with seed capsules, p = .04. Registered outcome priorities differ from the report. The trial used seeds in university students.

fit: dried cilantro leaf aqueous extract and mouse anxiety proxies with conflicting administration route
assessment: Original abstract says oral treatment and Methods say injected extract without route site. Open-arm measures favor extract, with a low-dose significance threshold different from the abstract. No clinical effect of intact dried leaf established.

fit: soybean oil diet and rodent open-field freezing
assessment: Open-field stopping time was 135.0 seconds on soybean oil versus 72.76 on equal-fat perilla under rotenone. This includes anxiety-like immobility and gives no human gait-freezing episode estimate.

fit: pea protein breakfast and exploratory cognition reporting
assessment: The registry schedules cognitive assessments before breakfast and at 90 and 180 minutes. The 37-person likely companion publishes intake only. A separate 32-person study uses NCT03154606 and cannot supply the registered executive results.

fit: pea protein comparator and prospective executive tasks
assessment: The registered 119-person healthy adult comparison uses about 40 g per day of pea protein as the comparator and specifies executive accuracy, Stroop and flanker outcomes. Results are unposted. No intervention arm uses cooked whole peas or enrolls people with Parkinson disease.

fit: isolated lectin and rat working memory
assessment: Y-maze spontaneous alternation declined in the combined toxin and lectin arm. The lectin-only arm had no clear change. The study measured rat behavior.

fit: A parsley allergy patient reported tolerance of dried preparation
assessment: Fresh and cooked exposure produced allergic symptoms. The dried tolerance was reported as clinical history. The abstract gives no formal graded oral swallow assessment or Parkinson cohort.

fit: A garlic-and-parsley dish appears in a dysphagia home-menu design
assessment: The published result is recipe development with workshops, without confirmed dried parsley consumption in a clinical subgroup or measured change in swallowing difficulty.

fit: Parsley-containing thick puree measured before and after oral processing
assessment: Five healthy volunteers prepared boluses that were spat out. Noodle purée viscosity decreased 61.07%, with no isolated parsley exposure or swallow severity measure.

fit: A parsley-containing recipe in a clinical dysphagia meal programme
assessment: Appendix A includes garlic and parsley in both versions. Only aggregate acceptability and production or texture outcomes were reported.

fit: working memory in non-Parkinson aged rats receiving lyophilized mushroom
assessment: Working memory improved at 0.5% dietary supplementation. The other concentrations did not demonstrate that improvement.

fit: randomized capsule exposure to dried white button mushroom in healthy older adults
assessment: Reported no significant cognitive treatment effect across the randomized comparison. Dried capsules and healthy participants leave the roasted Parkinson exposure unresolved.

fit: button mushroom supplementation in an amyloid model
assessment: The study reported spatial-memory improvement in a transgenic mouse model of amyloid disease. It supplies no preparation-specific Parkinson executive outcome.

fit: pooled mushroom intake and executive measures
assessment: Positive cross-sectional associations could reflect confounding or reverse causality. Species, roasting, and Parkinson status were unavailable.

fit: randomized white button and oyster mixture in non-Parkinson adults
assessment: Both arms improved immediate memory. Control-only delayed list recall improvement and null attention tasks are indirect cognitive findings. No roasted exposure was assigned.

fit: randomized whole UV-treated cremini exposure and cognitive testing
assessment: RBANS domains showed no significant time-by-group effects. Cremini shares the species but the trial used another market type, no roasting assignment, and no Parkinson cohort.

fit: exact mushroom species fraction in a Parkinson model
assessment: Beam-walking results used an isolated protein fraction in mice. No executive task was reported in the abstract.

fit: other mushroom species and direct executive task
assessment: Oyster mushroom trial reported a reaction-time interaction, with placebo slowing and unchanged accuracy. Button mushroom and Parkinson were outside the trial.

fit: hot-water pomegranate extract and drowsiness scores in sleep-deprived rats
assessment: The primary abstract reports amelioration in a sleep-deprivation model. Numerical score estimates are unavailable. The result does not establish daytime sleepiness after raw fruit in Parkinson disease.

fit: multi-ingredient polyphenol blend and registered daytime sleepiness
assessment: Sleepiness is registered in healthy adults. The primary pharmacokinetic report gives no separate score. The blend includes many plant extracts, with no isolated pomegranate comparison.

fit: four-botanical blend including pomegranate peel and self-reported alertness
assessment: Day-21 predose alertness favored the blend in a follow-up versus placebo (p=.03), while the group-by-session interaction was p=.07. The blend, healthy cohort and proxy measure preclude a conclusion about raw arils and Parkinson daytime sleepiness.

fit: nanoemulsified pomegranate seed oil and planned Parkinson daytime sleepiness
assessment: NMSS and a Parkinson sleep scale were planned. No results were verified. The intervention is a nanoformulated oil capsule.

fit: oral pomegranate juice and global sleep quality during opioid treatment
assessment: Global PSQI improved in the methadone subgroup. No separate daytime dysfunction estimate or sleepiness adverse-event count was verified. The cohort and exposure differ from the claim.

fit: pomegranate rind extract and a sleep-change subscale in premenstrual syndrome
assessment: The post-intervention sleep score was 8.40 versus 9.63, p=.146. The paper did not measure dedicated daytime sleepiness, raw arils or Parkinson disease.

fit: sequential pomegranate acai combination and self-reported alertness
assessment: The healthy cohort received the Peach Mango product first and Pomegranate Acai later. Alertness was planned. No result is posted and an isolated aril contrast is absent.

fit: reported tofu intake and diagnosis
assessment: The adjusted association with Parkinson diagnosis was inconclusive (OR .86, 95% CI .65 to 1.15). The abstract gives no baked preparation or drooling endpoint.

fit: okara-enriched tofu and acute salivary secretion during chewing
assessment: Enriched tofu elicited higher acute secretion in the author abstract. Baking and Parkinson drooling were not assessed. Saliva production and external loss are distinct outcomes.

fit: corn-oil comparator and time until fatigue during analgesic withdrawal
assessment: At the first visit off active diclofenac, time until fatigue changed by −0.76 hours in the corn arm (p=.19) and −0.19 hours in the fish arm (p=.64), each within arm. The eight-week table also gives inconclusive within-arm changes. Oil refining and Parkinson fatigue severity were not measured.

study: BNA2019 injected oil or preference member
fit: animal vehicle or flavored-milk preference outside the frozen preparation
assessment: PT080 and another member report injected corn oil as vehicle or control in a perimenopause model. The oil route, associated interventions and measures differ from oral corn oil.

fit: corn-oil high-fat rodent comparison
assessment: Muscle molecular markers differ across high-fat oils. The active comparator and molecular outcome do not estimate an isolated refined corn oil and Parkinson endpoint effect.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: Carney 2009 combines sertraline with corn oil; other original or protocol records use different lipid mixtures and symptom scales. The review cannot isolate the oil or a Parkinson endpoint.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: P210 compares EPA/DHA-enriched high-fat chow against corn-oil high-fat chow for muscle transcriptome and proteins. No separate frozen patient outcome.

fit: corn oil as high-fat diet control and partial marine-lipid substitution
assessment: Corn oil was one base formulation, with and without different marine PUFA fractions. Adiposity and lipids were measured. The possibly overlapping article concerns the same broad research and a refined corn oil symptom effect is unresolved.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: P233 is appended in the complete PMC HTML for this oral-key record and separately printed in the poster supplement. It compares corn and fish oil during shared exercise for strength and mechanistic outcomes. One study family.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: Printed P233 reports an omega-3 versus corn-oil comparator during shared resistance training. Its strength findings are distinct from the frozen clinical outcomes. The other PMC key reproduces this member.

fit: corn-oil control during exercise training
assessment: The final isometric interaction is p=.015 and the corn arm changed −1.4%. P233 uses −0.3%. Body strength during shared training does not measure any frozen Parkinson endpoint in these claims.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and VAS fatigue
assessment: A six-month Sjögren trial reports no clear group difference in fatigue or 24-hour sleep/rest time when comparing corn oil and evening-primrose gamma-linolenic acid. The public abstract omits grade and arm-level fatigue estimates.

fit: corn oil vs omega-3 and fatigue in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis
assessment: FSS contrasts p=.97 at six months and p=.57 across 24 months. Group means and oil grade unavailable.

fit: separate gastrointestinal conference member and ingredient context
assessment: A tumor experiment incorporates corn oil in control or combined diets involving EPA and aspirin. The study does not assign the frozen preparation and clinical endpoint.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and prespecified fatigue ratings
assessment: A Japanese registry identifies a completed healthy-adult study measuring fatigue around mental work and on awakening. The record has no arm-level results or refining grade.

fit: corn versus fish oil and exercise fatigue
assessment: Twenty healthy adults; official result reports no group difference without numbers. Separate from the UMIN mental-work fatigue study.

fit: blend containing marjoram and PSQI in rheumatoid arthritis
assessment: Massage trial reports global sleep changes across groups and no separate REM dream enactment. Mixed essential oils, skin exposure and rheumatoid arthritis differ from the claim.

fit: marjoram massage and bruxism trial or conference abstract
assessment: Registry specifies complaints and bruxism measures. The conference abstract reports jaw ultrasound results. No fresh culinary exposure or dream-enactment measure.

fit: blend containing marjoram, inhalation and topical bruxism trial
assessment: Trial specifies jaw ultrasound with pain and stress symptoms. It does not measure dream enactment and has no posted results.

fit: essential oil massage and detector-derived sleep measures
assessment: Wake or dream duration showed no clear group difference. The study did not measure dream enactment or eating fresh marjoram.

fit: methanolic basil leaf extract and rodent motor tests
assessment: Rotarod times were 31.0 and 32.7 seconds versus 12.7 seconds with haloperidol alone, and catalepsy scores were lower. Taxonomic naming and group sizes are internally unclear. No fresh culinary leaf or clinical Parkinson outcome was tested.

fit: injected sweet basil extract and rotarod/stair tasks
assessment: High-dose injected extract increased rotarod time from 57.3 to 144.6 seconds and shortened stair task time from 35.8 to 29.3 seconds. The text conflicts with tables at the lower level. There was no isolated clinical symptom measure.

fit: fresh basil in both clinical Parkinson diet menus
assessment: Both diet groups offered fresh basil in different dishes. The study gives no basil-dose contrast or separate postural instability effect by exposure.

fit: mixed Parkinson diet and composite motor score
assessment: Appendix A lists both herbs in a multicomponent diet. Composite UPDRS III scores improved. The examination includes postural stability, but no item-level result, individual herb amount or preparation, or herb-specific contrast was reported.

fit: oral sweet basil essential oil and coordination in mice
assessment: The highest oral oil group showed worse rotarod coordination, while the intermediate group did not show a clear motor deficit. The study used concentrated oil in mice without a Parkinson model and did not measure postural instability after eating fresh basil.

fit: rectal sesame oil in a multimodal regimen and speech item
assessment: The parkinsonism series reported a favorable within-person speech score. It supplies no speech estimate after consuming toasted sesame oil.

fit: sesame oil swishing and speech difficulty ratings in oral submucous fibrosis
assessment: The original table has inconsistent arm totals and gives no reliable between-arm speech estimate. The study does not verify consumption, toasted preparation, Parkinson disease or listener intelligibility.

fit: caraway essential oil odor; adults without neurodegenerative disease; no writing outcome
assessment: Odor ratings and separately analyzed language scores cannot determine handwriting size after toasted caraway.

fit: People with persistent smell problems describe lentil odor
assessment: Uncontrolled post-COVID self-report, not Parkinson disease; lentils are objects of altered odor perception and no ingestion effect, objective smell score or boiled preparation is established.

fit: Prospective dietary pattern includes legumes and analyzes B-SIT hyposmia
assessment: The cohort excluded diagnosed Parkinson disease; the reported null result compares overall Mediterranean-style diet adherence, not lentils or their preparation. Smell impairment was dichotomized against a reference distribution rather than tested as a lentil-specific change.

fit: PD broccoli and ground white mustard tea; single self-reported handwriting series
assessment: One unchanged handwriting rating under a mixed uncontrolled exposure does not assess toasted mustard seed or isolate its effect on hand dexterity.

fit: sesame oil used as a diagnostic smell stimulus
assessment: The adapted diagnostic test used a sesame oil scent to measure existing impairment. It did not test an ingestion effect.

fit: sesame oil odor in a community smell assay
assessment: The oil substituted for coffee as a test odor. The study provides a measure of sensory recognition without assigned ingestion or preparation-specific effect.

fit: diagnostic sesame-oil odor in Parkinson and multiple system atrophy
assessment: Correct identification was 44.4% in Parkinson disease and 100% in seven multiple system atrophy comparators (p=.010). This does not measure a change from consuming oil.

fit: intranasal sesame oil with respiratory and sleep outcomes
assessment: The original Methods and tables do not provide a measured change in olfactory function. The healthy study uses nasal exposure and no oral sesame comparison.

fit: sesame-labeled stimulus in Parkinson olfactory screening
assessment: The sesame stimulus had AUC 0.655 during discovery. An odor diagnostic contrast does not establish effect of oral cold-pressed oil.

fit: probiotic drops with reported soybean vehicle and stimulated saliva
assessment: Stimulated flow rose in both periodontal trial arms. The original abstract does not identify the oil. Soybean vehicle is secondary attribution, refining is unverified, and drooling is distinct from stimulated flow.

fit: human soybean-oil oral contact and measured emulsion properties
assessment: The study identifies the soybean oil in a mixture that participants swished and spat out. Incomplete recovery prevented estimation of salivary flow. Drooling severity in Parkinson disease was outside the study.

fit: registered one-week dark chocolate crossover with aggregate Parkinson symptom outcomes
assessment: A separate one-week protocol plans UPDRS and PDQ-39 along with several other measures. Status is Unknown and no outcomes are posted. Speech-item reporting and listener intelligibility remain unverified.

fit: plain dark chocolate versus cacao-free white chocolate and aggregate Parkinson motor score
assessment: The single-dose crossover tested 200 g of 80.1% cocoa dark chocolate without other supplements in 26 patients. The one-hour composite UPDRS III between-treatment effect was −0.54 points (95% CI −1.50 to 0.42). The original body gives no separate speech result or listener intelligibility test.

fit: flavonoid-rich cocoa in a rice beverage and fatigue in Parkinson disease
assessment: The pilot measured fatigue and fatigability after high- versus low-flavonoid cocoa beverages. The study gives no plain dark chocolate contrast or speech intelligibility estimate.

fit: fish odor in a Parkinson smell-identification test
assessment: The smell test used fish odor as one item and reported a group composite. It neither identifies cod nor measures change after eating baked fish.

fit: pooled fish intake and objective olfactory impairment in older adults
assessment: Top versus bottom fish intake quartile associated with lower prevalent olfactory impairment, OR 0.65 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.96), but five-year incident OR was 1.23 (0.75 to 2.02). The food category does not isolate cod or baking and the cohort results are for community-dwelling older adults.

fit: oral avocado-oil comparator and Visual Analog Mood Scale tranquility in healthy adults
assessment: Mean tranquility was 297.3 to 301.3 in the mint-flavored avocado oil arm and 303.0 to 302.4 with CBD, baseline-adjusted p=.85. This short-term proxy gives no verified refined grade, oil-free comparison or Parkinson anxiety result.

fit: oral cold-pressed avocado oil and plus-maze measures in obese mice
assessment: Plus-maze open-arm time and entries did not clearly differ across groups. The oil was cold-pressed, and the experiment did not measure clinical anxiety.

fit: avocado oil mayonnaise in a broader ketogenic case description
assessment: The uncontrolled Down syndrome and Alzheimer case included avocado-oil mayonnaise. Improvement in anxiety was qualitative. Neither a refined oil comparison nor Parkinson disease was present.

fit: ketogenic diet and measured Parkinson anxiety with unisolated oil exposure
assessment: The seven-person continuation reports mean PAS change −6.29 (p=.0313). A participant mentions coconut or avocado oil. The reported exposure, change, control and preparation do not allow an oil-specific effect.

fit: oral avocado oil during pregnancy and lactation and rat anxiety-like behavior
assessment: Oil and pulp groups showed shorter open-arm time and adult offspring in the oil group moved less. Refining, a Parkinson population and clinical anxiety were unverified.

fit: avocado oil within an oral placebo blend and measured anxiety in fibromyalgia
assessment: HADS anxiety means were 9.40 and 9.60 before and after the mixed placebo. The between-arm estimate was −1.56 (95% CI −4.43 to 1.32). The trial has no isolated refined avocado oil or Parkinson anxiety contrast.

fit: cardamom listed in multicomponent Parkinson diet and composite UPDRS III
assessment: The composite improved and includes postural stability. The authors did not report that item separately or isolate cardamom.

fit: Parkinson case with depression in treatment timeline
assessment: Authors reported improved depression during follow-up after combined formula treatment and rehabilitation. No scale or isolated culinary exposure was available.

fit: red and green pepper extracts and stress-model behavior
assessment: Red and green pepper extracts changed immobility during forced swimming. The red and green species differed in open-field effects. No Parkinson clinical outcome was measured.

fit: Sichuan pepper polyphenol extract with internally inconsistent mouse immobility reporting
assessment: The original Figure 2 bars for extract are above negative control, in agreement with Results and opposite to the Discussion's reading. Methods describe time until resting, and the graph gives only a generic time label. This result and the unaltered voluntary activity give no reliable direction for clinical depression from toasted pepper.

fit: mixed topical Sichuan pepper preparation and combined anxiety depression item
assessment: The recruiting pelvic-pain trial includes ground Sichuan pepper in a mixed plaster and EQ-5D as a secondary quality-of-life measure. It has no separate pepper arm, confirmed toasting, Parkinson cohort or posted results.

fit: placebo-controlled mood proxies with oral Nepalese pepper extract in healthy adults
assessment: In 82 healthy adults, the acute contentment interaction had no clear between-arm contrast at any individual assessment. No clear chronic mood or anxiety difference was reported over 56 days. The lipid extract is a separate species preparation, with no clinical depression scale or Parkinson cohort.

fit: Sichuan pepper fruit essential oil and stress-model behavior
assessment: Forced-swim immobility changed at all doses, with low-dose null findings for sucrose preference and tail suspension. The experiment used mice and essential oil.

fit: filtered marjoram tea and motor examination in Parkinson
assessment: The motor examination is reported in aggregate. No measure of letter size was presented.

fit: baked rye preparation and other human outcomes
assessment: The rye formulation was baked and measured mood and cognition. Freezing episodes and Parkinson’s were outside the design.

fit: gluten withdrawal report in one celiac parkinsonism case with partial original access
assessment: The original preview establishes walking difficulty, postural instability and baseline UPDRS II 8 and III 19. It stops ahead of the outcome table. The title and subsequent review describe improvement, without a verified freezing or rye bread outcome.

fit: paprika xanthophyll in a student exercise and mouth-rinse comparison
assessment: Trail Making B improved within conditions with exercise and mouth rinse with or without paprika. The abstract gives no direct isolated contrast.

fit: paprika xanthophyll in a seven-condition nighttime crossover
assessment: Only the three-component condition produced a reported pre-post Trail Making improvement. No paprika-alone or addition contrast was reported.

fit: repeated kindergarten vegetable exposure, intake and liking
assessment: Vegetables were offered in conjunction with a reward. The sample was children, and neither adult symptoms nor the matched preparation were assessed. The registration gives n = 82, while the two arm counts in the poster add to 84.

fit: oral red bell pepper extract and executive tasks in older adults
assessment: Trail Making B times improved in the before-exercise comparison across visits (p = .039) with an inconclusive postexercise comparison (p = .061). The 31 participants all received the extract and no Parkinson cohort was included.

fit: oral paprika xanthophyll and executive outcomes in a healthy crossover
assessment: Same UMIN000055963 crossover. Trail Making B improved by 1.1 seconds during extract and by 1.0 second during control, with interaction p=.877. Within-supplement changes cannot establish a comparative effect. Grilled pepper and Parkinson were outside the design.

fit: registered parallel paprika extract and cognitive testing in healthy adults
assessment: Official registry lists 40 enrolled, completion and unpublished outcomes. It lists cognitive tests and a supplement comparison, without a grilled food exposure.

fit: placebo-controlled paprika extract and executive tasks in students
assessment: The crossover plans Trail Making B and Stroop outcomes with extraocular exercise and oral capsules. Results remain unpublished and the study has no Parkinson cohort.

fit: green kiwi juice and rotarod in mice
assessment: Post-dose rotarod times were slightly lower and marked p < .05 versus saline despite the paper's absence-of-muscle-relaxation conclusion. The population and preparation differ.

fit: kiwi-containing extract combination and motor coordination
assessment: The oral three-fruit extract improved hanging-wire performance in a haloperidol model. A kiwi-only arm, raw fruit and clinical postural assessments were absent.

fit: kiwi as an ingredient and composite Parkinson motor results
assessment: The diet included kiwi and UPDRS III measured postural stability within a composite. The paper gives no preparation, isolated exposure or item-level estimate.

fit: hardy kiwi juice and beam walking in a Parkinson model
assessment: The investigator follow-up gives group sizes and a p < .01 motor comparison. Beam walking in MPTP mice and previously frozen hardy kiwi juice differ from clinical postural instability and raw fruit.

fit: bilberry and grape juice with dominant-hand pegboard
assessment: The mixed juice versus placebo study reports an inconclusive dominant-hand comparison (p=.41). It does not isolate raw grape intake.

fit: purified grape seed extract and simple finger movement rate
assessment: Baseline-adjusted estimates at weeks 6 and 12 were 123.24 to 125.71 with extract and 124.36 to 121.43 with placebo (interaction p=.005). The follow-up describes placebo decline and maintained extract performance. Complex results were inconclusive. The manuscript Methods match the CP9700 registry despite a conflicting cover ID.

fit: grape seed extract and a planned bilateral finger tapping outcome
assessment: The linked 2026 Papa subset publication reports continuous performance and mood. The registered motor result remains unverified.

fit: grape powder and planned grip and pinch strength
assessment: A single-group trial combines grape powder with water. No numerical hand-strength result, raw-fruit contrast or Parkinson cohort was verified.

fit: Concord grape juice and grooved pegboard in a healthy crossover
assessment: Juice was slower than placebo in phase one (63.2 vs 60.4 s), with no clear difference in phase two. This is a phase-specific processed juice comparison in healthy adults.

fit: juice plus exercise
assessment: The two papers describe one registered study. Juice supplied no clear added functional or cognitive benefit.

fit: rosmarinic-acid-containing perilla extract and urinary frequency
assessment: The patent reports fewer nighttime voids and inconclusive daytime and volume comparisons. The intervention was perilla extract and urgency was unmeasured.

fit: daily whole walnuts and Epworth Sleepiness Scale
assessment: Healthy young adults showed −1.37 points relative to baseline after 8 weeks (95% CI −2.21 to −0.52, p=.002). Control period had no clear baseline change. Whole nut and open-label non-Parkinson exposure.

fit: walnut oil within a placebo blend and reports of somnolence in fibromyalgia
assessment: The placebo containing walnut, avocado and MCT oil had three somnolence event reports versus five with cannabinoids. The endpoint and combined comparator leave cold-pressed walnut oil and Parkinson daytime sleepiness unresolved.

fit: sweet almond oil massage and total postoperative delirium scores
assessment: After open-heart surgery, the sweet almond oil massage arm had mean total NEECHAM scores of 26.70 on day 1 and 27.62 on day 3, versus 26.20 and 27.18 in routine care, with across-three-arm p=.39, .66, .06 at the three assessments. A separately scored attention item was unavailable. Topical massage, acute postoperative delirium, and chronic Parkinson attention impairment differ.

fit: sweet almond powder with rock candy and Alzheimer attention-domain scores
assessment: In Alzheimer disease, sweet almond powder plus rock candy changed mean MoCA attention scores from 5.26 to 5.20 versus 4.86 to 4.83 in routine care (p=.776 for the between-group change in the attention domain). The intervention combined whole-nut powder and candy and did not test oil or Parkinson disease.

fit: sweet almond syrup and parent-rated inattention in pediatric ADHD
assessment: Inattention scores moved 11.57 to 6.20 versus 8.05 to 8.10 under placebo. Raw Tukey contrasts were p=.003 at baseline and p=.011 at week 12. The printed table does not clearly show a baseline-adjusted estimate. All children took methylphenidate and the syrup is a separate formulation from cold-pressed almond oil.

fit: topical almond massage and delirium composite in acute cardiac care
assessment: A randomized post-infarction trial reported an overall three-arm NEECHAM composite time-by-group p<.001 after lavender massage, unscented sweet almond oil massage, or routine care. The published result does not isolate an almond-specific attention domain, and this was a topical intervention in acute cardiac care.

fit: whole celery extract and beam walking in mice
assessment: Beam crossing improved. The study did not count freezing episodes or use fresh leaves.

fit: celery named in a Parkinson diet with a gait-inclusive motor scale
assessment: No isolated celery arm, leaf identification or separate freezing of gait outcome.

fit: oral grapeseed oil cookie and registered gait speed
assessment: Gait speed was specified for a secondary correlation. No gait or fall estimate was reported in the publications checked. Participants were healthy adults.

fit: oral grapeseed oil cookie and registered walking speed
assessment: Walking speed is listed in a planned secondary correlation. There is no posted result or fall-count measure and no Parkinson cohort.

fit: grape seed extract and gait or rotarod in Parkinson-model rats
assessment: The hydroalcoholic extract increased stride length (p < .05) and rotarod time (p < .01). The study did not record clinical falls or feed grapeseed oil.

fit: dietary cold-pressed oil and measured sucrose intake and sociability
assessment: Oil in feed increased sucrose consumption in both sexes and sociability in males only. The unlesioned rat endpoints do not establish ground nigella seed effects on Parkinson apathy.

fit: Nigella oil and social approach after experimental antibiotic exposure
assessment: Nigella oil groups had higher sociability indices than the antibiotic-only group. Clinical apathy and the ground-seed preparation were untested.

fit: Multi-food Parkinson diet contains cooked green peas and reports an individual with prior postural hypotension and ongoing falls
assessment: Low-fat menus include peas in several cooked multi-ingredient recipes; individual consumption and event timing are unknown, falls are not counted, and midodrine was increased. No isolated pea or fall-frequency estimate.
