assessment: Six participants received linalool and eugenol as odor stimuli. Attention instructions changed odor-evoked electrical signals. The intervention contrast provides no estimate of clinical attention impairment after ground allspice ingestion.

fit: rat CNS activity and fresh allspice leaf extracts
assessment: Rat behavioral screening after injection included nonspecific CNS suppression. No explicit attention task or oral ground-berry comparison was reported.

fit: sunflower food frequency and composite Parkinson symptom burden
assessment: The poster reports +2 total PRO-PD points per intake frequency category (95% CI −10 to 13, p=.787). The cross-sectional exposure did not specify an oil grade. It gives no individual olfaction estimate.

fit: sunflower oil original source context
assessment: Study groups shared injected tamoxifen in sunflower oil. Gait and nonmotor tests include a buried-food olfaction task and operant sensation seeking, with no separate dietary oil comparison.

fit: freeze-dried cranberry powder and baseline PHQ-9 screening in healthy older adults
assessment: The protocol scheduled PHQ-9, and the Connell thesis and paper confirm baseline PHQ-9 screening in COMBAT participants. The cognitive, metabolite and baseline analyses do not give a post-treatment depression comparison by arm. Same trial family as ISRCTN76069316.

fit: cranberry extract in a mixed snack and depression scores during simulated altitude
assessment: POMS depression was higher in both high-altitude conditions than low altitude, with no detected difference between same-altitude mixture and placebo. Cranberry was one of multiple ingredients and the adults did not have Parkinson disease.

fit: cranberry juice crossover with a planned global mood score
assessment: The trial planned overall Profile of Mood States disturbance. It supplies no depression-subscale result or assignment to dried cranberries.

fit: cranberry drink and HADS depression and POMS depression-dejection in healthy students
assessment: HADS depression overall and week 12 were inconclusive. The distinct POMS depression-dejection score was higher at week 4 by 3.34 points (95% CI 0.526 to 6.16, p = .02). Later contrasts and the main treatment test were inconclusive. The article reports a treatment-by-visit p = .02 for the subscale. The frozen exposure and Parkinson population were not tested.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: A nursing-home poster reviews cranberry and oral anticoagulant coexposure. It does not compare frozen cranberries for Parkinson symptom changes.

fit: cranberry juice and older adult self-rated general mood
assessment: In the randomized six-week 50-person pilot, the author abstract reports inconclusive between-group tests for perceived mood and energy changes without item effect estimates. Juice and self-rated general mood are distinct from dried cranberry and depression severity in Parkinson disease.

fit: berry polyphenol extracts in a rat metabolic model
assessment: The biochemical table marks triglyceride differences in several extract arms. Preparation and model differ, and there is no symptom outcome. The cranberry denominators and route wording do not fully reconcile.

fit: freeze-dried commercial cranberry juice applied to a cell-free MAO-A assay
assessment: The article reports inhibition with discordant IC50 values and units. The enzyme source is unspecified. No participant exposure or depression outcome was tested. A separate human adipose experiment by overlapping authors used pomegranate.

fit: cranberry anthocyanin extract and mouse immobility proxies
assessment: Figure 2 shows no detected change relative to vehicle in tail-suspension or forced-swimming immobility at either extract dose. The animal measures and concentrated extract do not estimate a dried cranberry effect on clinical depression.

fit: diet pattern and composite outcome
assessment: Protein timing and motor activities were tested. Raw apricot and daily off time were not isolated.

fit: low-protein dietary regimen and matching off-time outcome
assessment: Randomized crossover reported shorter off time with low-protein products. Raw apricot was not isolated.

fit: apricot kernel extract and haloperidol model catalepsy rather than fruit or OFF time
assessment: Saleem and colleagues prepared a methanolic extract from authenticated fresh apricot kernels. In haloperidol-exposed rats, the highest tested extract group showed shorter bar-test catalepsy latency than disease controls (Figure 1, p < .001), with additional findings in beam and open-field tasks. This examines seed-kernel extract and evoked animal motor impairment. It supplies no human OFF-time diary or raw apricot flesh comparison.

fit: habanero extract and acute swallowing timing
assessment: Thirteen participants completed the Parkinson crossover. Four videofluoroscopy timing measures showed no clear difference after extract versus placebo. Ground cayenne and symptom severity were outside the comparison.

fit: placebo-controlled oral capsaicin film in mixed chronic dysphagia
assessment: In 42 gastrostomy-fed patients including people with Parkinson, oral capsaicin film reduced pooled immediate swallowing reflex latency. Sustained latency change was inconclusive. The abstract supplies no Parkinson subgroup estimate or ground cayenne exposure.

fit: aerosolized extract in an uncontrolled dysphagia series
assessment: The 16-patient series reports clinical use and associations without a Parkinson subgroup response or controlled severity estimate.

fit: capsaicin drink or chilled capsaicin probe and water swallow signs
assessment: The abstract reports pooled signs without a Parkinson subgroup or separate probe temperature effect.

fit: aerosolized capsaicin and endoscopic swallowing in mixed neurogenic dysphagia

fit: capsaicin jelly and green tea swallows in a mixed cohort
assessment: Nine participants included five with Parkinson. Pooled swallow latency and duration fell five minutes after jelly. No Parkinson subgroup data or ground cayenne. Same authors report follow-up in 2002, with participant overlap unknown.

fit: capsaicin jelly and instrumental timing in Parkinson
assessment: Fifteen with Parkinson and no overt aspiration took contrast jelly with and without capsaicin. Mean pharyngeal delay and passage times were shorter with capsaicin, with no significance tests given. The preparation and short-term endpoint differ from the claim.

fit: related ground red chili and non-Parkinson gargle
assessment: A filtered ground red chili gargle increased mean saliva-swallow counts from baseline at 20 minutes in ten healthy adults. Cultivar, between-condition effect and clinical Parkinson outcomes were unverified.

fit: related ground red chili and non-Parkinson physiology
assessment: Twelve healthy adults chewed fewer times and had altered manometry with commercial ground red chili in mochi. Cayenne cultivar and Parkinson dysphagia severity were untested.

fit: capsaicin and swallowing-related breathing with cohort and results unavailable

fit: qualitative dysphagia response during vinegar and levodopa coadministration

fit: oral capsaicin jelly and six-month dysphagia follow-up

fit: nonpungent CH-19 Sweet capsinoid seasoning on a VF jelly

fit: inhaled diagnostic stimulus
assessment: The registered and published analyses characterize cough physiology. No culinary or swallowing treatment contrast.

fit: inhaled diagnostic stimulus
assessment: Posted outcomes describe cough sensitivity and separate swallowing testing by disease group. No ground cayenne treatment contrast.

fit: aerosolized capsaicin used to measure reflex cough

fit: acute pharyngeal catheter challenge with CH-19 Sweet capsiate
assessment: In 12 older patients with aspiration pneumonia, mean reflex latency was 16.3 s with water and 6.1 s at 100 nM capsiate. Extract, catheter route and cohort differ from the frozen claim, and no Parkinson subgroup was reported.

fit: red-pepper-seasoned cabbage and swallowing reflex latency
assessment: Within-group latency shortened in older adults without dysphagia. The study had no unexposed control and removed the red pepper slices and pickling liquid before serving.

fit: topical aural capsaicin and mixed dysphagia
assessment: Pooled swallowing outcomes favored the intervention on some measures. Parkinson subgroup contained three participants with no separate effect.

fit: swallowing endoscopy after nebulized capsaicin in a stroke case
assessment: After a week, secretion ratings improved and silent aspiration for IDDSI Level 1 liquid remained unchanged. Later measurements followed combined therapy and used different test consistencies. This is an uncontrolled post-stroke inhalation case.

fit: aerosolized cayenne and cough
assessment: A mixed cohort included three participants with Parkinson disease. The study measured cough and supplied no Parkinson-specific swallowing estimate.

fit: capsaicin wafer and swallow timing
assessment: No clear swallowing timing improvement in the small wafer comparison.

fit: capsaicin as part of a Parkinson cough training program
assessment: The intervention combines cough practice, feedback and aerosol stimulus. It gives no isolated capsaicin or swallowing difficulty treatment estimate.

fit: capsaicin solution and mixed dysphagia population
assessment: The active arm showed a within-arm change. The abstract does not give a between-group or Parkinson-specific estimate.

fit: oral liquid extract and cough provocation in healthy adults

fit: ginger tea and post-dose pain ratings in a 50-student quasi-experiment

fit: fresh ginger in warm water and menstrual pain with conflicting tables

fit: ginger and tea beverage against aerobic exercise with conflicting comparator reports

fit: steamed ethanol extract and postpartum perineal versus uterine pain

fit: ginger in a mixture and menstrual pain

fit: supercritical ginger root extract and planned sciatica pain outcomes

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: P-862 reviews ginger and weight or fat loss, without a frozen Parkinson endpoint.

fit: Ginger extract and osteoarthritis pain

fit: Two-botanical extract and knee pain

fit: Encapsulated ground ginger rhizome and experimental arm pain

fit: Single-dose ginger and experimentally induced pain

fit: encapsulated ginger and gastrointestinal symptom scores outside Parkinson disease

fit: ginger root powder and placebo-controlled menstrual pain
assessment: The original abstract reports favorable VAS pain results with both schedules. The study concerns oral powder and primary dysmenorrhea.

fit: powdered ginger and KOOS pain in knee osteoarthritis

fit: isolated alpha-phellandrene and experimental nerve injury in rats

fit: ginger capsules and menstrual pain against an active comparator
assessment: In 122 students, two-cycle maximum pain scores were 43.49 and 38.19 mm for ginger versus 39.01 and 33.75 mm for mefenamic acid (both inconclusive). No placebo arm, equivalence margin, grated ginger intervention or Parkinson pain outcome.

fit: ethanol ginger extract and acute exercise soreness

fit: eight-component formula and abdominal pain

fit: combined herbal extract and abdominal pain outside Parkinson disease
assessment: Abdominal pain favored the mixture. Fresh ginger was not isolated.

fit: standardized ginger extract alongside ketoprofen in acute migraine

assessment: At least 50% fewer attacks in 42% versus 39% after 90 days. Severe-pain days were also inconclusive. Different duration, extract and indication from the acute study.

fit: reported ginger intake and bodily aches in a small Parkinson sample

fit: planned adolescent sleep measures with a mixed oil placebo containing corn oil

fit: sleep quality registered for an energy-matched corn canola and fructose control

fit: registered corn-oil comparator with linked sleep results retracted
assessment: The registry lists PSQI and ESS and shows no structured results. The linked reported results were retracted after data and analysis discrepancies. Registry narrative and repeats of the retracted publication supply no directional result.

assessment: Six-month nighttime behavior p=.69. Corn-oil means 4.9 to 3.7 among item-positive subsets of 33 and 19. Changing denominators and a broad nighttime item leave an insomnia outcome unresolved. No refining grade or no-oil arm.

fit: equal corn-oil carrier in an overnight crossover and objective sleep measures
assessment: In 26 healthy completers, corn-only versus drug-in-corn sleep latency was 13.4 versus 9.8 minutes and wake after sleep onset 46.2 versus 47.10 minutes. Both were inconclusive. PSQI was a screening measure. No oil-free phase, refined grade or Parkinson insomnia diagnosis.

fit: corn oil as capsule placebo in a REM sleep behavior trial
assessment: The primary measures covered REM sleep behavior rather than insomnia. No independent corn oil contrast was available.

fit: corn oil capsules as comparator in a 12-week sleep quality trial
assessment: Endpoint measured efficiency was 96.0% with DHA/EPA versus 93.7% with corn oil, p=.018. Subjective sleep initiation and maintenance had p=.351. The result is a fish-oil comparison in generally healthy adults and does not identify a corn oil effect, refining, or Parkinson insomnia.

fit: topical corn-oil-containing comparator and global sleep quality after herpes zoster
assessment: Comparison-arm mean PSQI 7.83 to 6.25 versus 7.88 to 4.35 in the active arm. Adjusted treatment-comparison difference -1.95 with 95% CI -3.18 to -0.72. Multiple co-ingredients and topical exposure prevent a dietary or independent refined-oil inference.

fit: eggs on a Parkinson example menu and clinical walking speed
assessment: The study measured 0.93 versus 1.06 m/s in Parkinson participants and controls. The illustrative menu had eggs as an option with no egg-specific exposure or speed comparison.

fit: observational tea analysis or prediabetes egg program
assessment: Three members identify the EGGSPDITe egg intervention program in prediabetes, including protocol and remote-delivery snapshots. They do not report a relevant egg effect on the frozen symptom.

fit: egg frequency and perceived slow movement in Parkinson baseline data
assessment: Near-zero inverse sign for general slowness. The report gives no timed walking, poaching or pairwise uncertainty.

fit: poached egg in food-frequency measures and physical performance in older adults
assessment: The physical performance battery included an 8-foot walk with no clear group effect on the composite. The study did not assign individual preparations or report a Parkinson effect.

fit: boiled eggs with a labeled phosphatidylcholine challenge
assessment: The egg challenge concerns gut microbial and blood metabolites. The outcome and preparation are separate from the frozen claim.

fit: egg within varied nonseafood dietary proteins
assessment: Egg is a bundled exposure in the nonseafood dietary pattern. The trial reports lipids instead of falls or gait, and does not isolate poached egg.

fit: shared collection original source context
assessment: Genuine egg exposures appear in food intake surveys and the varied nonseafood arm of PO2.144. The student surveys overlap, and no isolated poached or Parkinson outcome is reported.

fit: shared collection original source context

assessment: The adjusted model treats egg frequency as one predictor of estimated low protein intake. Egg preparation and Parkinson falls and walking speed were not studied. The conference presentation and full article share the same data.

fit: reported chicken and egg label use
assessment: The survey identifies consumer attention to product labels. It does not measure consumption at a controlled preparation or fatigue, falls or gait.

fit: carotenoid food recalls and macular pigment measurements

assessment: C4 studies fertilized egg-yolk extract relative to cheese powder for muscle protein synthesis. The preparation and outcome do not match poached egg and Parkinson falls or walking.

fit: processed egg yolk and tissue synthesis
assessment: Twenty older adults received the yolk fraction or cheese powder. The published 18% synthesis difference concerns tissue metabolism and is not a poached-egg fall or walking outcome.

fit: eggs in a Parkinson diet intervention and composite motor score
assessment: The intervention menu lists eggs and the motor scale includes gait. The study gives no egg preparation, actual exposure, or outcome specific to walking slowness.

fit: weekly egg intake and gait tests reported by osteosarcopenia status
assessment: The author abstract associates weekly egg intake with osteosarcopenia and describes gait by musculoskeletal diagnosis. The available text gives no egg-to-gait estimate or cooking detail. The full article remains gated.

fit: commercial mint oil and post-cesarean flatulence pain
assessment: The abstract favors oral Supermint for procedure-related pain and gives inconsistent participant totals. Species, fresh spearmint and Parkinson pain were unverified.

fit: commercial mint drops and pediatric colonoscopy pain
assessment: The primary paper gives a lower procedure pain score with the product versus no drops. The paper calls the product peppermint, and the study lot species remains unconfirmed.

fit: commercial mint drops and post-cholecystectomy pain
assessment: Early pain contrasts were inconclusive, and the abstract and figure describe differing later directions. The concentrated product is not verified as fresh spearmint.

fit: mixed extracts including spearmint and IBS abdominal pain
assessment: The small placebo comparison reported lower abdominal pain severity p=.016 with the three-extract mixture. Standard treatment also depended on bowel subtype. Fresh spearmint and Parkinson pain were not separately tested.

fit: spearmint oil contact allergy and erosive oral lichen planus
assessment: The retrospective study found 14 cases of erosive oral lichen planus among 19 clinically relevant patch test positives. No fresh leaf or Parkinson pain comparison.

fit: brewed spearmint and osteoarthritis pain
assessment: The high-rosmarinic-acid tea arm reported reduced knee pain from baseline without a significant between-arm contrast. Fresh leaves and Parkinson pain were outside the study.

fit: mint oil capsule with inconsistent botanical identity and epigastric pain
assessment: The mint group reported no epigastric pain during washout. The trial enrolled adults with tuberculosis and does not supply a fresh spearmint pain effect.

fit: whole-diet comparison and a qualitative OFF-time report
assessment: One participant described prolonged OFF time after a high-fat meal during the ketogenic period. The trial does not isolate refined coconut oil or report a separate daily OFF-time treatment contrast.

fit: coconut oil as an example in self-reported Parkinson OFF coping strategies
assessment: The Fox Insight survey included 2,110 respondents with OFF periods and 1,416 free-text coping responses. Coconut oil is one example in the six-response supplements category. No oil-specific count, processing grade, comparator or measured change in daily OFF time is reported.

fit: fractionated oil and ordinal daily off-time ratings
assessment: The standard-diet group had higher off-time scores, including at baseline. This whole-diet comparison does not isolate refined coconut oil.

fit: confirmed saffron odor in a post-traumatic rotating regimen
assessment: The 2024 companion Methods identify saffron in month three, together with other odors. The 2021 report evaluates the full program, with no separate saffron contrast or oral Parkinson exposure.

fit: hyposmic non-PD cohort; orange and saffron extracts in salt; taste outcome
assessment: Flavor mixture was tested for taste perception, not treatment-related olfactory severity; no stand-alone ground saffron effect or PD comparison.

fit: Peach juice carrier in healthy volunteer antipsychotic protocol; planned drug-induced postural instability measure
assessment: Juice is used in all drug and placebo arms; no peach contrast, no raw fruit, no idiopathic Parkinson disease, and no posted results.

fit: Multi-food low-fat Parkinson menu includes optional peach and a pre-existing falls case
assessment: Composite motor scores and one participant with pre-existing postural hypotension and ongoing falls do not isolate peach or establish a direction for postural instability.

fit: Parkinson vegetarian diet appendix lists peach; UPDRS III encompasses postural stability
assessment: Peach intake, raw preparation, individual postural score, and an ingredient-specific comparison are not reported; outcome is multi-food composite.

fit: Independent flaxseed-derived omega-3 and vitamin E trial with motor components
assessment: The 40-person trial gives Part III −1.9 versus +3.1, printed p=.05. The official initial and revised IRCT versions both omit UPDRS and differ on intervention quantities and location. No separate rest item, pressing method or differential oil-only arm is reported.

fit: Flaxseed-derived omega-3 plus vitamin E and Parkinson total UPDRS
assessment: Total UPDRS change was −3.3 versus +4.4, p=.02, with vitamin E coadministered. Clinical UPDRS first appears in the available 2019 revision after publication. The paper gives no rest item, cold-press grade or motor-exam medication state.

fit: plasma alpha-linolenic acid and examiner-rated Parkinson resting tremor
assessment: Rest tremor ρ = .059 (p = .728) adjusted for age and .034 (p = .842) adjusted for sex. The cross-sectional exposure was plasma ALA, with no test of flaxseed oil.

fit: possible cold-pressed flaxseed blend in an uncontrolled combined Parkinson regimen
assessment: The filing reports tremor reduction in Case 4, with resting tremor present before treatment. The case combined oral and intravenous treatment and provides no isolated oil comparison or standardized follow-up tremor measurement.

assessment: The 2025 report follows the same maternal capsule study as PMID36130610. Neonatal swab testing examines facial responses to odors. The study does not measure a change in adult olfactory impairment, roasted kale exposure or Parkinson outcomes.

fit: mashed potato and registered acute sleepiness in a pediatric crossover
assessment: A 22-child six-meal crossover registers a repeated sleepiness item. The plausibly linked primary abstract describes frozen and microwaved mash and supplies no item result. Boiling, full source linkage and exact sleepiness results remain unverified.

fit: acute emotion inventory in a baked or fried potato protocol
assessment: The acute emotion measure includes sleepiness. This recruiting protocol uses baked and fried foods in adults without a Parkinson comparison. Boiled potato is absent.

fit: potato chips compared with pistachios with daytime sleep related impairment
assessment: A recruiting study in midlife women compares potato chips and pistachios and registers daytime effects of sleepiness. No posted results, boiled potato, or Parkinson cohort.

fit: separate baked and fried potato meal protocol with sleep-related measures
assessment: The second REB experiment separately registers an acute sleepiness item plus next-morning sleep quality. The recruiting record provides no results, confirmed participant overlap or boiled potato assignment.

fit: Parkinson diet plan includes potatoes simmered in mixed meals and reports a daytime sleepiness item
assessment: Whole-diet randomized contrast; individual potato intake and meal timing are unknown, preparation is part of mixed soup or hotpot, and the sleepiness item is not a food-specific comparison.

fit: Dietary follow-up includes Epworth sleepiness and classifies potato/corn chips
assessment: Cohorts excluded Parkinson history and exposure is broad ultraprocessed patterns; chips classified separately, no boiled potato or clinical Parkinson symptom comparison.

fit: Registered potato-salad meal comparison includes two postprandial sleepiness measures
assessment: Healthy men, unspecified potato preparation and consumption, altered bread and added dextrin; registry fields conflict on randomization and results are unpublished.

fit: dried sage diagnostic smell identification
assessment: Workbook counts are 2/34 Parkinson and 6/53 controls. The paper found no clear group difference for sage. The test used sniffing and gives no clinical result after eating ground sage.

fit: common sage oil inhalation in participants selected for unimpaired smell
assessment: The original trial evaluated aromatherapy and inpatient satisfaction. Unimpaired olfaction was an inclusion criterion, not a measured response to consuming ground sage.

fit: Combined distressing dreams and hallucinations item in Parkinson disease
assessment: One participant changed from 2 to 0 during aroma massage on the combined item. The other three stayed at zero. Dream enactment was not separately observed and there was no brewed tea exposure.

fit: mixed lemongrass–lemon drink and categorical postpartum sleep duration
assessment: The report presents closely matching figures as both a group and a before–after comparison. The study has no matched placebo, isolated herb, Parkinson cohort or observed REM behavior endpoint.

fit: Randomized inhaled oil comparison of global sleep quality in smokers
assessment: The young adult smoker cohort improved on global PSQI with essential oil versus sunflower oil control. There was no separate dream enactment outcome, oral tea or Parkinson cohort.

fit: Brewed leaf tea with dream recall and nightmares in volunteers
assessment: Fifty volunteers reported sleep and dream recall after two active preparations and a placebo. The authors found no clear differences. Dream enactment, polysomnography and a Parkinson cohort were absent.

fit: registered mixed topical lotion and global sleep quality outside Parkinson disease
assessment: Single-arm topical lotion includes Cymbopogon flexuosus oil and citral, plus melatonin and other components. The registry gives 35 actual participants and no posted results. SQS and Fitbit do not measure enacted dreams or REM without atonia. No brewed tea.

fit: oral leaf infusion in laboratory sleep tests with a separate injected citral comparison
assessment: The complete Part I body reports no tea potentiation of pentobarbital-induced sleep and no change in rat slow-wave or REM EEG measures. Injected isolated citral was the positive sleep-potentiation comparison. The digitized EEG dose labels disagree. The study provides no observation of enacted dreams or Parkinson-specific outcome.

fit: lemongrass flavor in the comparison drink and adverse-event reporting
assessment: One nightmare was reported in the active mixture group and none in the flavored comparator. Flavor species and dose are unverified. There was no standalone lemongrass comparison or dream-enactment measure.

fit: mixed fragrances with lemongrass notes and REM dream emotionality
assessment: Two of 20 participants used different lemongrass-labelled mixed cartridges. Pooled dream emotionality comparisons were inconclusive. No ingredient-specific contrast, witnessed enactment, brewed tea or Parkinson population.

fit: injected distilled lemongrass oil and barbiturate-induced sleep in rats
assessment: Table 6 reports longer drug-induced sleep for the oil group. Methods and table caption list different barbiturate doses. Induced sleep duration is distinct from witnessed dream enactment or REM without atonia.

fit: processed seed-derived glucoraphanin; broad PD outcomes
assessment: The compound intervention is not raw kale and no urinary urgency frequency result is posted.

fit: both mixed-diet plans list kale or spinach; broad urinary item
assessment: The low-fat plan offers uncooked kale or spinach in a smoothie and the ketogenic plan offers sauteed kale or spinach; individual choices are unverified. The ketogenic versus low-fat urinary-problems item change differed by -0.70 points, without a raw-kale contrast or urgency-frequency estimate.

fit: food-frequency chili intake and composite including timed walking
assessment: Usual-pace four-meter walking was measured, and chili intake was assessed separately from sweet pepper. The study published chili estimates for the composite sarcopenia definition, without a chili-specific walking estimate or ground preparation.

fit: oral red chili extract and treadmill endurance
assessment: Time to exhaustion was longer with extract. Velocity was set before each graded test, so ordinary walking slowness could not be estimated. The intervention was a formulated extract in healthy overweight adults.

fit: cayenne capsules and electronically measured maximal sprint speed
assessment: Nineteen healthy athletes showed similar fastest and average repeated sprint times during commercial cayenne and placebo. Combined gastrointestinal symptoms increased. No ordinary walking assessment or Parkinson sample.

fit: herb named in a mixed Parkinson menu
assessment: Lovage is among the menu ingredients with no individual apathy outcome or verified drying status.

fit: individual Parkinson symptoms and diet scores
assessment: Apathy associations were inconclusive at the pattern level and no dried lovage item was analyzed.

fit: MPTP mouse model; dried whole-plant methanolic extract; motor tasks
assessment: Mouse beam and drag measures do not assess dystonia in people consuming fresh leaves.

fit: rice bran in a multicomponent fiber bar
assessment: The open-label study found no clear constipation or bowel-frequency change after the bar. It provides no refined rice bran oil contrast.

fit: defatted rice bran and stool form in adults
assessment: Normal stool-form prevalence increased after defatted bran. The formulation is fiber-containing and defatted, and the participants did not have Parkinson disease.

fit: rice bran oil in a four-oil blend and stool measures
assessment: The blend improved stool outcomes in loperamide-treated mice. Rice bran oil comprised 26.02%, with no individual oil arm or Parkinson population.

fit: registered fermented rice bran bowel diary trial
assessment: The trial follows bowel movement counts and stool consistency, with results unpublished. The intervention is fermented bran food in generally healthy adults.

fit: Pimenta dioica alcoholic leaf extract and motor toxicity in mice
assessment: Original oral toxicity observations include sedation and motor incoordination. The authors discuss alcohol. The preparation, animal behavior and lack of a hand task leave the frozen handwriting outcome unresolved.

fit: chive leaf extract and cognition after cerebral ischemia in mice
assessment: The experiment reports behavioral changes in a stroke model. It gives no executive-function outcome for people with Parkinson disease who consume fresh chives.

fit: oral oil vehicle and objective REM-atonia measures in a tauopathy model
assessment: Among nine PS19 mice with an REM behavior disorder phenotype, DORA-12 lowered percentage REM without atonia relative to peanut oil vehicle (p = .004). The report gives no separate effect of oil or declared grade.

fit: oral drug formulation and REM stage duration in an Alzheimer model
assessment: Diphenhydramine increased dark-phase REM time relative to vehicle (p = .0365). Oil was named in the oral formulation, and the study supplies no isolated oil contrast or dream enactment data.

fit: posted aggregate MCCB results in the Wynn oral curcumin trial
assessment: Official results give composite changes, with no separate attention-domain estimate. Registry and Wynn article describe one cohort.

fit: curcumin and registered MMSE outcome
assessment: The outcome labeled attention and memory used MMSE. Curcumin had a more favorable numerical change, without a statistical comparison or isolated attention score.

fit: solid lipid curcumin and healthy older adult digit vigilance
assessment: One-hour accuracy comparison p=.046, demographic-adjusted p=.168. The difference was no longer apparent at three hours.

fit: whole turmeric capsules and working memory
assessment: Single-dose whole turmeric at breakfast produced a borderline working-memory finding in older adults with prediabetes. No distinct attention measure or fresh grated preparation.

fit: BCM-95 turmeric formulation and repeated cognition tasks outside Parkinson disease
assessment: Original analyses show no clear attention-containing task change between arms and an inconclusive baseline to 12-month MoCA interaction (p=.25).

fit: oral Theracurmin versus placebo and a secondary timed attention proxy
assessment: Trail A time fell from 32.6 to 24.9 seconds versus 30.5 to 28.4 in nondemented adults (interaction p=.04). The formulation and timed task do not isolate a culinary effect on Parkinson attention.

fit: twice assessed Flanker inhibition and attention in healthy adults
assessment: Table 3 shows identical rounded trajectories for both groups (8.3 to 8.5, interaction p=.97). The comparison provides a counterweight to isolated positive supplement findings.

fit: same cohort as terminated NCT02476708 with attention/vigilance measured
assessment: Original Table 1 reports mean changes +9.20 versus −6.80, five per arm and p=.209. Reported preparation and active dose differ from the official registry capsule regimen.

fit: curry intake and cognitive attention proxies
assessment: Backward digit span differed across curry intake groups without a clear group-by-time interaction. The survey did not isolate turmeric or Parkinson.

fit: oral phospholipid curcumin in a nonrandomized Parkinson cohort
assessment: Full tables report total NMSS without a separate attention result. MMSE was a screening criterion.

fit: nanomicellar oral curcumin randomized in Parkinson disease
assessment: Primary abstract and registry do not give an attention item or distinct attention contrast. Original full results remain open.

fit: turmeric extract and eye-tracking attention
assessment: A small adult trial found a favorable exploratory eye-tracking result, alongside inconclusive computerized attention and primary composite memory measures.

fit: grapeseed nanocapsule core and antipsychotic-related oral dyskinesia in rats
assessment: An injected drug formulation with a grapeseed oil core partly attenuated acute involuntary chewing, and all loaded nanoformulations attenuated it after repeated dosing. Dystonia severity and oral culinary exposure were not tested.

fit: injected isolated eugenol and pentobarbital loss of righting
assessment: Eugenol prolonged the barbiturate-induced loss-of-righting interval (p=.002). Spontaneous sleep, insomnia and oral ground allspice were unmeasured.

fit: eugenol formulations and behavior after induced REM loss
assessment: The rat study measured post-deprivation sensorimotor and learning tasks. It provides no sleep recovery or insomnia estimate for ground allspice.

fit: contrasting associations of serum carrot-associated carotenoids with sleepiness in general adults
assessment: In NHANES Table 4 Model 2, sleepiness factors were inversely associated with serum alpha-carotene and positively associated with beta-carotene. Other specifications were inconclusive. No raw carrot intervention, Parkinson cohort or separate Epworth estimate was involved.

fit: diet-pattern scores and excessive sleepiness before diagnosis
assessment: Higher pattern scores were associated with lower odds of excessive daytime sleepiness. The cohort excluded diagnosed Parkinson's and the exposure was a whole diet score.

fit: diet-pattern scores and measured Parkinson daytime sleepiness
assessment: The Parkinson analysis did not report a significant diet-pattern association with daytime sleepiness or separate raw carrot.

fit: plant-rich and time-restricted nutrition with Epworth scores in people with Parkinson disease
assessment: The six-month trial's Table 2 shows Epworth means 6.65 to 6.5 in controls and 6.55 to 6.7 with personalized nutrition, with post-test p=1.000. The whole program had several components and the report supplies no carrot-specific intake or contrast.

fit: isolated eugenol and mouse immobility
assessment: The primary abstract describes antidepressant-like performance in forced swim and tail suspension tests, with hippocampal biomarkers. The food exposure and a patient mood outcome remain unmeasured.

fit: oral isolated eugenol and rodent behavior
assessment: Fourteen days of isolated eugenol was associated with no significant behavioral changes in a mouse safety study including tail suspension. The design provides no Parkinson or culinary estimate.

fit: isolated eugenol nanoemulsion and rodent behavior
assessment: Intranasal delivery using a clove-oil phase changed locomotor and forced-swim outcomes. Motor effects and formulation limit inference for ground allspice or Parkinson mood.

fit: oral isolated eugenol and depression-like outcomes after paraquat
assessment: The primary abstract reports improvement in social interaction and tail-suspension immobility after toxin exposure, without numerical behavioral estimates. Literature linkage and culinary Parkinson exposure remain unresolved.

fit: injected allspice leaf extract and rat CNS suppression
assessment: Fresh leaf extracts injected in rats decreased general CNS activity. The 14-day oral fraction experiment measured pressure, heart rate and weight. Neither reported depressive behavior or ground allspice berries.

fit: proprietary melon juice concentrate and stress-related fatigue
assessment: The four-week trial reported lower fatigue-related questionnaire scores with a melon concentrate. Participants were otherwise healthy and no raw cantaloupe arm was used.

fit: melon SOD and gliadin in women with self-perceived fatigue
assessment: General fatigue decreased 1.6% with supplement and 4.1% with placebo, an inconclusive comparison. Neither raw fruit nor Parkinson was studied.

fit: palm-oil-coated melon concentrate and physical fatigue
assessment: The physical fatigue scale favored the extract at day 84 and was inconclusive at day 28. The trial tested a proprietary capsule in healthy adults, with no raw fruit or Parkinson group.

fit: melon concentrate, exercise and subjective fatigue
assessment: The healthy exercise study found no clear between-group fatigue difference. Melon concentrate was given alongside training rather than as raw fruit.

fit: Vauclusien melon extract and Chalder fatigue in locomotive syndrome
assessment: Six-month Chalder fatigue change was inconclusive (p = .15). The product contains melon SOD and gliadin, and the participants did not have Parkinson.

fit: strain-defined fermented milk
assessment: The trial found constipation and aggregate nonmotor signals with the specific preparation.

fit: oral turmeric powder added to naproxen and menstrual pain
assessment: Reported VAS reductions 7.0 versus 5.6 (p<.001). The unblinded article describes two groups and 149 analyzed. Linked registration says randomized crossover and 90 actual. Neither source resolves the discrepancy.

fit: curcumin extract and pain outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The baseline-adjusted SF-36 pain contrast was unclear. The intervention was a standardized extract.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: P-14-005 studies a joint cinnamon and turmeric-extract blend. Other posters concern isolated curcumin in prostate cancer or cell and platelet experiments. No Parkinson symptom comparison is supplied.

fit: isolated curcumin pretreatment in cultured human endothelial cells
assessment: The original congress member reports curcumin among inhibitors of linoleate-induced LOX-1 expression. The later abstract describes classes of inhibitors. The cell outcome does not answer a culinary turmeric symptom claim.

fit: isolated curcumin and hepatic glucose production
assessment: The later article reports lower glucose production and lower PEPCK activity in a specified condition. The related original abstract reports no PEPCK effect. Experimental differences and any link to culinary turmeric remain unresolved.

fit: curcumin extract alongside a weight-loss diet in PCOS
assessment: No separate Parkinson symptom or culinary turmeric result was recorded. Within-group metabolic changes do not establish a between-group clinical response.

fit: turmeric-colored bread and child sensory preference
assessment: Children chose yellow bread less often. The study concerns colour and liking, without a swallowing or other relevant clinical endpoint.

fit: oral isolated curcumin and thermal pain tests in diabetic mice
assessment: The primary abstract reports attenuation of evoked thermal hyperalgesia in a diabetic mouse model after isolated curcumin. This does not give a pain effect in Parkinson disease after ground turmeric.

fit: Curcuma longa in a 14-component granule
assessment: An exploratory headache outcome was measured under a combined formula. Ground turmeric and general pain were not isolated.

fit: BCM-95 curcuminoids and pain in rheumatoid arthritis
assessment: Within-arm visual-analog pain scores improved in all three active groups. No inactive placebo or between-group pain estimate establishes how ground turmeric affects Parkinson-related pain.

fit: injected isolated curcumin and inflammatory nociception in mice
assessment: Later-phase formalin licking and separate writhing were reduced. Early-phase formalin findings were inconclusive. Injection, constituent and species differ from the frozen claim.

fit: combined herbal extract and abdominal pain outside Parkinson disease
assessment: Abdominal pain favored the mixture. Ground turmeric was not isolated.

fit: isolated curcumin and tactile allodynia after laboratory nerve injury
assessment: The original body reports lower mechanical allodynia in animal oral and intrathecal curcumin comparisons. Whole culinary turmeric and clinical pain were not measured.

fit: combined ginger and turmeric powder extracts and rat joint pain
assessment: Reports attenuation in an animal osteoarthritis model after combined ginger and turmeric extract. Individual turmeric effect is unidentifiable.

fit: pooled supplement exposure and composite outcome
assessment: Adjusted cross-sectional association favored lower aggregate scores. The preparation and pain were not isolated.

fit: turmeric and pepper powder in an uncontrolled diet study of rheumatic chronic pain
assessment: The 45-participant four-month pilot supplied a commercial combination powder while changing food intake. Pain NRS declined in 30. An exploratory turmeric-score association with pain was marked p<.10 in Figure 3 and occurred within the multicomponent regimen. The study gives no isolated ground turmeric or Parkinson pain estimate.

fit: exposure survey
assessment: Respondents reported turmeric use. The survey did not estimate a pain effect.

fit: bioavailable turmeric formulation and exercise soreness outside Parkinson disease
assessment: NCT04946981 compared Turmipure Gold with placebo in 44 moderately active adults. Primary 72-hour soreness AUC did not clearly differ and a post hoc maximum-to-72-hour recovery contrast favored the formulation. The published models differ from the original baseline-adjusted plan. The intervention is a formulated extract and the cohort does not estimate Parkinson pain. Conference abstract OAP36_02 is the same trial.

fit: placebo-controlled pilot of whole turmeric powder and hand osteoarthritis pain
assessment: Primary one-month group comparison inconclusive. Later p=.032 and .017 are within-arm baseline comparisons. Raw and modeled changes need reconciliation, and a separate significant between-arm estimate is unavailable.

fit: ground turmeric in both sequences of a chronic-pain crossover
assessment: Pain scores declined over time in 29 adults receiving the same ground turmeric regimen. The comparison changes pepper addition (p=.157), with no turmeric-free control and no Parkinson-specific estimate.

fit: practitioner-reported turmeric capsule
assessment: The questionnaire specifies an enhanced-absorption turmeric capsule. It reports no patient-level pain measure.

fit: reported spice intake and bodily aches in a small Parkinson sample
assessment: The thesis names açafrão, which can refer to turmeric or saffron, among foods said to relieve aches. Species, preparation, count by ingredient, and Parkinson-related pain severity are unreported.

fit: whole walnut snack and short-term salivary flow
assessment: Flow did not clearly increase after the walnut snack. This is whole-nut chewing in 12 adults and salivary production, with no drooling score or Parkinson population.

fit: sweet basil leaf extract and measured insomnia in menopause
assessment: Sixty participants were randomized in a menopausal population. At one month, reported insomnia scores were 5.6 versus 11.0 (p<.001). The study used an extract and no Parkinson cohort.

fit: dried aerial-part powder and postpartum sleep quality
assessment: The powder and placebo groups had total postpartum sleep scores of 17.63 and 16.15 (adjusted p=.400). The study used dried aerial parts and overall postpartum sleep quality, without a Parkinson insomnia measure.

fit: injected isolated myrcene and pentobarbital sleep in mice
assessment: Mean time under pentobarbital was 40.9 minutes in controls and 64.0 and 106.6 after injected isolated myrcene. Motor performance also declined. The food preparation and spontaneous sleep remained untested.

fit: oral isolated myrcene and pentobarbital sleep in rats
assessment: A single dose prolonged barbiturate sleep and repeated dosing with a different challenge interval shortened it. Authors attribute the timing-dependent results to drug metabolism. No culinary ingestion or spontaneous insomnia was measured.

fit: human leaf-volatiles and visual vigilance
assessment: Low-exposure inhalation preserved a late true-hit index, and high exposure had a faster reaction time at one time point. Other subjective responses differed.

fit: whole-leaf incense and animal cognition
assessment: The exposed scopolamine group had better measures of spatial memory. It did not receive ground leaf by mouth or model Parkinson attention.

fit: bay leaf volatiles and visual vigilance in an earlier controlled human report
assessment: At the lower odor load the reported 30-minute contrast had p=.026. The higher load did not clearly differ. Shared team and task leave participant overlap with the later report unresolved. The exposure was inhaled.

fit: nigella-derived melanin and registered reflux endpoints
assessment: Registry specifies GERD-Q and general safety, without a distinct dysphagia measure or whole-ground seed assignment. No posted results.

fit: nigella oil mouth rinse and self-reported oral intake during chemotherapy
assessment: Table 2 reports favorable early normal-food tolerance and 26/27 versus 20/25 normal-diet counts on day 28 (p=.159). One nigella recipient was on a liquid diet, qualifying the broad abstract assertion. Topical oil in mucositis does not test ingested ground seed or neurogenic swallowing.

fit: self-selected Parkinson records with ground white mustard in a mixed seed tea
assessment: The 2024 primary report names ground white mustard in the preparation. Symptoms were self-rated and could be modified. Selected records omit any visual hallucination frequency result and the study did not isolate mustard.

fit: pediatric kidney bean allergy and cross-reactivity
assessment: The children experienced immediate hives or facial swelling following ingestion. The observations do not measure Parkinson drooling or visual hallucinations.

fit: pooled legume or bean intake and whole-diet general hallucinations scores
assessment: Table 2 reports general hallucinations against whole diet scores. Table S4 evaluates pooled bean or legume intake against aggregate symptom burden and does not identify species or preparation. It does not quantify visual hallucination frequency.

fit: acute gastrointestinal illness after inadequately cooked kidney beans
assessment: The outbreak investigation supports an undercooking-related gastrointestinal exposure. It did not monitor hallucination frequency or ordinary cooked kidney bean ingestion in Parkinson's.

fit: fresh green kiwi and subjective waking alertness
assessment: Fresh kiwi yielded 53.1 versus 44.2 for water (p = .082) on waking alertness. The trial had no objective attention test or Parkinson cohort.

fit: freeze-dried kiwi and planned computerized cognitive testing
assessment: The registry plans COMPASS cognitive testing after evening freeze-dried kiwi in men with poor sleep. No published result, raw kiwi arm or Parkinson population is recorded.

fit: previously frozen green kiwi pulp and attention tasks in healthy adults
assessment: The breakfast crossover found no clear treatment or treatment-by-time effect on choice reaction time or Stroop. ACTRN12615001259538 records the same tests. The linked Mishra metabolic report describes 200 g peeled Hayward pulp stored frozen and re-frozen after crushing. The crossover compared cereal meals in healthy volunteers and gives no Parkinson-specific estimate.

fit: green versus gold kiwi meal and porcine brain bioamines
assessment: The author abstract and matching dissertation experiment describe 48 pigs, post-meal GABA and other bioamine trajectories by cultivar. Tissue analysis is a biochemical endpoint, not a human attention performance measure. The two cultivar meals also differ in fiber and other nutrients.

fit: hoarseness during supervised whole roasted hazelnut challenges in children
assessment: Table 1 records hoarseness in three children during food challenges with finely ground roasted whole hazelnuts. The separate oil-body experiments used immunoblotting. The clinical study provides no cold-pressed edible-oil challenge, acoustic loudness measure or Parkinson cohort.

fit: pooled voice and throat symptoms in a pediatric food-allergy cohort
assessment: Dysphonia, pruritus or throat constriction occurred in 22 of 88 children in a pooled food-allergy cohort. Results were not attributable to a single food or separately to reduced vocal loudness. The study did not use cold-pressed hazelnut oil or enroll Parkinson patients.

fit: lipidated curcumin, PSQI daytime dysfunction and older adults
assessment: Table S12 shows 1/38 versus 9/38 worsened at week 12 and 1/38 versus 2/38 improved, with p=.018 for the full category comparison. Daytime dysfunction is a combined component and no separate Epworth or item result was identified.

fit: Parkinson curcumin and overall sleep quality
assessment: Nanomicelle curcumin improved global PSQI in a small trial. ESS or daytime-dysfunction component scores were not reported.

fit: turmeric-extract combination and registered PSQI daytime dysfunction
assessment: Biomarker-selected chronic pain intervention combines turmeric, black pepper, ashwagandha and olive-leaf extracts. Registry adds no observed daytime functioning or sleepiness data.

fit: rhizome capsules and sleepiness reports
assessment: EMA's account of the trial describes sleepiness reported across turmeric and comparison groups, with no arm-specific count or validated scale.

fit: turmeric extract and mouse sleep promotion
assessment: Oral extract shortened sleep latency and increased non-REM sleep in mice. Daytime sleepiness and Parkinson disease were not assessed.

fit: curcumin and Epworth daytime sleepiness
assessment: A randomized curcumin study outside Parkinson found inconclusive Epworth and severity results. Both arms received piperine.

fit: oral aqueous tarragon extract and sprint performance
assessment: The recreationally trained men received creatine in both crossover periods. Peak power, mean power and work had no clear group-by-time interaction. Clinical fatigue and dried culinary tarragon were unmeasured.

fit: ethanolic tarragon extract and voluntary exercise metabolism
assessment: Obese mice receiving extract had greater fat oxidation during matched wheel-running bouts. The study does not provide a fatigue outcome and the published corrigendum is open.

fit: corn oil vehicle shared by both estradiol comparison arms in rats
assessment: The author abstract attributes odor discrimination and recovery differences to the estradiol comparison on a common injection background.

fit: corn oil preference by mouse olfactory-model status
assessment: Experimentally altered olfaction preceded the oil-choice task. Normal mice preferred a wider concentration range. The study does not estimate smell changes after oil intake.

fit: corn oil feed and measured canine odor thresholds
assessment: Behavioral olfactometry tested corn, coconut and beef-tallow diets with conditioning strata. The reported deterioration concerned unconditioned dogs on coconut oil. Trial results do not establish corn-induced worsening.

fit: maize oil addition and canine odor detection crossover
assessment: Maize oil diet improved adjusted near-threshold detection against a distinct high-fat diet. Comparisons with the original low-fat maintenance diet and tests of absolute odor thresholds showed no clear differences. Refining and Parkinson disease were unmeasured.

fit: corn oil injection sham in mouse olfactory training
assessment: The reported pellet-finding times separate injury and training arms from an injected sham. No oil-only dietary comparison.

fit: injected corn oil vehicle and measured mouse olfaction
assessment: The control and toxin groups had matched injected corn oil. Olfactory differences reflect toxin or training contrasts on a shared vehicle background.

fit: low
assessment: The original supplement shows total UPDRS III trajectories at fourteen days. It does not supply a hand-task, pegboard, oil-grade, or individual oil intake comparison in the Parkinson diet trial.

fit: low
assessment: Mung bean extract prepared in heated pumpkin oil was compared with separate soybean oil extracts and other treatments. The authors report wire-hanging and falls during the task. Neither arm isolates oil, and suspension endurance differs from hand dexterity.

fit: low
assessment: A Cucurbita extract improved rat rotarod coordination in a cuprizone model. The primary abstract does not identify culinary oil. Rotarod performance and the demyelination model differ from hand dexterity in Parkinson’s.

fit: dried marjoram as a sensory stimulus
assessment: Only 31% recognized the single odor despite some participants reporting culinary use. This does not compare a change in general olfaction after ingestion.

fit: dried marjoram diagnostic smell identification
assessment: Workbook counts are 1/34 Parkinson and 5/53 controls. The paper found no clear group difference for marjoram. The test used sniffing and gives no clinical result after eating dried marjoram.

fit: topical fresh dill preparation and hemodialysis sleep quality
assessment: The trial reported lower follow-up Pittsburgh sleep scores with topical dill than with comparators, with inconsistent baseline reporting. The route, preparation, sleep measure and dialysis population differ from the frozen claim.

fit: reduced spontaneous locomotion after injected dill extracts
assessment: Dose-dependent locomotor changes are described as sedative, with no direct sleep or insomnia assessment. Part and preparation differ.

fit: oral dill tablet and premenstrual sleep quality
assessment: The study reported better Pittsburgh sleep scores for dill tablets than placebo. Plant part was unreported, and general sleep quality in premenstrual syndrome does not measure Parkinson insomnia.

fit: dill extract beverage and registered sleep quality outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The official record lists Thai PSQI as a six-week secondary outcome and gives no published arm results. This is sleep quality under an extract beverage.

fit: related Zanthoxylum oil inhalation with exercise and postural sway
assessment: The eyes-closed velocity comparison favored intervention at four weeks and follow-up. Dynamic reach and fear of falling had inconclusive interactions. Related species and inhalation do not identify ground Sichuan pepper.

fit: related pepper species and animal coordination proxy
assessment: Distilled Japanese pepper given intranasally increased time on the rotating rod in mice. The study did not measure Parkinson postural instability after culinary exposure.

fit: oral soybean-oil placebo and measured vocal tremor modulation
assessment: The essential voice tremor crossover quantified sustained-vowel amplitude modulation during the soybean-oil placebo and active periods. The methods omit oil grade and the study does not estimate habitual vocal loudness in Parkinson disease.

fit: Injected cineole and non-cardamom leaf oil in mice; haloperidol catalepsy rather than dystonia
assessment: Potentiated experimental catalepsy is not evidence ground culinary cardamom worsens Parkinson dystonia; primary abstract only.

fit: Oral cyclodextrin-complexed isolated cineole in reserpine mice; bar catalepsy rather than dystonia
assessment: Reduced induced catalepsy in a different model, formulation and route cannot establish a change in clinical dystonia after ground cardamom.

fit: hoarseness with competing anatomical cause in one adult who ate blueberries
assessment: Hoarseness progressed despite blueberry cessation and imaging found an anterior mediastinal mass with partial tracheal compression. The case supplies no verified berry preparation, acoustic voice-volume measure, causal allergy challenge, or Parkinson cohort.

fit: blueberry powder in juice and different outcome
assessment: A possible preliminary gait report was located. No voice-volume estimate is available.

fit: mixed diet allows frozen blueberries; aggregate motor score
assessment: Menus allow frozen berries but actual selection is unverified; motor total does not separately quantify voice volume or blueberry effects.

fit: isolated green-leaf chalcone and behavior in a 6-OHDA mouse model
assessment: Intracerebral DDC improved broad behavior measures and reduced neuronal loss. The available report gives no specific rigidity outcome or dietary leaf exposure.

fit: strain-defined fermented milk
assessment: The trial provides composite motor and nonmotor data for a distinct intervention.

fit: firm yogurt used as a diagnostic bolus
assessment: The study compared existing swallowing performance in patients and controls. Strained yogurt and handwriting were untested.

fit: yogurt drink used as a diagnostic bolus
assessment: The test evaluated whether a voice change indicated airway penetration or aspiration. The report supplies no handwriting effect.

fit: yogurt as a diagnostic comparator
assessment: Yogurt was a diagnostic comparison material and no separate effect on handwriting was measured.

fit: yogurt as a diagnostic swallowing bolus
assessment: The mixed neurological sample used a diagnostic bolus. The study did not estimate strained yogurt and handwriting change.

fit: raw apple or dried rings in a whole diet and composite motor outcome
assessment: Food diaries tracked raw apples or dried rings. The 114-page supplement gives a high versus low fiber comparison using Part III totals. No separate apple intervention or rest-tremor item is reported.

fit: Apples with peel among choices in the Dutch BrAIN diet crossover
assessment: The protocol lists apples with peel among unprocessed or frozen fruit choices. The registry reports no significant effect on the overall motor score, without an apple assignment or a separate rest-tremor estimate.

fit: standardized peeled apple chewing task in medicated Parkinson participants and controls
assessment: Both groups chewed apple. The table compares chewing EMG, relative contraction and workload, and the cohort overlaps the 2023 Copenhagen paper under NCT05356845. It gives no apple-specific change in resting tremor.

fit: apple consumption task and separate rest-tremor measurement

fit: common-sage extract chemistry and antiproliferative experiment

fit: sage extract and mouse footprint geometry
assessment: Sciatic function improved. The test supplies no measure of falls.

fit: Parkinson randomized trial administers common sage leaves

assessment: Mean urgency severity fell by 1.6 and 1.9 points at days 7 and 37 in patients with urinary infection. No control arm, episodes of urgency, separate leaf exposure or Parkinson group. Registry and paper describe one cohort.

fit: lovage root combination and acute cystitis urgency severity
assessment: The same phase III cohort showed falling urgency severity in both acute cystitis arms. The herbal arm received a root mixture and the assessment did not measure frequency after dried lovage leaf in people with Parkinson disease.

fit: dried oregano infusion and drug-induced hypnosis in mice
assessment: At the higher infusion dose pentobarbital-induced hypnosis was longer. Spontaneous daytime sleepiness was not measured.

fit: standardized oregano extract and overnight polysomnography in healthy men
assessment: The patent and 2012 conference abstract describe one crossover cohort. Sleep architecture showed no apparent change and the experiment did not measure clinical daytime sleepiness.

fit: oral avocado oil and systemic pressure in hypertensive rats
assessment: Systolic and diastolic pressure were lower in treated hypertensive rats. The study measured neither an orthostatic response nor subjective lightheadedness.

fit: oral avocado oil and pressure in hypertensive and normotensive rats
assessment: Avocado oil lowered pressure in hypertensive rats and had no clear effect in normotensive rats. This does not measure orthostatic symptoms or the frozen refined-oil exposure.

fit: oral avocado oil and blood pressure in adults with metabolic syndrome
assessment: The official result says blood pressure did not clearly change compared with soybean oil. It supplies no postural pressure, symptoms, Parkinson cohort or refined-oil designation.

fit: Four Parkinson participants reported clarity of writing
assessment: Table 15 writing-clarity scores remained 0, 0, 1 and 1 across all conditions. Character size was not measured and the exposure was inhaled or topical oil.

fit: bok choy grouped with dark-green vegetables in a prospective falls cohort
assessment: The questionnaire listed bok choy in a combined dark-green vegetable category. Among 953 Taiwanese postmenopausal women, 183 fell and 25 had low-impact fractures. The report gives no separate effect for bok choy, no cooking detail and no Parkinson postural testing.

fit: thyme-containing mixed diet; aggregate motor daily living score
assessment: Both menus include thyme in cooked recipes; Part II contains handwriting but no item-specific micrographia or fresh thyme effect is reported.

fit: low
assessment: Oral essential-oil pretreatment worsened mouse motor coordination under midazolam challenge. Rotating-rod motor performance after a sedative drug differs from a hand dexterity test, and whole ground seed remained untested.

fit: enriched rice bran oil and rat stride length
assessment: Footprint stride length improved in treated haloperidol rats. Chamuangone and oil were assigned together, with no plain refined oil arm or human stride result.

fit: cod fillet hydrolysate and grip strength in older adults
assessment: A blinded older-adult trial found no clear grip-strength difference with the hydrolysate. It did not test handwriting size, grilled cod, or a Parkinson group.

fit: PD low-fat mixed menu includes raw cucumber as replaceable salad ingredient; individual consumption and posture item unavailable
assessment: No cucumber-specific effect or postural-instability estimate is reported; the trial only reports the total motor scale and allows courgette substitution.

fit: PD mixed ovo-lacto vegetarian diet with cucumber among menu ingredients; some participants also received enemas
assessment: Raw preparation, individual cucumber intake and postural-instability item are not established; no cucumber-specific effect can be isolated.

fit: Aqueous cucumber fruit extract in lead-exposed rats; motor tests unnamed in accessible abstract
assessment: Non-Parkinson animal toxicity model and aqueous extract differ from raw cucumber consumption and human postural instability; original full methods unavailable.

fit: Millet porridge in both groups of a labor analgesia study; pain measurement but no millet comparison
assessment: Pain differences compare epidural selection, not millet intake; species and preparation details are unspecified and population does not have Parkinson disease.

fit: Millet flour bread contaminated by monocrotophos; acute abdominal pain in an outbreak
assessment: Pain is associated with measured pesticide contamination rather than ordinary boiled millet; no Parkinson sample or clean control.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: S7.519 discusses physical treatment of millet crops and root development. No ingestion or symptom outcome was tested.

fit: veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison
assessment: The Pennisetum entry identifies pearl millet and a reported association with agalactia in sows. Other millet names identify different grasses. There is no culinary or Parkinson motor comparison.

fit: dissolved powdered ginger and resting pressure in older women
assessment: Hypertensive water and ginger groups showed comparable resting systolic changes of −2.70 and −3.28 mmHg. No standing challenge, Parkinson cohort or fresh-grated ginger.

fit: Ginger rhizome extract given to healthy volunteers with acute cuff blood pressure measurements
assessment: Systolic pressure declined from the higher-dose arm baseline at two hours. The recorded posture, controlled contrast and standing lightheadedness are unverified; the extract differs from culinary grated ginger.

fit: Fine-chopped ginger as an assigned food in 22 healthy men; postprandial cuff pressure
assessment: The primary paper reports no matched ginger-versus-control difference for the named standing symptom. Postprandial cuff measurements, fine chopping and non-Parkinson participants limit fit.

fit: Parkinson randomized mixed diets both include minced ginger and record lightheadedness safety events
assessment: Individual ingestion and grating were not established. Safety event counts do not identify on-standing severity or attribute the events to ginger.

fit: Single-arm ginger extract capsule study with ambulatory pressure averages in type 2 diabetes
assessment: Reported declines are pre-post ambulatory averages; no standing challenge, symptom-specific severity, matched dietary preparation or Parkinson population.

fit: human Parkinson grapefruit juice with cabergoline pharmacokinetics
assessment: Five people receiving cabergoline had about 1.7 times the plasma concentration with grapefruit juice coadministration. The abstract gives no raw whole-fruit comparison, stride result or observed motor change.

fit: grapefruit-derived vesicles applied at the tendon and objectively measured mouse stride
assessment: The authors report stride nearer to healthy mice after a local grapefruit-vesicle microneedle treatment for tendon injury. This is neither a Parkinson model nor raw grapefruit ingestion.

fit: grapefruit essential oil aroma in a mixed population
assessment: The planned measures do not isolate a raw grapefruit effect on stride length. The registry gives no results.

fit: oregano extract and in vitro monoamine oxidase activity
assessment: The patent reports MAO-A and MAO-B inhibition by extract in an enzyme assay. No daily OFF hours, food preparation contrast or human regimen was studied.

fit: oregano on a shared Parkinson diet and levodopa-equivalent dose
assessment: The diet includes oregano among many seasonings. The reported daily medication dose changes are distinct from daily OFF time, and Table 4 values differ from the narrative.

fit: separate Origanum species tea and Parkinson motor examination
assessment: The Parkinson pilot measured UPDRS III and reports a within-arm p of .069. Filtered dried marjoram tea differs from eating fresh oregano and the paper gives no daily OFF duration.

fit: sumac extract in Parkinson-derived fibroblasts
assessment: The study measured cellular responses and did not measure muscle rigidity after sumac ingestion.

fit: soybean oil changed in oral feed with stepping and locomotion measures
assessment: Soybean oil went from 30 to 0 g/kg as other feed components changed. Stepping and open-field results did not clearly differ by diet. Oil grade and an independent human bradykinesia effect remain unknown.

fit: soybean oil in mixed oral diets with timed motor measures
assessment: Soybean oil was 10 g/kg in control feed and absent in the alternate formulas. There is no separable oil effect and timed pole performance is a mouse motor proxy.

fit: soybean oil comparator with slower rat motor behavior after interesterified fat
assessment: The interesterified-fat offspring group showed lower adult locomotion. This developmental rat comparison gives no independently measured refined soybean oil or clinical bradykinesia effect.

fit: soybean comparator in a mouse pole test
assessment: The rotenone soybean group took 7.83 seconds versus 4.73 in unlesioned mice on the same soybean diet. Middle and high perilla outperformed rotenone soybean, with no isolated refined oil or clinical bradykinesia estimate.

fit: soybean oil in an enteral formula and concurrent levodopa treatment
assessment: The combined tube formula contains soybean oil of unspecified grade. No isolated bradykinesia measure or soybean oil exposure comparison.

fit: PD Sargol powder tablet; planned Part II; no drooling-item outcome accessible
assessment: Part II includes saliva and drooling item 2.2; its planned assessment and total scores cannot establish an effect on drooling severity.

fit: egg-yolk oil as adjunct in hemiplegia dysarthria
assessment: The deposited abstract reports a larger change in a broad Robertson measure with an egg-yolk-derived product. Original route, individual speech measures and full methods are open. The comparison uses hemiplegia and an oil intervention.

fit: eggs in a Parkinson diet intervention and composite motor score
assessment: The intervention menu lists eggs and the motor scale includes speech. The study gives no egg preparation, actual exposure, or outcome specific to speech intelligibility.

fit: whole walnuts and mouse rotarod latency to fall
assessment: 6% walnut diet did not clearly affect rotarod latency (p=.9999). Walnut plus housing enrichment improved performance, with no enrichment-only arm. Whole nuts, experimental latency and aged mice.

fit: whole walnut diets and latency to fall on rod or plank
assessment: Aged rats had task-dependent longer latency at 2% or 6% and shorter latency on the large plank at 9%. Several tasks were null. Whole nuts and challenge latency differ from oral oil and everyday falls.

fit: whole walnuts with matched training and postural sway
assessment: Selected mediolateral dual-task interactions favored walnuts plus training. Anteroposterior significance differs between Table 4 and prose. Healthy older men, whole nuts and no clinical fall counts.

fit: registered freeze-dried table grape and Hamilton anxiety comparison
assessment: The official record lists active and no longer recruiting for the four-week randomized trial in college students. It includes the Hamilton scale and has no posted results.

fit: whole freeze-dried table grape powder and anxiety in postmenopausal women
assessment: Forty randomized and 32 completed. The 2020 abstract reports no clear anxiety result after 12 weeks and gives no anxiety score, group contrast or uncertainty.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: S2.146 and S9.719 study isolated resveratrol in pea mitochondria or rat nerve recovery. S9.660 identifies grapes as one source. Grape snail is unrelated terminology.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: P-07-009 and P-14-003 work with grape pomace or plant extracts. P-18-008 studies isolated resveratrol in old rat skeletal muscle. No dietary grape comparison measures Parkinson anxiety or rigidity.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: P384 tests grape seed extract in colorectal cells and P593 studies isolated resveratrol in oral-tissue reconstruction. Neither provides a dietary grape comparison.

fit: isolated resveratrol and adipose thermogenic markers
assessment: Rat tissue markers followed treatment with extracted compound and different energy-restriction arms. The compound is not the raw grape exposure; anxiety was not measured.

fit: grape juice and immediate calm outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The healthy crossover found higher calm ratings with purple grape juice. Order influenced the outcome, and the study tested juice rather than raw grape.

fit: grape extract and anxiety outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The trial found lower anxiety scores with grape extract in healthy older adults. Baseline anxiety was low and no Parkinson cohort was studied.

fit: grape polyphenol concentrate and measured open-field center time in a Parkinson mouse model
assessment: A53T mouse center time was 30.6 ± 6.6 seconds with concentrate and 36.0 ± 9.8 seconds with water (means ± SEM). Table 1 found no clear diet or diet-by-genotype effect. The concentrate and open-field proxy differ from raw grapes and clinical anxiety.

fit: oral dried whole Vitis vinifera and anxiety-like behavior in a Parkinson rat model
assessment: Black Corinthian currants reduced day-38 open-field thigmotaxis in rotenone rats (P=.006; interaction P=.025). Elevated-plus-maze anxiety index showed no clear diet effect (P=.929; interaction P=.610). The exposure was dried fruit and these are animal behavioral proxies.

fit: juice plus exercise
assessment: The two papers describe one registered study. Juice supplied no clear added functional or cognitive benefit.

fit: clinical case or dietary history without a matched ingredient comparison
assessment: A restricted diet history includes a grape or olive. Grape-like morphology occurs elsewhere. The case supplies no grape-controlled comparative effect.

fit: enriched rice bran oil and rat motor coordination
assessment: Ladder and hanging measures improved, without a hand dexterity test or plain oil arm.

fit: extracted rice bran oil and rotarod coordination
assessment: The oil group showed less haloperidol-induced rotarod impairment, with grade, individual digit dexterity and clinical Parkinson outcomes unverified.

study: BNA2019 injected oil or preference member
fit: animal vehicle or flavored-milk preference outside the frozen preparation

fit: shared collection original source context

fit: shared collection original source context

fit: oral corn oil comparator and apathy item in Alzheimer disease
assessment: Among item-positive patients, average apathy was higher after six months in the corn group. The comparative estimate was inconclusive and enrollment was for Alzheimer disease.

fit: shared oral Parkinson trial corn vehicle and part I aggregate
assessment: The treatment table gives no motivation item change or independent contrast for oil.

fit: Oral exposure to dill in cooked food and observed oropharyngeal allergy

fit: Authentic dried dill leaf capsules with gastrointestinal symptom tracking
assessment: Esophageal symptoms were captured in a type 2 diabetes trial. Drooling and salivary flow were not separate endpoints.

fit: Green beans among optional foods in a multifood Parkinson diet and lactulose pilot; actual individual intake and cooking unspecified

fit: Leaf extract and drug-induced involuntary rat oral movements
assessment: The tested leaf extract and alkaloid fraction addressed involuntary oral movements following prolonged neuroleptic exposure. The study gives no scored facial expressiveness or cooked leaf intervention.

fit: Hoarseness observed after contaminated rice bran oil exposure

fit: Rice oil odor comparison with wet-hoarse voice in a swallow rubric
assessment: The modified water swallowing test includes cough or wet-hoarse voice in one grade. The study did not grade voice loudness or change after ingesting oil.

fit: Oral rice bran oil placebo and Parkinson motor examination
assessment: The primary clinical study provides no vocal intensity or component speech scores, no oil refinement specification, and no oil-free arm.

fit: Millet listed among foods in a multi-ingredient Parkinson diet; no separate dyskinesia result
assessment: Preparation, individual millet intake and millet-specific comparator are unspecified; the reported motor total cannot estimate dyskinesia severity.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: S7.519 discusses physical treatment of millet crops and root development. No ingestion or symptom outcome was tested.

fit: veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison
assessment: The Pennisetum entry identifies pearl millet and a reported association with agalactia in sows. Other millet names identify different grasses. There is no culinary or Parkinson motor comparison.

fit: ginger odor threshold measured in Parkinson participants
assessment: Table 5 gives recognition-pressure thresholds at three stimulus concentrations. The protocol did not compare olfactory severity after eating grated ginger.

fit: ginger in four-aroma sensory training
assessment: 24 weeks vs conventional odors gave no clear TDI contrast. The regimen combined exposures and did not test ingestion.

fit: dried ginger in six-aroma inhalation regimen
assessment: Identification change favored training versus mometasone among completers. Nonrandomization, unbalanced attrition and the multi-aroma exposure leave ginger oral effects untested.

fit: herb named in a mixed Parkinson menu
assessment: The menu and composite motor outcome cannot quantify freezing episodes after dried lovage leaf.

fit: source-context follow-through with preparation or outcome limits
assessment: S1.97 proposes parsley as a possible dietary source of related Rubisco peptides while modelling spinach-derived rubiscolin. No parsley isolate, dose or Parkinson outcome is measured.

fit: veterinary reference context only, without a tested Parkinson comparison
assessment: The Petroselinum crispum entry describes furanocoumarins and primary photosensitization. The broader common-name cross-reference includes other genera. No frozen culinary or Parkinson symptom result appears.

fit: Parkinson dietary menu with parsley and reported medication use
assessment: The source lists parsley among many ingredients. Neither the herb's form nor an item-level dyskinesia or time-with-dyskinesia estimate is available.

fit: Verified oral dried powdered leaf preparation in people
assessment: Metabolite absorption was measured in healthy men. The trial gives no levodopa-induced dyskinesia observation and the formulation included yogurt.

fit: A parsley-associated isolated flavone in a Parkinson-like motor model
assessment: Coordination, gait and molecular endpoints in an animal model do not measure levodopa-induced abnormal involuntary movements or a dried herb effect.

fit: oral tarragon supplement and systolic blood pressure

fit: oral extra-virgin avocado oil and rat recognition and spatial memory
